+
+============================================================================
+  OPEN, PROMINENT:  A SESSION ON DOCUMENT CONSISTENCY IS DUE.
+  See 'adm/DISCUSSIONS/disc-1-document-consistency.txt'. Until it is held,
+  a README sentence may lag its ruling and a component's laws may stand in
+  another component's RATIONALE -- read the RATIONALE index lines first.
+============================================================================
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+RE-RECORDING A GOOD: THE VERDICT MUST NOT MOVE
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+A GOOD is re-recorded when a change is DESIGNED -- a name, a phrase, a
+column. It is not re-recorded because the suite went red.
+
+THE TWO ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE BY EYE, and a redirect makes both green:
+
+    python3 test-x.py choice > GOOD/test-x.py--choice.txt
+
+That command records whatever came out, a FAILURE or a TRACEBACK
+included, and the next run agrees with it perfectly.
+
+SO CHECK THE VERDICT, ALWAYS, before and after:
+
+    grep -c '^FAILURE\|^  FAIL' <old>   ==   same in <new>
+
+A count that MOVED is not a designed change: it is the suite telling
+you something and being silenced. Read the diff.
+
+This is written down because it happened three times in one session:
+twice caught, once not -- 'test-coverage_provision.py--harvested' was
+blessed FAILING and stayed green for hours, because the failure was
+its own oracle.
+
+A VERDICT COUNT IS NOT ENOUGH FOR A DISPLAY-ONLY SUITE
+------------------------------------------------------
+Some suites carry no 'FAIL'/'SUCCESS' line at all: they SHOW what
+happened and the GOOD is the whole of the judgement ('test-remove.sh',
+'test-wishlist.sh', 'test-report.sh'). There the verdict check has
+nothing to count, and a change can turn the test into a SILENT NO-OP
+that still prints, still matches its fresh GOOD, and asserts nothing.
+
+That happened here: the record key became the file WHOLE, the fixture
+kept asking 'hwut.remove' for the STEM, the face looked under a key
+that does not exist, found nothing, and said so politely --
+
+    TO BE FORGOTTEN: test-app -- 0 file(s)
+        book entry: none stood
+    AFTER { ... book: ['test-app.sh'] }        <- unchanged
+
+-- and that was recorded as the oracle. Nothing failed. Nothing was
+tested either.
+
+SO COUNT THE PHRASES THAT MEAN 'I FOUND NOTHING', before and after:
+
+    none stood | not registered | no recorded artefact | <no entry>
+    <none> | never run | GOOD missing | nothing to accept | is EMPTY
+
+A count that ROSE is the suite going quiet, not the suite agreeing.
+
+THE IMPORT GRAPH, AND THE LAYERING
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+'adm/import_graph.py' reads every module with 'ast' and reports who
+depends on whom at a stated DEPTH -- 1 the outer directories, 2 the
+inner ones, 0 the modules themselves.
+
+    adm/import_graph.py . --depth=1 --exclude="*/TEST/*" \
+        --exclude="*/test-*" --exclude="*/config.py"
+
+AN IMPORT IS A FACT IN THE TEXT, and nothing here guesses. That is why
+this tool is static while a CALL graph could not be: duck typing and
+dynamic dispatch mean a static call graph INVENTS edges, and an
+invented edge in an architecture document is worse than no document.
+Real calls are observed, never derived.
+
+THE SUITES ARE EXCLUDED. A test application imports whatever it tests,
+upward and downward alike, and is no part of the shape it examines.
+
+FORMATS: 'tree' (nested blocks and arrows, for reading), 'edges' (one
+per line, for grep and for diff -- the form a GOOD file wants), 'dot'
+(graphviz), 'mermaid' (a browser, with nothing installed).
+
+'--check' MAKES THE ARCHITECTURE EXECUTABLE. 'adm/LAYERING.txt'
+declares the permitted DIRECTION between components; an edge no rule
+permits is a violation naming both ends, and the tool answers 1.
+
+    adm/import_graph.py . --depth=2 --check=adm/LAYERING.txt \
+        --exclude="*/TEST/*" --exclude="*/test-*" \
+        --exclude="*/config.py"
+
+The suite is 'adm/TEST/test-import_graph.sh'. Its 'layering' choice
+shows the check PASSING and BITING, because a check that never fails
+proves nothing; its 'vut' choice records the real tree's outer picture
+and its layering, so a change to either shows up as a moved GOOD.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+
+STATIC ANALYSIS -- THE RATCHET
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+'adm/TEST/test-static-analysis.sh' runs 'ruff' over the tree with the
+tree's own configuration and records, SORTED, every kind of finding
+that still stands.
+
+TWO SUITES IN THIS TREE ASK ABOUT THE CODE BASE'S SHAPE RATHER THAN
+ITS BEHAVIOUR -- this one and 'test-import_graph.sh'. Every other
+suite RUNS the product and reads what came out; these two read the
+SOURCE and never run it. That is what 'static analysis' names, and it
+is why they live in 'adm' rather than beside the component they
+examine: their subject is the tree.
+
+NOT 'COMPLIANCE': that word names conformance to an EXTERNAL standard
+-- a MISRA clause, a PEP, an ISO paragraph. There is none here. The
+tree declares its own tolerance in 'adm/ruff.toml' and the GOOD
+records what remains, so the authority is entirely inward and the
+word would point the wrong way.
+
+AND NOT 'HYGIENE', WHICH IS ALREADY TAKEN and means something
+narrower: A COMPONENT'S OWN SOURCE AND GOOD FILES, checked against the
+defects that recurred while that component was built --
+'engine/operations/TEST/test-hygiene.py' is the instance, and disc-6
+expects more. A hygiene suite belongs TO ITS COMPONENT and knows what
+that component keeps getting wrong. This suite belongs to no component
+and knows nothing but what a tool reports about every file alike.
+Terminological invariance: one word, one thing.
+
+IT IS NOT A TEST THAT THE TREE IS CLEAN. It is a test that the tree is
+NO LESS CLEAN THAN IT WAS. One more instance of a tolerated kind, or a
+kind not tolerated before, moves the GOOD and the suite says so. A
+finding REMOVED moves it too, and that re-blessing is the record of an
+improvement.
+
+WHAT IS IGNORED IS IGNORED BY NAME, in 'adm/ruff.toml', each with its
+reason: '%' formatting, hand-aligned imports and asserts-as-door-guards
+are house style, not findings, and 878 of one kind drown every finding
+that matters.
+
+THE 'MUST STAND AT ZERO' SET is four rules, each of which can HIDE A
+FAILURE rather than merely offend:
+
+    F      a name that is not there
+    B011   a dispatch that vanishes under 'python -O' and then hands
+           None to a caller who blames their own code
+    B020   a loop variable rebinding what the loop reads from
+    S110   a swallow with no reason given
+
+'S102' (exec) is deliberately NOT among them: the pype language
+executes its own effect blocks, so exec is the feature. A set that can
+never be empty is a set people learn to ignore.
+
+THE RUFF VERSION IS PRINTED, AND IT IS A HAPPY PATTERN
+
+    eq-pattern = ["ruff [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+"]
+
+so two runs under different ruffs are EQUIVALENT on that line. THIS IS
+WHAT HAPPY PATTERNS ARE FOR: the version is not the fact this suite is
+about -- the findings are. A ruff that knows new rules moves the list,
+and there the suite speaks; a ruff that merely counts higher and finds
+the same things has said nothing, and the suite says nothing back.
+
+Without the pattern the test would go red on every upgrade for a
+reason nobody could act on, and A SUITE THAT CRIES AT NOISE IS A SUITE
+THAT GETS RE-BLESSED UNREAD.
+
+NO RUFF, NO REPORT. A missing tool is a MISSING PRECONDITION, and a
+missing precondition is a RESULT stated as one -- never a silent pass
+that would let hygiene rot unwatched.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+
+CONTRACT MATERIAL -- '--shared'
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+    adm/import_graph.py . --depth=3 --shared=3 \
+        --exclude="*/TEST/*" --exclude="*/test-*" --exclude="*/config.py"
+
+names every NAME that three or more components import, and where it
+lives today.
+
+A NAME THAT THREE COMPONENTS REACH FOR IS NO PART OF WHICHEVER ONE
+HAPPENS TO HOLD IT. Where it lives inside one of its own readers it
+HOLDS A CYCLE SHUT -- and the report says which name, so the question
+stops being 'is there a cycle' and becomes 'what would moving ONE name
+do'.
+
+THE TEST FOR CONTRACT MATERIAL: would moving it move BEHAVIOUR? An
+enum has none and is the clearest case there is. A class with twenty
+methods is not contract however many components import it -- it is
+shared because a REAL dependency exists, and the layering must express
+that rather than hide it.
+
+    adm/import_graph.py . --depth=2 --format=svg > architecture.svg
+
+draws the picture HERE -- no graphviz, no browser, no dependency.
+Components in rows, importers above what they import, and A MUTUAL
+PAIR IN AMBER WITH A HEAD AT BOTH ENDS, so a cycle shows itself.
+
+AND IT IS EDITABLE. Every box is a GROUP with an id, holding the
+rectangle and both labels; every arrow is an INKSCAPE CONNECTOR bound
+to two of those ids, and every box carries 'connector-avoid'. Open the
+file, take the Selector ('S'), drag a box: THE LINES FOLLOW, routing
+around the boxes rather than through them.
+
+    the connector tool   'O' (or Ctrl+F2) -- click one box, click
+                         another, to draw a NEW arrow
+    the XML editor       Ctrl+Shift+X -- shows
+                         'inkscape:connection-start/-end'
+    a deleted box        leaves its connectors dangling; they are not
+                         removed with it
+
+THE 'd' ATTRIBUTE IS WRITTEN ANYWAY, because a browser knows nothing
+of connectors and must still see a line. Inkscape recomputes it the
+moment anything moves, so ONE FILE serves both.
+'engine/compare/contract' is the first fruit of both
+(engine/compare/RATIONALE.txt, C-1).
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+SEALED COMPONENTS
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+'adm/LAYERING.txt' has two line shapes, because there are two kinds of
+law.
+
+    <from> -> <to>      a permitted DIRECTION between two components,
+                        judged at the '--depth' asked for
+    SEALED <glob>       a component that IMPORTS NOTHING of this tree,
+                        judged at MODULE depth and therefore true at
+                        EVERY '--depth'
+
+A DIRECTION IS ABOUT A PAIR and can only be read where both are named:
+at depth 2 the whole of 'engine/compare' is one box, and a rule about
+what happens inside it cannot be tested. A SEAL IS ABOUT ONE
+COMPONENT, and 'nothing leaves here' is the whole of a contract's
+claim -- so it holds however coarsely the rest is declared.
+
+SEALED TODAY: 'engine/compare/contract', 'engine/procsitter',
+'auxiliary', 'test_writing_support'.
+
+THREE OF THE FOUR NEEDED NO MOVING, ONLY DECLARING. They already
+imported nothing of this tree; the seal is that sentence made
+checkable, so what is true today cannot quietly stop being true.
+
+WHAT A SEAL DOES NOT FORBID: a sealed component's own modules may
+speak among themselves. The pair that results is INSIDE the seal,
+where nothing outside can be made to wait on it.
+______________________________________________________________________________

+disc-1  A SESSION ON DOCUMENT CONSISTENCY IS DUE                  ** OPEN **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+WHY       The tree's documents have drifted from the tree, and from each
+          other, in ways a reader cannot see from any one of them:
+
+          - THE RULINGS THAT SHAPE A COMPONENT STAND IN ANOTHER'S
+            RATIONALE. The book's membership law (E-20, E-22, E-34,
+            E-36) is in 'services/RATIONALE.txt'; the bookkeeper's own
+            RATIONALE begins at B-1 and never mentions them. The
+            provision inversion (disc-2) is in 'engine/operations';
+            the door doctrine (E-37, E-38) is in services. A reader of
+            a component cannot find its laws from its own directory.
+          - README SENTENCES OUTLIVE THEIR RULINGS. 'bookkeeper/
+            README.txt' said the book held "the reproducible
+            configurations" the day after B-6 removed them; 'run/
+            RATIONALE.txt' ruled 'specification.py' keeps its name,
+            and the live module was 'configuration_tree.py' with the
+            named one a dead twin.
+          - TWO NAMES, ONE THING: 'feed'/'port'; 'labels' under two
+            paths; 'numeric'/'tolerance.numeric_ratio'; 'first_accept'/
+            'last_accept'; 'FAILURES'/'HINTS'. Each was swept in code;
+            not every sweep reached every document.
+          - RATIONALE IS APPEND-ONLY BY LAW, so a superseded entry
+            still reads as current unless annotated, and annotation
+            has been uneven (E-36 has one; E-31 and E-20 do not).
+
+WHAT      One session, nothing else on the table:
+          1. Every component's RATIONALE gains an INDEX of the rulings
+             that shape it, wherever they stand.
+          2. Every superseded entry carries a one-line note naming
+             its successor.
+          3. Every README is read against its component as it IS
+             (Defence Test, 'Guideline-for-README-Reviews.txt').
+          4. A terminology table: one noun per concept, and the
+             graveyard of old nouns, so a sweep has a checklist.
+          5. The three-bin rule re-checked per component: README
+             mechanics only, RATIONALE decisions, DISCUSSIONS forks.
+
+MARKED    2026-09-01, on Frank-Rene's instruction, while amending B-6
+          to B-7 -- the second amendment to the book's shape in two
+          days, each of which found a document saying otherwise.

+#  LAYERING -- the permitted DIRECTION between components.
+#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#  Read by 'adm/import_graph.py --check'. A rule reads
+#
+#      <from-glob> -> <to-glob>
+#
+#  and states that such an edge MAY exist. An edge no rule permits is
+#  a VIOLATION, named by both ends. The declaration says what may
+#  happen; everything else is drift.
+#
+#  '#' to end of line is a comment; blank lines are nothing.
+#
+#  THE CENTRAL LAW: DATA FLOWS INTO THE ENGINE, AND THE ENGINE IMPORTS
+#  NOTHING BACK. A face builds and hands down; the engine consumes.
+#  There is no rule 'engine/* -> services*' below, and its absence is
+#  the law -- one such edge and the check goes red.
+#
+#  This declaration describes the tree at depth 2. Run:
+#
+#      adm/import_graph.py . --depth=2 --check=adm/LAYERING.txt \
+#          --exclude="*/TEST/*" --exclude="*/test-*" \
+#          --exclude="*/config.py"
+#
+#  THE SUITES ARE EXCLUDED, and deliberately: a test application
+#  imports whatever it tests, upward and downward alike, and it is not
+#  part of the shape it examines.
+#  ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+#  THE FOUNDATION. These import nothing of this tree, and the check
+#  needs no rule to say so -- a component with no outgoing edge cannot
+#  violate a direction.
+
+#  A CONTRACT IMPORTS NOTHING. 'engine/compare/contract' holds the
+#  vocabulary in which the parties of a comparison name the same
+#  things -- enums, the analogy shapes, the semantics that give them
+#  meaning. It has NO outgoing edge, and that is the property which
+#  makes it a contract: every party sits above it, so no party can be
+#  made to wait on another.
+#
+#  ENFORCED BY 'SEALED', which is judged at MODULE depth and so holds
+#  at every '--depth' this file is read with -- including depth 2,
+#  where the whole of 'engine/compare' is one component and everything
+#  inside it would otherwise be invisible.
+#
+#  A DIRECTION is about a PAIR and can only be read where both are
+#  named. A SEAL is about ONE COMPONENT, and 'nothing leaves here' is
+#  the whole of a contract's claim.
+
+SEALED engine/compare/contract
+
+#  THE DOOR OF 'compare'. The largest component of the tree, and the
+#  one whose insides move most; what the rest of the tree needs of it
+#  is five names ('Configuration', 'is_equivalent', 'associate',
+#  'RegionSyntaxError', 'feeder_ui'). They stand in one module, and a
+#  caller reaching past it is drift the check catches.
+DOOR engine/compare/api
+SEALED engine/protocol
+
+#  'procsitter' IS ALREADY A CONTRACT IN FACT: it imports nothing of
+#  this tree, and 'operations' and 'orchestrator' both read
+#  'Procsitter', 'ProcsitterConfig' and 'E_Containment' from it. It
+#  needed no moving -- only DECLARING, so that what is true today
+#  cannot quietly stop being true.
+#
+#  MEASURED, not assumed: 'adm/import_graph.py --shared' names those
+#  three among the cross-component vocabulary, and the seal check
+#  confirms nothing leaves.
+SEALED engine/procsitter
+
+#  AND ITS DOOR. A sealed component with a door is the strongest shape
+#  the check can state: nothing leaves, and nothing enters but here.
+DOOR engine/procsitter/api
+
+#  COVERAGE. Its surface was made deliberate by D-26 -- the table left
+#  the code -- and this states where it now is.
+DOOR engine/coverage/api
+
+#  THE BOOKKEEPER, which owns TWO databases -- the book of decisions
+#  and this machine's observations -- and was reached at seven modules
+#  before this line.
+DOOR engine/bookkeeper/api
+
+#  THE FOUNDATION IS SEALED FOR THE SAME REASON. 'auxiliary' and
+#  'test_writing_support' import nothing of this tree, which is what makes
+#  them a foundation; the seal is that sentence, made checkable.
+SEALED auxiliary
+SEALED test_writing_support
+
+#  THE ENGINE rests on the foundation, and its parts rest on one
+#  another in one direction.
+engine/*            -> adm
+engine/*            -> auxiliary
+engine/*            -> test_writing_support*
+
+engine/bookkeeper   -> engine/compare
+engine/coverage     -> engine/bookkeeper
+engine/operations   -> engine/bookkeeper
+engine/operations   -> engine/compare
+engine/operations   -> engine/coverage
+engine/operations   -> engine/procsitter
+engine/orchestrator -> engine/bookkeeper
+engine/orchestrator -> engine/compare
+engine/orchestrator -> engine/coverage
+engine/orchestrator -> engine/operations
+engine/orchestrator -> engine/procsitter
+
+#  THE RUN REPORT PROTOCOL. 'engine/protocol' holds what a producer
+#  of the run's event stream and a consumer of it AGREE ON -- the
+#  vocabulary, the receiver a consumer derives from, the fold that
+#  answers what a run came to.
+#
+#  IT REPLACED THE ONE SIDEWAYS ARROW IN THIS TREE.
+#  'engine/display -> engine/orchestrator' stood here until the
+#  protocol moved out of the producer: a consumer reaching into a
+#  producer for the shape they share. Now display points DOWN, as
+#  every other component does, and a TUI or a customer's own consumer
+#  needs three leaf modules rather than the orchestrator.
+engine/display      -> engine/protocol
+engine/orchestrator -> engine/protocol
+
+#  THE FACES rest on everything, and nothing rests on them.
+services*           -> adm
+services*           -> auxiliary
+services*           -> engine/*
+services*           -> test_writing_support*
+
+#  A FACE FAMILY AND ITS PARENT. 'services -> services/lib' is a face
+#  reaching for a family's door ('lib/labels', 'lib/viewers');
+#  'services/lib -> services'
+#  is that door reaching back for what every face shares ('_core',
+#  '_exit').
+#
+#  THIS IS A CYCLE AT DEPTH 2, and it is admitted here rather than
+#  hidden. VERIFIED at module depth: no import runs in a circle
+#  between these two -- the shared members ('_core', '_exit') are
+#  leaves and the door is a leaf. It is a thing to WATCH, not a thing
+#  that is well.
+#
+#  THE MODULE GRAPH AS A WHOLE IS NOT ACYCLIC: ten cycles stand, all
+#  INSIDE single components --
+#
+#      4  engine/compare/region
+#      2  engine/operations/run
+#      1  each: engine/compare/engine, engine/compare/reading,
+#               engine/operations/interaction,
+#               engine/orchestrator/exploration
+#
+#  A cycle inside a component is not a layering violation, and this
+#  declaration does not forbid one. Whether each is a design or an
+#  accretion is a question for the review, not for this file.
+services            -> services/lib
+services/lib        -> services
diff --git a/adm/PHILOSOPHY.txt b/adm/PHILOSOPHY.txt

+++ b/adm/PHILOSOPHY.txt
@@ -0,0 +1,371 @@
+                            HWUT -- PHILOSOPHY
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+                    H W  U  T
+                         |  '---- tolerance      compare
+                         '------- understanding  pype
+
+    BEHAVIOUR            the object of judgement; never available directly
+        |
+        |  expression, measurement, perception
+        |  THE CHANNEL -- adds order scramble, interleaving, timing,
+        v                addresses, paths, numeric noise
+    PERCEPTION           two of them: the subject, and the frozen nominal
+        |
+        |  FREEING -- understanding first, tolerance only after
+        v
+    JUDGEMENT            green if and only if the behaviour was admissible
+                         -- and 1.1 says exactly when a test can deliver
+                            that 'if and only if'
+
+
+1  THE OBJECT
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+Behaviour is what is judged. A green light is owed exactly when the
+behaviour was admissible -- both directions of the "if and only if" carry
+weight, and section 7 shows that they fail differently.
+
+The behaviour belongs to a UNIT: a causal system with a causal contract and
+a consistency contract. A TEST is one complete arc of that unit --
+compilation, run, termination -- observed from outside the process. A CHOICE
+is one scenario of that arc.
+
+
+1.1  WHEN A TEST IS WORTH HAVING
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+Write D for the transformation from BEHAVIOUR to DESCRIPTION -- what the
+unit does, turned into the text a test reads. Write Eq(x, y, T) for the
+comparison of two descriptions under a stated tolerance T. Let GOOD be
+the admissible behaviours and BAD the inadmissible ones, and let
+
+    GOOD  intersect  BAD  =  {}
+
+THE CRITERION. A test, and the description it rests on, is worth having
+IF AND ONLY IF
+
+    for all b0, b1 in GOOD :        Eq(D(b0), D(b1), T)  =  true
+    for all b0 in GOOD, b in BAD :  Eq(D(b0), D(b),  T)  =  false
+
+That is: Eq o D collapses ALL of GOOD into ONE class, and NO member of
+BAD falls into it.
+
+                      D                      Eq(-, -, T)
+    BEHAVIOUR  ------------->  DESCRIPTION  ------------->  one class
+
+         .--------.                     .--------------.
+         |  GOOD  | ------------------> |  ONE class   |   every good
+         '--------'                     '--------------'   behaviour,
+                                                           indistinguishable
+         .--------.                     .--------------.
+         |  BAD   | ------------------> | anywhere ELSE|   no bad behaviour,
+         '--------'                     '--------------'   ever inside
+
+TWO WAYS TO FAIL, and they are the only two:
+
+    a GOOD pair that DIFFERS      the description or the tolerance
+    (first line broken)           discriminates too finely. FALSE RED --
+                                  loud, annoying, and self-reporting.
+
+    a BAD one that MATCHES        the description or the tolerance is
+    (second line broken)          too coarse. FALSE GREEN -- silent, and
+                                  it cannot report itself.
+
+D AND T ARE THE ONLY KNOBS, and section 5 names them: UNDERSTANDING
+shapes D, TOLERANCE shapes T. So "understand what you can, tolerate only
+what you cannot" is not taste -- it is the instruction for satisfying two
+inequalities at once, using the transform that composes before reaching
+for the relation that does not.
+
+ACCEPTANCE IS NOT A FREE CHOICE. It is tempting to say the nominal's
+identity does not matter -- if every good description matches every other,
+any b0 in GOOD would serve. That is true and it is the wrong lesson,
+because it demands the strictest possible form of the criterion and gives
+nothing back.
+
+TO ACCEPT IS TO DECLARE THE POLE OF GOODNESS: not any member of GOOD, but
+the one all the others are arranged around. And the word already said so
+-- a NOMINAL value, in engineering, is the designated centre with the
+tolerance band around it. It was never 'whatever run we happened to
+freeze'.
+
+The gain is measurable. Around an ARBITRARY member, the band must span
+the whole spread; around the POLE it need only reach the furthest member:
+
+    arbitrary b0     T  >=  diameter( D(GOOD) )
+    the POLE         T  >=  radius( D(GOOD) )        and radius <= diameter
+                                                     <= 2 x radius
+
+So the pole roughly HALVES the tolerance the criterion needs -- and every
+unit of tolerance not spent is margin left over against BAD. The margin
+condition becomes
+
+    radius( D(GOOD) )  <=  T  <  distance( pole, D(BAD) )
+
+which is a strictly easier thing to satisfy than the same statement about
+an arbitrary representative.
+
+    .......... D(GOOD) ..........
+    o     o    o   X   o    o   o          X = the pole
+          |<---- radius --->|              a band reaching the furthest
+    |<-------- diameter -------->|         member, not spanning the spread
+
+WHERE THE POLE IS NOT KNOWN, and usually it is not, acceptance is a
+HYPOTHESIS: that this run stands at the centre. The hypothesis is
+falsifiable, and a disagreement between two good runs is exactly what
+falsifies it. So a test that starts failing on a second machine has not
+found a bug in the code -- it has found that the accepted description was
+not the pole, and the answer is to move the nominal toward the centre or
+to widen D until the spread vanishes.
+
+ACCEPTING A RUN NEAR THE EDGE IS A MISTAKE EVEN THOUGH THE RUN IS GOOD.
+That is the practical content of all of this, and it is invisible without
+it.
+
+THE VERDICT MUST NOT DEPEND ON WHICH GOOD BEHAVIOUR WAS ACCEPTED. Written
+out, that is a constraint on Eq itself:
+
+    Eq(D(b0), D(b), T)  is not a function of  b0
+
+The criterion already implies it -- if every good description matches
+every other and none matches a bad one, then any b0 in GOOD decides
+identically. So the danger is not that the rule is missing; it is that
+NOTHING CHECKS IT, and a tolerance can break it quietly.
+
+THE NUMERIC CASE, which is where it bites first. Accept 0.815 under a
+RELATIVE tolerance and the band is centred on 0.815; accept 0.816 and it
+is centred there instead. A value near the edge is then admissible or not
+DEPENDING ON WHICH RUN HAPPENED TO BE ACCEPTED:
+
+    accepted 0.815 |-----------o-----------|
+    accepted 0.816     |-----------o-----------|
+                                           ^
+                                     inside one band,
+                                     outside the other
+
+Two demands follow.
+
+  Eq MUST BE SYMMETRIC. 'within r of the NOMINAL' is not: it makes the
+  nominal an anchor, and the criterion is not even well posed. A relative
+  tolerance must be relative to something symmetric -- the larger
+  magnitude, or the mean -- or be absolute.
+
+  THE MARGIN CONDITION. Let d be the distance Eq thresholds, so that
+  Eq(x, y, T) holds exactly when d(x, y) <= T. Since every comparison is
+  against the POLE and never between two arbitrary members, the two lines
+  of the criterion read
+
+      radius( D(GOOD) )  <=  T  <  distance( pole, D(BAD) )
+
+  and such a T EXISTS if and only if
+
+      radius( D(GOOD) )  <  distance( pole, D(BAD) )
+
+  -- the good descriptions must lie closer to their centre than that
+  centre lies to any bad one. Where that holds, non-transitivity never
+  bites, because nothing is ever chained: every comparison has the same
+  fixed anchor.
+
+AND THIS IS WHY UNDERSTANDING COMES FIRST. A canonicaliser that collapses
+the varying part reduces the diameter of D(GOOD) TO ZERO, and then any
+T >= 0 satisfies the left inequality and the choice of representative
+cannot matter at all. Tolerance is needed exactly where D cannot do that
+-- and there the margin must be checked, not assumed.
+
+    radius 0          any T works; where the pole IS matters not at all
+    radius > 0        T must fit between the spread about the pole and
+                      the gap to BAD -- and somebody must know both
+
+THE HEART OF THE OPERATION, then, is one expression:
+
+    Equivalence( D(b_pole),  D(b),  T )
+
+and its three parts are owned by three different parties. That division
+is the whole architecture:
+
+    Equivalence   its STRUCTURE      THE FRAMEWORK. The same for every
+                  --------------     test ever written; no test may
+                                     change how equivalence WORKS, only
+                                     what it is given.
+
+    D             the DESCRIPTION    THE TEST APPLICATION, in two pieces:
+                  --------------     what it PRINTS, and the
+                                     canonicaliser that rewrites that
+                                     into canonical form. Both are the
+                                     author's, and together they are D.
+
+    T             the TOLERANCE      THE TESTER, as declared parameters.
+
+    b_pole        the REFERENCE      THE STORE. Written by acceptance,
+                  --------------     read by every comparison after.
+
+THE FRAMEWORK OWNS NO JUDGEMENT. It supplies the machinery for both knobs
+and chooses neither -- which is why every absorption is a CLAIM the
+author makes and can be held to (section 8), rather than a behaviour the
+tool exhibits.
+
+AND THE TWO KNOBS ARE THE AUTHOR'S TOGETHER. D and T are not owned by
+different people or held in different places: they are one decision about
+one scenario, taken twice. Section 6 says which to reach for first;
+nothing says they may be separated, and a design that files them apart
+makes "what does this test absorb?" a question with two answers in two
+places.
+
+THE DISJOINTNESS IS A DEMAND ON THE AUTHOR. GOOD and BAD must not overlap
+-- and where a specification leaves a behaviour both admissible and not,
+no test of it can exist. The fault is then in the specification, and no
+choice of D or T repairs it.
+
+
+2  THE CHANNEL
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+Behaviour is never inspected. It is expressed, measured, perceived, and only
+the perception arrives. The path from the one to the other adds distortion:
+the same behaviour, run twice, is perceived differently.
+
+The channel cannot be removed. It can only be compensated for. Every
+mechanism in HWUT exists for that single purpose.
+
+
+3  THE TWO ARMS
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+Judgement compares two perceptions, not a perception against truth:
+
+    admissible behaviour --> channel --> perception --> freeing --> NOMINAL
+                                                          ^
+                                                     THE SAME MAP
+                                                          |
+    current behaviour ----> channel --> perception --> freeing --> SUBJECT
+
+The nominal -- the GOOD file -- is one more perception, distorted by the
+same channel, then frozen. It is evidence, not authority.
+
+THE LAW OF THE ARMS: the freeing map is identical on both arms. Applied to
+the subject alone, it compares an interpretation against a raw perception,
+and the comparison means nothing.
+
+Its corollary, where the nominal is stored already freed:
+
+    free(NOMINAL) == NOMINAL          -- IDEMPOTENCE
+
+A freeing that is not idempotent makes the arms asymmetric silently.
+
+
+4  FREEING IS A QUOTIENT
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+Compensating for the channel means declaring which differences are channel
+and which are behaviour. Perceptions are thereby collected into classes, and
+the classes -- not the perceptions -- are compared.
+
+There are exactly two ways to build such a class.
+
+
+5  THE TWO MEANS
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+    UNDERSTANDING       sees the invariant behind the varying appearance.
+                        Picks one CANONICAL REPRESENTATIVE of the class,
+                        then compares BYTE-EXACT.
+                        Equality after a function: reflexive, symmetric,
+                        TRANSITIVE.
+                        Carried by pype.
+
+    TOLERANCE           compares pairwise within a band; no representative.
+                        Reflexive, symmetric, NOT transitive --
+                            a ~ b,  b ~ c,  yet  a !~ c
+                        (two values each within epsilon of a third, two
+                        epsilons apart). This is the mathematical tolerance
+                        relation: congruence with transitivity removed.
+                        Carried by compare.
+
+Understanding loosens nothing. It changes the object, then judges it
+exactly. Seeing through the disorder is what buys the strictness.
+Tolerance loosens the criterion itself.
+
+
+6  THE HIERARCHY
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+    Understand what can be understood.
+    Tolerate only what cannot.
+
+A transitive quotient composes: classes may be built, nested and reasoned
+about. A tolerance relation does not compose, so nothing can be built on top
+of it. Choosing tolerance where understanding was available is therefore a
+strict loss, not a matter of taste.
+
+In the terms of 1.1: both knobs move the same two inequalities, but D
+moves them by CHANGING THE OBJECT and T by WEAKENING THE RELATION. Only
+the first leaves a relation that composes -- so reach for D first, and
+for T only over what D cannot reach.
+
+A suite heavy in tolerances and light in pype scripts is a suite whose
+author declined to understand the output and bought a looser verdict
+instead.
+
+
+7  THE ASYMMETRY OF ERROR
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+    admissible, but RED     the FIRST line of 1.1 broken. A nuisance.
+                            Visible. Someone investigates.
+
+    inadmissible, but GREEN the SECOND line broken -- the real failure,
+                            invisible by construction: a passing test
+                            reports nothing, and the evidence was
+                            discarded before the comparison.
+
+Every tolerance and every canonicalisation is therefore a CLAIM: what is
+absorbed here is channel distortion, not behaviour. A wrong claim swallows a
+real difference and the light stays green.
+
+Hence: absorb the least that works.
+
+
+8  DECLARATION
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+A claim that is written down can be reviewed, argued with, and withdrawn. A
+pype script and a stated tolerance are on the record. A matcher that absorbs
+variation by inference makes the same claims invisibly, and no reader can
+attack what no reader can see.
+
+This, not superior leniency, is the argument for HWUT's shape.
+
+
+9  DIRECTNESS
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+The freeing happens in the mind of the tester. HWUT supplies the tools for
+that mind, and is measured by the distance between what the tester knows and
+what the tester must write:
+
+    knows    "these six lines are a set, not a sequence"
+    writes    potpourri                              -- distance ~ 0
+
+    knows    "this timestamp is not behaviour"
+    writes    a regex over the line shape            -- distance > 0:
+                                                        mechanism, not meaning
+
+THE CRITERION: the artefact is isomorphic to the thought.
+
+Wherever the tester must speak in terms of the mechanism rather than the
+meaning, the tool has failed -- however capable that mechanism is. This is
+the review question to put to every construct in the language.
+
+
+10  THE NAME
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+Understanding and Tolerance are the differentiator. Every golden-master
+framework has some tolerance mechanism; almost none declares an
+understanding stage in front of the comparison, and so most buy leniency by
+giving up exactness. HWUT buys exactness by understanding first.
+
+"Unit test" names a category with a thousand members and hides all of the
+above. U and T say what the thing is for; the letter order is also the
+data flow and the epistemic order.

+================================================================================
+HWUT 2.0: ROLLOUT MANIFEST -- STAGED STEPS TOWARD ADOPTION
+================================================================================
+Status: PROPOSAL, 2026-07-19. Written down to be reconsidered later; nothing
+here is committed work. Update STATE markers as decisions fall.
+
+Companion documents:
+    claude/PLAN-compare-region-refactoring.txt   engine work (DONE thru Stage 7)
+    DOC/SEMANTICS.txt (in repo)                  the authoritative semantics
+    MANUAL.txt        (in repo)                  the user-facing front door
+
+GUIDING RULE (the one honest sentence)
+======================================
+Every stage that only builds infrastructure must be followed by a stage
+that tests whether anyone cares. Plumbing first is the comfortable order;
+it is not the order that finds out whether the market does.
+
+The strategic positioning to test (from review, 2026-07-19): HWUT's
+tolerant-comparison semantics as the DETERMINISTIC ORACLE LAYER for fuzzy
+output -- classical golden-file testing AND AI/agent-output evaluation --
+differentiated from exact-match (too brittle) and LLM-as-judge (costly,
+unreproducible) alike.
+
+
+STAGE R-1: RUNNER CORE (discovery + build-as-test)        STATE: PROPOSED
+================================================================================
+User's step, confirmed as the right start; well-understood, weeks not months.
+    - Recurse directory trees for TEST/ dirs; read the --hwut-info protocol
+      (title, CHOICES); execute language-agnostically: .py via interpreter,
+      everything else as-is via shebang (rule already proven in the sandbox
+      runner and by tool/TEST/test-hwut-compare-tool.sh).
+    - MAKE/BUILD IS PART OF THE TEST: a failing build is a FAILING TEST,
+      not an error outside the system. Capture the build log as a
+      first-class artifact on failure. Consider incremental-build caching
+      across choices (build time dominates suite time in C/C++ shops --
+      the audience this feature serves).
+    - Parallel execution with deterministic output ordering. Isolation is
+      free (black-box model); take the parallelism.
+    - PRIORITY WITHIN THE STAGE: the RE-RECORD WORKFLOW over traversal
+      depth. Daily UX is "a golden drifted -- show the semantic diff,
+      accept/reject per test, per choice." This loop is where users decide
+      whether they love the tool. Budget accordingly.
+
+STAGE R-2: REACH BEFORE FEATURES (packaging that tests adoption)  STATE: PROPOSED
+================================================================================
+Replaces "deb/rpm" as the packaging target; reach-ordered for the current
+world:
+    1. PyPI: 'pipx install hwut' -- one-command trial for strangers.
+    2. CI integration: a GitHub Action + GitLab CI template ('run HWUT,
+       fail the pipeline on red, attach the diff report').
+    3. Container image.
+    4. deb/rpm LAST -- for the embedded/regulated shops that genuinely
+       require OS packages. They will ask; that is the moment to build it.
+Consider a pytest-plugin face (invoke HWUT dirs from pytest) -- adoption
+is ecosystem-driven; meet developers inside their ecosystem rather than
+beside it.
+GATE: after R-2, watch for organic adoption signal (installs, issues,
+questions from strangers). The gate decides how much conviction the later
+stages deserve.
+
+STAGE R-3: THE CONCEPT, NAMED AND PUBLISHED                STATE: PROPOSED
+================================================================================
+Concepts get established by a memorable NAME + a WRITTEN SEMANTICS + a
+REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION. Two of three exist (SEMANTICS.txt, the engine).
+    - Name the discipline (working candidates: "tolerant oracles",
+      "lawful comparison" -- decide deliberately, it is the brand).
+    - One long-form concept piece written FROM SEMANTICS.txt: equivalence
+      as edit-class membership; analogies as consistency obligations;
+      nominal-authoritative asymmetry; THE LAW (two faces, one verdict,
+      machine-checked). Conference-talk version of the same.
+    - NOT an HWUT manual, NOT a book-for-money (reviewed 2026-07-19:
+      books market tools at a loss; they do not monetize them).
+
+STAGE R-4: THE DIFFERENTIATOR DEMO (AI at the edges)       STATE: PROPOSED
+================================================================================
+AI belongs at the EDGES of the framework, never in the verdict -- the
+engine's value IS the deterministic, lawful verdict.
+    - GOLDEN GENERALIZER: from N sample runs of the same test, infer the
+      tolerance annotations (varying hex/ids -> analogies; wobbling
+      numbers -> numeric tolerance; reordered blocks -> potpourri;
+      trace rules -> constraint_db). Turns hand-annotation into review.
+      This is the demo that makes people lean forward.
+    - RE-RECORD REVIEWER: when a golden drifts, classify the semantic
+      diff (benign drift vs. behavioral change). Directly attacks the
+      "change-detector test" stigma -- the concept's biggest cultural
+      liability.
+    - Optional, architecture-ready: an '##! semantic' region handler
+      whose equivalence is judged by a model, framed and bounded by the
+      deterministic engine (region kinds are the OPEN axis; one package +
+      one registry entry, by design).
+
+STAGE R-5: COVERAGE -- DEFERRED, AND SCOPED IF EVER        STATE: DEFERRED
+================================================================================
+Original step "generalized coverage storage" (parse a wide range of
+coverage data, unify in an hwut-common format) is NOT recommended as
+stated: format-parsing is a maintenance treadmill, interchange formats
+already exist, and coverage aggregation is not why anyone chooses HWUT.
+    - IF built: consume lcov info + Cobertura XML ONLY (~90% of the
+      ecosystem exports one of these) -- never N native formats.
+    - The strategically interesting version: PER-TEST coverage storage
+      feeding TEST-IMPACT SELECTION ("this diff touches these files; run
+      only tests whose coverage intersects"). Turns coverage from
+      reporting into daily-felt speed. Build it for THAT, or not at all.
+    - ENTRY CONDITION: a real user asks, or R-2's gate shows adoption.
+
+STAGE R-6: MONETIZATION -- ONLY BEHIND THE GATE            STATE: PROPOSED
+================================================================================
+If (and only if) the R-2 gate shows signal:
+    - Paying niches, in order of fit: (a) regulated/embedded verification
+      (black-box output testing with a written semantics + machine-checked
+      consistency maps onto certification needs); (b) AI-agent output
+      evaluation (deterministic evals, cheaper + reproducible vs.
+      LLM-as-judge).
+    - Monetize via consulting, training, enterprise support -- not books,
+      not licenses on the engine (openness IS the adoption strategy).
+
+
+RECONSIDER-LATER LIST (open, deliberately undecided)
+====================================================
+    - CLI UX design (user's step 3): agreed necessary; design it around
+      the re-record loop (R-1) rather than as a separate stage.
+    - The concept name (R-3) -- decide once, early, deliberately.
+    - Whether the pytest-plugin face compromises the language-agnostic
+      identity or amplifies it (lean: amplifies -- it is a door, not a home).
+    - Multi-run golden capture protocol for the generalizer (R-4): does
+      the runner re-run tests N times, or collect across CI history?
+    - Where the AI features live: core, plugin, or paid tier.
+
+
+ORDERING SUMMARY (proposed vs. user's original)
+===============================================
+    user:      discovery/build -> coverage unification -> CLI -> deb/rpm
+    proposed:  R-1 discovery/build (+re-record UX, CLI folded in)
+               R-2 PyPI/CI reach                        <- GATE: adoption?
+               R-3 concept named + published
+               R-4 AI golden-generalizer demo
+               R-5 coverage (deferred; per-test/impact-scoped if ever)
+               R-6 monetization (behind the gate)
+================================================================================

+#! /bin/bash
+# SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+#
+# @hwut {
+#     title      = "adm/import_graph.py: who depends on whom, and the layering"
+#     choices    = ["depth", "formats", "layering", "refused", "shared",
+#                   "unreadable", "vut"]
+#     eq-pattern = ["STATUS: [0-9]"]
+# }
+#
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# 'adm/import_graph.py' -- the import graph at a stated DEPTH, and the
+# LAYERING check that makes the architecture executable.
+#
+# depth       THE DEPTH IS THE ZOOM: 1 names outer directories, 2 the
+#             inner ones, 0 the modules themselves. The same tree,
+#             three pictures.
+# formats     'tree' for reading, 'edges' for grep and for diff, 'svg'
+#             for a picture drawn HERE -- no graphviz, no browser --
+#             'dot' for graphviz, 'mermaid' for a browser with nothing
+#             installed. A MUTUAL PAIR is drawn with a head at both
+#             ends, so a cycle shows itself.
+# layering    A DECLARATION SAYS WHAT MAY HAPPEN; an edge no rule
+#             permits is a VIOLATION, named by both ends. The check
+#             passes on an obedient tree and BITES on a disobedient
+#             one -- both shown, because a check that never fails
+#             proves nothing.
+# shared      WHICH NAMES DO SEVERAL COMPONENTS IMPORT? A name three
+#             components reach for is no part of whichever one holds
+#             it -- it is CONTRACT MATERIAL, and where it lives inside
+#             one of its own readers it holds a cycle shut.
+# unreadable  a module that cannot be parsed is REPORTED, never
+#             silently dropped: a graph missing an edge it could not
+#             read is a graph that lies.
+# refused     by name: an unknown format, an unknown option, a
+#             declaration that is not one.
+# vut         THE REAL TREE. The outer picture, and the layering it
+#             declares -- so a change to either shows up here.
+#
+# THE FIXTURES ARE TINY TREES built in a work directory, so what this
+# suite proves does not depend on the shape of the tree it lives in --
+# except in the 'vut' choice, which is about exactly that.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)      # the tree root: adm/TEST is two below
+TOOL="$ROOT/adm/import_graph.py"
+unset NO_COLOR CI COLUMNS
+
+case "$1" in
+    --hwut-info)
+        echo "adm/import_graph.py: who depends on whom, and the layering;"
+        echo "CHOICES: depth, formats, layering, shared, unreadable, refused, vut, door;"
+        echo "HAPPY: STATUS: [0-9];"
+        exit 0 ;;
+esac
+
+WORK=$(mktemp -d)
+trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
+cd "$WORK"
+
+face() {                # <args...> -- status and stdout
+    python3 "$TOOL" "$@" > out.txt 2> err.txt
+    echo "STATUS: $?"
+    echo "STDOUT {"; sed "s|$WORK|<work>|g" < out.txt \
+                     | sed 's/^/    /'; echo "}"
+    if [ -s err.txt ]; then
+        echo "STDERR {"; sed "s|$WORK|<work>|g" < err.txt \
+                         | sed 's/^/    /'; echo "}"
+    fi
+}
+
+fixture() {             # a tiny tree: faces -> engine -> base
+    mkdir -p tree/faces tree/engine/plan tree/engine/store tree/base
+    printf 'from tree.engine.plan.wish import Wish\nfrom tree.base.util import helper\n' \
+        > tree/faces/run.py
+    printf 'from tree.engine.store.book import Book\n' \
+        > tree/faces/show.py
+    printf 'from tree.engine.store.book import Book\nfrom tree.base.util import helper\n' \
+        > tree/engine/plan/wish.py
+    printf 'from tree.base.util import helper\n' \
+        > tree/engine/store/book.py
+    printf 'def helper(): pass\n' > tree/base/util.py
+    for d in tree tree/faces tree/engine tree/engine/plan \
+             tree/engine/store tree/base; do
+        printf '' > "$d/__init__.py"
+    done
+}
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+case "$1" in
+
+depth)
+    fixture
+    echo "--- depth 1: the outer directories"
+    face tree --depth=1 --format=edges
+    echo "--- depth 2: the inner ones"
+    face tree --depth=2 --format=edges
+    echo "--- depth 0: the modules themselves"
+    face tree --depth=0 --format=edges
+    echo "--- and the nested blocks a person reads"
+    face tree --depth=2
+    ;;
+
+formats)
+    fixture
+    echo "--- dot"
+    face tree --depth=1 --format=dot
+    echo "--- mermaid"
+    face tree --depth=1 --format=mermaid
+    echo "--- svg: the shape of it, without the coordinates"
+    #  THE NUMBERS ARE LAYOUT, not architecture: a GOOD holding pixel
+    #  positions would move whenever a box grew a character. What is
+    #  recorded is WHAT THE PICTURE CONTAINS.
+    python3 "$TOOL" tree --depth=1 --format=svg > pic.svg 2>&1
+    echo "STATUS: $?"
+    echo "THE PICTURE {"
+    echo "    elements:  $(grep -c '<rect' pic.svg) rect, \
+$(grep -c '<path' pic.svg) path, $(grep -c '<text' pic.svg) text"
+    echo "    boxes:     $(grep -o 'font-size="12"[^<]*>[^<]*' pic.svg \
+| sed 's/.*>//' | sort | tr '\n' ' ')"
+    echo "    mutual:    $(grep -c 'marker-start' pic.svg) pair(s)"
+    echo "    editable:  $(grep -c 'inkscape:connection-start' pic.svg) \
+connector(s) bound, $(grep -c 'connector-avoid' pic.svg) box(es) avoided"
+    echo "    ids:       $(grep -o 'id=\"n_[a-z_]*\"' pic.svg | sort \
+| tr '\n' ' ')"
+    echo "}"
+    ;;
+
+shared)
+    #  CONTRACT MATERIAL, measured.
+    fixture
+    printf 'from tree.base.util import helper, E_Kind\n' \
+        > tree/faces/more.py
+    printf 'from tree.base.util import E_Kind\n' \
+        >> tree/engine/plan/wish.py
+    printf 'from tree.base.util import E_Kind\n' \
+        >> tree/engine/store/book.py
+    echo "--- names three or more components import"
+    face tree --depth=2 --shared=3
+    echo "--- and two or more, which finds the rest"
+    face tree --depth=2 --shared=2
+    ;;
+
+layering)
+    fixture
+    printf 'faces -> engine\nengine -> base\nfaces -> base\n' \
+        > rules.txt
+    echo "--- a tree that obeys its declaration"
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=rules.txt
+    echo "--- ONE edge the declaration does not permit"
+    printf 'from tree.faces.show import thing\n' \
+        >> tree/engine/store/book.py
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=rules.txt
+    echo "--- and a declaration permitting it makes the tree obedient"
+    printf 'engine -> faces\n' >> rules.txt
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=rules.txt
+    echo "--- globs stand on either side"
+    printf 'faces -> *\nengine -> *\n' > wide.txt
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=wide.txt
+
+    #  A SEAL IS ABOUT ONE COMPONENT, not a pair, and is judged at
+    #  MODULE depth -- so it holds at a depth where the direction
+    #  rules cannot see the component at all.
+    echo "--- SEALED: a component that imports nothing of this tree"
+    mkdir -p tree/base/contract
+    printf '' > tree/base/contract/__init__.py
+    printf 'E_Kind = 1\n' > tree/base/contract/enums.py
+    printf 'faces -> *\nengine -> *\nbase -> *\nSEALED base/contract\n' \
+        > sealed.txt
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=sealed.txt
+    echo "--- and one import out of it breaks the seal, at DEPTH 1,"
+    echo "    where 'base/contract' is not even a component"
+    printf 'from tree.engine.plan.wish import Wish\n' \
+        >> tree/base/contract/enums.py
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=sealed.txt
+
+    #  A DOOR IS THE MIRROR OF A SEAL: a seal says NOTHING LEAVES, a
+    #  door says NOTHING ENTERS BUT HERE. Judged at MODULE depth too,
+    #  and a component's own modules are not callers.
+    echo "--- DOOR: one module is a component's only entrance. Here"
+    echo "    every caller already reaches PAST it, and each is named"
+    printf 'from tree.engine.store.book import Book\n' \
+        > tree/engine/plan/api.py
+    printf 'faces -> *\nengine -> *\nbase -> *\nDOOR engine/plan/api\n' \
+        > door.txt
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=door.txt
+    echo "--- every caller through the door instead, and the tree is"
+    echo "    obedient -- while the component's OWN module still"
+    echo "    reaches its parts freely: a door is for callers, and a"
+    echo "    part is not a caller"
+    printf 'from tree.engine.plan.api import Wish\n' > tree/faces/show.py
+    printf 'from tree.engine.plan.api import Wish\n' > tree/faces/run.py
+    printf 'E_Kind = 1\n' > tree/base/contract/enums.py
+    printf 'from tree.engine.plan.wish import Wish\n' \
+        >> tree/engine/plan/api.py
+    face tree --depth=1 --check=door.txt
+    ;;
+
+unreadable)
+    #  A GRAPH MISSING AN EDGE IT COULD NOT READ IS A GRAPH THAT LIES.
+    fixture
+    printf 'def broken(:\n' > tree/engine/plan/torn.py
+    face tree --depth=1 --format=edges
+    ;;
+
+refused)
+    fixture
+    echo "--- a format that does not exist"
+    face tree --format=sideways
+    echo "--- an option the tool does not take"
+    face tree --sideways
+    echo "--- a declaration that is not one"
+    printf 'faces and engine\n' > bad.txt
+    face tree --check=bad.txt
+    echo "--- a declaration that is not there"
+    face tree --check=nowhere.txt
+    ;;
+
+vut)
+    #  THE REAL TREE: the outer picture, and its own declaration.
+    #  THE SUITES ARE EXCLUDED -- a test application imports whatever
+    #  it tests, and is no part of the shape it examines.
+    cd "$ROOT"
+    python3 "$TOOL" . --depth=1 --exclude="*/TEST/*" \
+        --exclude="*/test-*" --exclude="*/config.py" > "$WORK/o.txt" 2>&1
+    echo "STATUS: $?"
+    echo "THE OUTER PICTURE {"; sed 's/^/    /' < "$WORK/o.txt"; echo "}"
+    python3 "$TOOL" . --depth=2 --check=adm/LAYERING.txt \
+        --exclude="*/TEST/*" --exclude="*/test-*" \
+        --exclude="*/config.py" > "$WORK/c.txt" 2>&1
+    echo "STATUS: $?"
+    echo "THE LAYERING {"; sed 's/^/    /' < "$WORK/c.txt"; echo "}"
+    ;;
+
+*)
+    echo "no such choice: $1"
+    exit 1 ;;
+esac

+#! /bin/bash
+# SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+#
+# @hwut {
+#     title      = "Static analysis: what this tree tolerates"
+#     eq-pattern = ["ruff [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+"]
+# }
+#
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+# STATIC ANALYSIS: the source read WITHOUT BEING RUN.
+#
+# NOT A 'HYGIENE' SUITE, and the word is deliberately avoided: hygiene
+# in this tree means A COMPONENT'S OWN source and GOOD files, checked
+# against the defects that recurred while THAT component was built
+# ('engine/operations/TEST/test-hygiene.py'). It belongs to its
+# component and knows what that component keeps getting wrong. This
+# suite belongs to no component and knows only what a tool reports
+# about every file alike. This suite and
+# 'test-import_graph.sh' beside it are the two in this tree that ask
+# about the code base's SHAPE rather than its BEHAVIOUR -- every other
+# suite runs the product and reads what came out.
+#
+# IT IS A RATCHET. 'ruff' is run over the tree with the tree's own
+# configuration ('adm/ruff.toml'), and every kind of finding that
+# still stands is printed, SORTED -- what this tree TOLERATES today.
+#
+# IT IS NOT A TEST THAT THE TREE IS CLEAN. It is a test that the tree
+# is NO LESS CLEAN THAN IT WAS. A finding of a new kind, or one more
+# instance of a kind already tolerated, moves the GOOD and the suite
+# says so. A finding REMOVED moves it too, and that re-blessing is the
+# record of an improvement.
+#
+# WHAT IS NOT LISTED HERE IS IN 'adm/ruff.toml', ignored BY NAME with
+# its reason: house style ('%' formatting, hand-aligned imports,
+# asserts as door guards) is not a finding, and 878 of one kind drown
+# every finding that matters.
+#
+# THE RUFF VERSION IS PRINTED, and it is a HAPPY PATTERN: two runs
+# under different ruffs are EQUIVALENT on that line. The version is
+# not the fact this suite is about -- THE FINDINGS ARE. A ruff that
+# knows new rules will move the list below, and that is where the
+# suite speaks; a ruff that merely counts higher and finds the same
+# things has said nothing, and the suite says nothing back.
+#
+# WITHOUT THE PATTERN this test would go red on every upgrade for a
+# reason nobody could act on, and a suite that cries at noise is a
+# suite that gets re-blessed unread.
+#
+# NO RUFF, NO REPORT. A missing tool is a MISSING PRECONDITION, and a
+# missing precondition is a RESULT stated as one -- never a silent
+# pass that would let hygiene rot unwatched.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+HERE=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)
+ROOT=$(cd "$HERE/../.." && pwd)      # the tree root: adm/TEST is two below
+CONFIG="$ROOT/adm/ruff.toml"
+unset NO_COLOR CI COLUMNS
+
+case "$1" in
+    --hwut-info)
+        echo "Static analysis: what this tree tolerates;"
+        echo "HAPPY: ruff [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+\\.[0-9]+;"
+        exit 0 ;;
+esac
+
+if ! command -v ruff > /dev/null 2>&1; then
+    echo "PRECONDITION MISSING: 'ruff' is not installed"
+    echo "    the static analysis of this tree cannot be asked"
+    echo "    without it;"
+    echo "    'pip install ruff' and run again"
+    exit 1
+fi
+
+cd "$ROOT"
+
+echo "==[ STATIC ANALYSIS ]========================================"
+echo "ground:  $(ruff --version)"
+echo "config:  adm/ruff.toml"
+echo "ignored: $(python3 - <<'PYEOF'
+import re, io
+text = io.open("adm/ruff.toml", encoding="utf-8").read()
+match = re.search(r"lint\.ignore\s*=\s*\[(.*?)\]", text, re.S)
+print(", ".join(sorted(re.findall(r'"([^"]+)"', match.group(1))))
+      if match else "(none)")
+PYEOF
+)"
+echo
+
+#  SORTED BY RULE, never by count: a count that ties would order two
+#  lines by whichever the tool named first, and a GOOD file may hold
+#  no such coin-toss.
+echo "TOLERATED {"
+ruff check --config "$CONFIG" . --statistics 2>/dev/null \
+    | grep -E '^ *[0-9]+\s+[A-Z]+[0-9]+' \
+    | sed -E 's/^ *([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+([A-Z]+[0-9]+)[[:space:]]*(\[.\])?[[:space:]]*/\2|\1|/' \
+    | sort \
+    | awk -F'|' '{ printf "    %-10s %5d  %s\n", $1, $2, $3 }'
+echo "}"
+echo
+
+TOTAL=$(ruff check --config "$CONFIG" . --statistics 2>/dev/null \
+        | grep -E '^ *[0-9]+\s+[A-Z]+[0-9]+' \
+        | awk '{ s += $1 } END { print s + 0 }')
+echo "total tolerated: $TOTAL"
+
+#  THE CORRECTNESS SET STANDS AT ZERO, and this is the line that must
+#  never move upward. Four rules, chosen because each can HIDE A
+#  FAILURE rather than merely offend:
+#
+#      F      a name that is not there
+#      B011   a dispatch that vanishes under 'python -O' and then
+#             returns None to a caller who blames their own code
+#      B020   a loop variable rebinding what the loop reads from
+#      S110   a swallow with no reason given
+#
+#  'S102' (exec) is NOT here: the pype language executes its own
+#  effect blocks, so exec is the feature. A set that can never be
+#  empty is a set people learn to ignore.
+echo
+echo "MUST STAND AT ZERO {"
+ZERO=$(ruff check --config "$CONFIG" --select F,B011,B020,S110 \
+       --exclude "*/TEST/*" . --statistics 2>/dev/null \
+       | grep -E '^ *[0-9]+\s+[A-Z]+[0-9]+' \
+       | sed -E 's/^ *([0-9]+)[[:space:]]+([A-Z]+[0-9]+).*/    \2 \1/')
+if [ -z "$ZERO" ]; then
+    echo "    empty -- no name that is not there, no dispatch that"
+    echo "    vanishes under '-O', no swallow without a reason"
+else
+    echo "$ZERO"
+fi
+echo "}"
diff --git a/adm/cythonizer.py b/adm/cythonizer.py
new file mode 100644

+++ b/adm/cythonizer.py

+from setuptools import setup, Extension
+from Cython.Build import cythonize
+import os
+import sys
+
+sys.argv = [sys.argv[0]] + ["build_ext", "--inplace"]
+
+# Define the extension module
+# Ensure the path matches your project structure
+ext = Extension(
+    name="engine.compare.tolerance.line_element",
+    sources=["engine/compare/tolerance/line_element.pyx"],
+    # Adding compiler directives for maximum performance
+    extra_compile_args=["-O3"] if os.name != 'nt' else ["/O2"],
+)
+
+setup(
+    name="LineElement Extension",
+    ext_modules=cythonize(
+        [ext],
+        compiler_directives={
+            'language_level': "3",
+            'boundscheck': False,
+            'wraparound': False,
+            'cdivision': True,
+            'initializedcheck': False,
+        }
+    ),
+)

+"""SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+PURPOSE: THE SHAPE OF EVERY DIFFERENCE IN A TREE, in one reading.
+
+For each 'GOOD/<member>.txt' that has a candidate from the last run in
+'TMP/store/<member>.stdout', the two texts are read and one shape is
+reported:
+
+    SAME       the texts are equal
+    GREW       every recorded line stands, in order; lines stand
+               between or around them
+    SHRANK     every line that stands was recorded, in order; lines
+               the GOOD holds are gone
+    DIVERGED   neither: a recorded line changed or moved
+    UNREADABLE a file could not be read
+
+The shapes are 'hwut.run''s own ('operations/result.py'); this reads a
+whole tree at once, from what a run already left, and runs nothing.
+
+EVERY SHAPE BUT 'SAME' IS A FAILURE. The shape says WHERE TO LOOK, not
+who is wrong. A GOOD blessed under a framework that swallowed output
+GREW; so did a filter that stopped filtering. One is stale ground, the
+other is the defect a golden master exists to catch, and they wear the
+same shape. Nothing here decides which, and nothing here blesses:
+'hwut.accept' is the one door a nominal changes through.
+
+    adm/good_audit.py [<directory>] [--verbose]
+
+EXIT: 0 where every member stands as recorded, 1 where any does not,
+      2 where the directory does not exist.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+"""
+import os
+import sys
+
+
+def subsequence_f(small, large):
+    """
+    RETURN: bool, True where every line of 'small' appears in 'large'
+            in the same order -- 'large' may hold lines between and
+            around them, and holds no line of 'small' out of turn.
+    """
+    it = iter(large)
+    return all(line in it for line in small)
+
+
+def shape_of(good_path, candidate_path):
+    """
+    RETURN: str, one of 'SAME', 'GREW', 'SHRANK', 'DIVERGED',
+            'UNREADABLE' -- the shape of the difference between the
+            GOOD and the candidate, in the framework's own words.
+    """
+    try:
+        with open(good_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
+            old = fh.read().splitlines()
+        with open(candidate_path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as fh:
+            new = fh.read().splitlines()
+    except OSError:
+        return "UNREADABLE"
+
+    if old == new:                       return "SAME"
+    if len(new) > len(old) and subsequence_f(old, new): return "GREW"
+    if len(old) > len(new) and subsequence_f(new, old): return "SHRANK"
+    return "DIVERGED"
+
+
+def pair_list_of(directory):
+    """
+    YIELD: [0] str  the GOOD's path
+           [1] str  the candidate's path in 'TMP/store'
+           [2] str  '<test>--<choice>', the member's name
+
+    Only members a run has left a candidate for: a GOOD with no
+    candidate was not run and cannot be judged.
+    """
+    for here, dir_name_list, file_name_list in os.walk(directory):
+        if os.path.basename(here) != "GOOD": continue
+        store = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(here), "TMP", "store")
+        if not os.path.isdir(store): continue
+        for name in sorted(file_name_list):
+            if not name.endswith(".txt"): continue
+            stem = name[:-len(".txt")]
+            candidate = os.path.join(store, stem + ".stdout")
+            if os.path.isfile(candidate):
+                yield os.path.join(here, name), candidate, stem
+
+
+def main(argv):
+    """
+    RETURN: int, 0 where every member stands as recorded, 1 where any
+            does not -- EVERY shape but 'SAME' is a failure; 2 where
+            the directory does not exist.
+    """
+    directory  = "."
+    verbose_f  = False
+    for argument in argv:
+        if   argument in ("-v", "--verbose"): verbose_f = True
+        elif argument in ("-h", "--help"):    print(__doc__); return 0
+        else:                                 directory = argument
+
+    if not os.path.isdir(directory):
+        print("no such directory: %s" % directory, file=sys.stderr)
+        return 2
+
+    bin_db = {"SAME": [], "GREW": [], "SHRANK": [], "DIVERGED": [],
+              "UNREADABLE": []}
+    for good, candidate, stem in pair_list_of(directory):
+        bin_db[shape_of(good, candidate)].append(
+            (os.path.relpath(good, directory), stem))
+
+    for kind, note in (("GREW", "extra lines; every recorded line "
+                                "stands, in order"),
+                       ("SHRANK", "lines missing; what stands was "
+                                  "recorded, in order"),
+                       ("DIVERGED", "a recorded line changed or moved"),
+                       ("UNREADABLE", "could not be read")):
+        entry_list = bin_db[kind]
+        if not entry_list: continue
+        print("%s -- %d:" % (kind, len(entry_list)))
+        print("    %s" % note)
+        for path, _stem in entry_list: print("        %s" % path)
+        print()
+
+    if verbose_f and bin_db["SAME"]:
+        print("SAME -- %d member(s) stand as recorded" % len(bin_db["SAME"]))
+    else:
+        print("%d member(s) stand as recorded" % len(bin_db["SAME"]))
+
+    return 0 if len(bin_db["SAME"]) == sum(len(v) for v in bin_db.values()) \
+             else 1
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

new file mode 100644
