+THE VUT COVERAGE RECORD -- the format, line by line
+==============================================================================
+
+Mechanics only. WHY the format is shaped this way stands in RATIONALE
+(D-5 the skeleton, D-7 the provenance, D-8 and D-18 the run, D-11 the
+measures, D-12 named points). What is OPEN stands in DISCUSSIONS.
+
+A record has TWO SPELLINGS of one content: the TEXT spelling, sections
+1 to 7, and the BINARY spelling, section 8. The file on disk,
+'.cover', is BINARY. The text is the presentation: 'hwut.cov convert'
+renders either into the other, and the tests print it.
+
+In the text spelling a record is UTF-8, LF terminated. Every line is
+one of five kinds, in this order:
+
+    ##VUT-COVERAGE <version>     the version line, FIRST
+    ##<key>: <value>             header lines
+    SF:<path>                    a source file, opening a BLOCK
+    EX:<ranges>  CV:<ranges>     the line axis of that block
+    <TAG>:<points>               a registered measure of that block
+
+Blank lines are skipped wherever they stand. Trailing whitespace on a
+line is stripped before reading.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+1  THE VERSION LINE
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    ##VUT-COVERAGE 2
+
+FIRST line of the record. The number is decimal. A reader that does not
+write this version REFUSES; it does not attempt a partial reading.
+
+    1    the header named the run by NAME: '##test:' and '##choice:'
+    2    the header names RUN IDS: '##run:'      <- what this build writes
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+2  THE HEADER
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Six keys, every one REQUIRED. A missing key is a refusal. Order is as
+written below; a reader accepts any order. Leading and trailing
+whitespace around key and value is stripped, so the column alignment
+below is cosmetic.
+
+    ##run:      <run ids>       WHO ran -- see 2.1
+    ##language: <name>          the language of the sources
+    ##tool:     <name>          the coverage tool that made the artifact
+    ##format:   <name>          the artifact format it was read from
+    ##counts:   no | yes        whether 'CV' carries hit counts -- see 4.3
+
+'language', 'tool' and 'format' are free text without commas. A MERGED
+record whose parts disagree on one of them carries every value it saw,
+comma separated and sorted ('coverage,trace').
+
+2.1  THE RUN LINE
+
+    ##run:      0.1             one run
+    ##run:      -               NO run: the record names none
+    ##run:      0.0,0.1,3       several runs: a MERGED record
+
+A run id is '<app id>' or '<app id>.<choice id>', both decimal, issued
+by the register of the test directory ('bookkeeper/test_id_db.py'). The
+value is a SET: ids sorted ascending, comma separated, no spaces. '-'
+is the empty set, which is what a record fresh from a reader carries
+until 'record.seated' gives it one.
+
+A word that spells no run id is a refusal, and the refusal names the
+word.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+3  THE SOURCE FILE LINE
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    SF:parser/core.py
+
+Opens a BLOCK and closes the one before it. The path is RELATIVE TO THE
+TEST DIRECTORY, with '/' as separator on every platform. It may leave
+the directory ('../core.py'); an aggregator rebases it onto the gather
+root.
+
+Blocks are written in ascending path order, so two runs of one test
+produce the same bytes.
+
+A block MUST carry 'EX' and 'CV'. A block missing either is a refusal.
+A source file that was not measured has NO block -- absence and
+emptiness do not collapse. A source file measured and found to hold no
+executable line has a block with an EMPTY 'EX'.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+4  THE LINE AXIS
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    EX:3+12,5+5        the ranges that COULD be executed
+    CV:3+12            the ranges that WERE
+
+Both are DELTA CODED range lists. 'uncovered = EX - CV' and every
+percentage are DERIVED by whoever renders; neither is stored.
+
+4.1  A RANGE
+
+Half-open: '[begin, end)', 'end' the first line AFTER the range. Ranges
+in one list are sorted, disjoint, and never adjacent -- two adjacent
+runs of lines are ONE range.
+
+4.2  THE DELTA CODING
+
+    <d>            a range of ONE line
+    <d>+<L>        a range of L lines
+
+'d' is the gap from the PREVIOUS range's end; the first 'd' is the
+first line number itself. So every 'd' is positive and small.
+
+    lines 3..14 and 20..24     ->    3+12,5+5
+    lines 3, 7, 40             ->    3,3,32
+
+An EMPTY list is the empty string: 'EX:' with nothing after the colon.
+
+REFUSALS: a piece that spells no number; a delta of zero or less (the
+ranges would not advance); a length below one (the range covers no
+line).
+
+4.3  HIT COUNTS
+
+OFF by default. The header's 'counts:' declares whether they stand, so
+a reader never guesses.
+
+    <d>*<C>        a one-line range hit C times
+    <d>+<L>*<C>    an L-line range hit C times
+
+Counts ride on 'CV' only. 'counts: yes' with a piece carrying no count
+is a refusal, and so is a count where the header promised none.
+
+A MERGE of records carrying counts is REFUSED by name
+('CountsNotMergeable'): the union of two ranges has no answer for two
+different counts over one line.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+5  THE MEASURES
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Every measurement that is not the line axis rides in its own line under
+the TAG its measure claims. A block with no such measurement writes no
+such line, so a record of line coverage alone is byte-identical to what
+it was before any measure existed.
+
+Measures are written in registered-NAME order, after 'EX' and 'CV'.
+A tag no measure claims is a refusal; the refusal names every tag this
+build knows. 'hwut.cov formats' prints the table this section
+describes, generated from the registry (RATIONALE D-13) -- when the two
+disagree, the generated one is right.
+
+5.1  REGISTERED MEASURES
+
+    TAG  NAME     SHAPE          MERGEABLE   WHAT IT COUNTS
+    BR   branch   point          no          of the arms leaving this
+                                             decision, how many were taken
+    MC   mcdc     point, same    no          of the conditions in this
+                  line admitted              decision, for how many was
+                                             independence demonstrated
+    TG   toggle   named point    YES         whether this signal bit
+                                             reached both 0 and 1
+    CP   cover    named point    YES         whether this cover point
+                                             was hit
+
+MERGEABLE says whether two records holding it may be unioned. 'branch'
+and 'mcdc' say no: a COUNT of arms taken does not carry WHICH arms, so
+two runs covering different arms cannot be combined. A merge of records
+carrying either is refused by name ('MeasureNotMergeable').
+
+5.2  THE POINT SHAPE  (BR, MC)
+
+    <d>*<covered>/<total>
+
+per DECISION POINT, comma separated, in line order. 'd' is the delta
+from the previous point's line; the first must advance from zero.
+
+    BR:2*1/2          line 2, one of two arms taken
+    MC:4*2/3,0*3/3    line 4, two decisions on it
+
+A delta of ZERO means ANOTHER DECISION ON THE SAME LINE, which
+'if (a && b || c)' produces. It is admitted for 'mcdc' and refused for
+'branch', which is reported per line.
+
+REFUSALS: a piece that spells no point; a first delta that does not
+advance from zero; a zero delta where the measure admits none; a total
+below one; 'covered' above 'total'.
+
+5.3  THE NAMED POINT SHAPE  (TG, CP)
+
+    <d>*<name>*<covered>/<total>
+
+per NAMED point, comma separated, in (line, name) order. The line is
+the point's DECLARED position -- a signal's declaration, a 'cover
+property' statement -- so several points share one line as a matter of
+course: a delta of zero is admitted from the SECOND point on.
+
+    TG:12*data[0]*1/1,0*data[1]*0/1
+
+THE NAME IS WHAT MAKES THE MEASURE MERGEABLE: point identity is
+carried, so two runs are unioned point by point and a point covered in
+either is covered.
+
+A name carrying '*' or ',' -- the encoding's own separators -- is
+REFUSED at writing. There is no escape scheme: a refusal is preferable
+to a corruption, and no witnessed identifier carries one.
+
+REFUSALS: as 5.2, plus a piece that names no point, and a MERGE where
+one (line, name) carries two different totals -- the two records do not
+describe one point.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+6  A WHOLE RECORD
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+    ##VUT-COVERAGE 2
+    ##run:      0.1
+    ##language: c
+    ##tool:     gcov
+    ##format:   gcov-annotated
+    ##counts:   no
+    SF:parser/core.c
+    EX:3+12,5+5
+    CV:3+12
+    BR:5*1/2
+    SF:parser/table.c
+    EX:
+    CV:
+
+'table.c' was measured and holds no executable line. A source file that
+was NOT measured would have no block at all.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+7  WHAT A READER REFUSES
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Every refusal names the FIRST fault and stops. A coverage record half
+read is a coverage report that lies, so nothing recovers and carries
+on.
+
+    RecordFault            the record cannot be read
+      no version line, or one that spells no number
+      a version this build does not write
+      a header key missing
+      a 'run' word that spells no run id
+      a block without 'EX' or 'CV'
+      'EX', 'CV' or a measure line before any 'SF'
+      a line whose key is neither 'SF', 'EX', 'CV' nor a claimed tag
+      a range or count that spells no number
+      a delta that does not advance, a length below one
+      counts promised and absent, or given and not promised
+    MeasureFault           a measure line cannot be read -- see 5.2, 5.3
+    NotMergeable           the records cannot be unioned
+      CountsNotMergeable     one of them carries hit counts
+      MeasureNotMergeable    one of them carries a measure declaring
+                             itself unmergeable
+
+A file that does not parse is SKIPPED by an aggregator and named on
+stderr: one broken record must not cost a whole selection, and it must
+not vanish either. So is a record that names NO run -- it cannot be
+attributed, and a guess would be worse than the loss.
+
+
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+8  THE BINARY SPELLING
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Little-endian throughout. The whole file is ONE zlib stream (level 6);
+what follows is its content, front to back, no padding, no offsets.
+
+    file     =  "VUTC"  u8 version  header  u32 n_files  file_block*
+    header   =  run_set  str language  str tool  str format  u8 counts
+    run_set  =  u32 n  (u32 app_id  u32 choice_id)*
+    str      =  u16 length  UTF-8 bytes
+    file_block = str path  stream EX  stream CV  [stream counts]
+                 u8 n_measures  (tag  stream)*
+    stream   =  u32 n_bytes  byte*
+    tag      =  two ASCII bytes, the measure's tag (5.1)
+
+    version     1 -- what this build writes and reads
+    choice_id   0xFFFFFFFF spells 'no choice' ('47' in the text)
+    counts      0 or 1; 'stream counts' stands iff 1
+    n_files     blocks follow in ascending path order
+
+8.1  THE NUMBER STREAM
+
+Every delta-coded sequence is a stream of unsigned bytes with one
+escape:
+
+    0x00 .. 0xFE   the number itself
+    0xFF           the number follows as u32
+
+Ranges: the stream holds 'd, L' pairs as section 4.2 defines them.
+Counts: one number per COVERED range, in order.
+Points (5.2): 'd, covered, total' per point.
+Named points (5.3): 'd, name, covered, total' per point, the name
+spliced into the stream as a 'str' (u16 length, UTF-8 bytes).
+
+8.2  REFUSALS, in addition to section 7's
+
+    not a zlib stream; no "VUTC"; a version this build does not write;
+    the buffer ends where a field expects more; bytes after the last
+    block; a range delta of zero or a length of zero; an escaped number
+    cut short; a tag no measure claims.
+
+8.3  ONE CONTENT
+
+'unpack(pack(r))' and 'parse(format(r))' are the same record, and
+'format(unpack(pack(r))) == format(r)' byte for byte. The test proves
+it on every witnessed artifact ('TEST/test-binary.py').

+HOW TO INTEGRATE A COVERAGE
+==============================================================================
+
+PURPOSE
+
+This document is the procedure for ADMITTING ONE MORE COVERAGE TOOL
+into the component: what to do, in what order, and where each piece
+goes. It is walked once per tool, by a developer of this component.
+
+It does not explain how a test run OBTAINS coverage -- that chain
+(build the coverage target, wrap, report, harvest) is README section 5
+and RATIONALE D-19, built in 'operations/coverage_action.py'. And it does not restate the laws of
+the record or of a reader; those live in README.txt and RATIONALE.txt
+and are only POINTED AT from here.
+
+
+THE STAGES
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+                            +---------+
+                            | WITNESS |
+                            +----+----+
+                                 |
+                    the ARTIFACT decides the road
+                   format read      format new
+                        |                |
+                        v                v
+                   +-------+        +--------+
+                   | ALIAS |        | READER |
+                   +---+---+        +----+---+
+                       |                 |
+                       |            axis new?
+                       |           no |     | yes
+                       |              |     v
+                       |              | +---------+
+                       |              | | MEASURE |
+                       |              | +----+----+
+                       |              |      |
+                       v              v      v
+                       +--------------+------+
+                                      |
+                                      v
+                                +----------+
+                                | REGISTER |
+                                +----------+
+                                      |
+                                      v
+                                +----------+
+                                |  PROVE   |
+                                +----------+
+                                      |
+                                      v
+                                +----------+
+                                |  LEDGER  |
+                                +----------+
+
+
+WITNESS
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Run the real tool over a real source file. Keep what it wrote under
+'WITNESS-<topic>/<language>/', and add to 'WITNESS-<topic>-artifacts.txt':
+the exact commands with tool versions, and what the artifact shows that
+a specification would not have told you.
+
+    lua 5.4.6, luacov 0.16.0:
+        lua -lluacov demo.lua && luacov
+    FINDING: the stats file cannot tell 'never run' from 'not
+    executable'; only the REPORT can. The reader reads the report.
+
+No reader is written from a specification alone, and no alias is placed
+on belief -- the road is decided by the artifact. Where the tool cannot
+run here, a fixture answering the format's OWN INVARIANT stands in, the
+substitution is stated at the fixture, and the witness remains owed.
+
+
+ALIAS
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+The artifact turned out to be a format already read: one line in
+'readers/__init__.py', one candidate in the registry, done.
+
+    ALIAS_DB:          "gcovr": "lcov"
+    ROOT_CONF_TEXT:    c { coverage = [..., "gcovr", ...] }
+                       (services/_boundary.py -- the shipped table, D-26)
+
+An alias is a FRAMEWORK over a shared format: it is invoked as the
+framework it reads through, and stamps its own name. A tool that needs
+its own call form or its own second call deserves a framework class.
+
+
+FRAMEWORK
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+The artifact is a format already read, but the tool is invoked its own
+way: one 'CCoverageFramework' subclass naming the existing format.
+
+    class FooFramework(CCoverageFramework):
+        name   = "foo"
+        format = LcovFormat()                        # what it writes
+        def wrap(self, argv, config, work_dir):      return argv
+        def report_argv(self, config, work_dir):     return None
+        def instrumented_f(self, target, work_dir):  return None  # optional
+
+    register(FooFramework())
+
+'instrumented_f' is OPTIONAL and answers None where the tool leaves no
+trace to check; it never answers False for want of a way to know.
+
+
+FORMAT
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+The artifact is a new format: one module under 'readers/' holding a
+'CCoverageFormat' and the framework that writes it.
+
+    class FooFormat(CCoverageFormat):
+        name = "foo-json"
+        def read(self, work_dir, source_root, config=None):
+            ...                    # artefact -> record_of(self, ...) | None
+
+    class FooFramework(CCoverageFramework):
+        name   = "foo"
+        format = FooFormat()
+        def wrap(self, argv, config, work_dir): ...
+
+    register(FooFramework())
+
+The laws a format must obey -- absence is None, paths made relative,
+the gather set applied, EX never invented, the pair never the
+percentage, no tool stamped -- and a framework -- spawn nothing, name
+the call -- are 'reader.py' docstring and README section 6. Read an
+existing module of similar shape first; 'simplecov.py' is a small one.
+
+
+MEASURE
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Only where the artifact carries an axis the record does not hold yet
+(line and branch exist; toggle and cover exist). One 'register' call in
+'measure.py': a name, a record tag, an encoding, and the honest answer
+to whether two records holding it merge.
+
+    register(NamedPointMeasure(name="toggle", tag="TG"))
+
+The axis enters at a FILE and a LINE or it does not enter (disc-9,
+RATIONALE D-12).
+
+
+REGISTER
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+Make the tool electable:
+
+    ROOT_CONF_TEXT     the language's 'coverage' list in the shipped
+                       root conf ('services/_boundary.py'), in
+                       preference order -- readable formats first. THE
+                       TABLE IS NOT IN THIS COMPONENT (D-26): an author's
+                       tree carries its own copy in 'hwut-root.conf'.
+    EXTENSION_DB       only where the source extension is new; it
+                       serves 'hwut.cov convert' and the record header
+
+A candidate with no reader is still listed: the machine then refuses
+BY NAME instead of reporting no coverage. An empty candidate list is
+itself an answer ('this build vouches for no tool here') -- never
+invent one.
+
+
+PROVE
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+One HWUT choice in 'TEST/test-readers.py'. The fixture is the tool's
+bytes, pasted verbatim. The choice PRINTS what the reader made of them
+-- plus the format's own cross-check where one exists -- and the
+recorded GOOD file is the specification. No assertions.
+
+    cd TEST && python3 test-readers.py foo > GOOD/test-readers.py--foo.txt
+    # audit the file line by line, THEN bless it
+
+Re-record 'GOOD/hwut.cov--formats.txt': the generated tool/format table
+gained a row, and a reader admitted without it turns the suite red
+(RATIONALE D-13).
+
+
+LEDGER
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+One line each, history only -- what was built, when, against which
+witness:
+
+    DISCUSSIONS.txt todo-2           the reader ledger
+    OVERVIEW-coverage-roads.txt      the road walked, the finding
+
+Do not copy the tool/format table anywhere; it has one author, the
+registry, and 'hwut.cov formats' prints it (RATIONALE D-13).

+LANGUAGES, TOOLS, FORMATS -- the coverage roads, and what is witnessed
+==============================================================================
+
+THE THREE AXES, AND WHO OWNS WHICH. A LANGUAGE names a registry entry;
+the entry lists TOOLS in preference order; 'elect' takes the first the
+machine has; the tool's FORMAT names the reader. Twenty-one tool names,
+eleven formats, one record. The record is the unifier -- everything
+below dies at harvest.
+
+THE COUNTS ABOVE ARE THE ONLY NUMBERS THIS FILE STATES. The table of
+which tool speaks which format is printed by 'hwut.cov formats' from
+the registry itself, and is not copied here (RATIONALE D-13). What
+follows is the SHAPE of the roads and the HISTORY of how each was
+witnessed -- which is what this file is for and what the registry
+cannot hold.
+
+THE FORMATS, and the languages that reach them:

+                                 disc-9(b) is structural, not an
+                                 availability gap
+
+ON A 'UNIFYING BINARY FORMAT'. The unifying FORMAT exists and is not
+binary: the VUT-COVERAGE record -- text, delta-coded, versioned,
+measure-tagged, one writer per key space. Its being TEXT is load-
+bearing: the GOOD files read as specifications, a record diff is a
+legible fact, and 'grep' is a query tool. At these sizes binary buys
+nothing and costs inspection. What 'hwutcov' SHOULD name, if anything,
+is the unifying EXECUTABLE: one entry point with verbs --
+
+    hwutcov elect <language>          name the tool this machine serves
+    hwutcov instrument <build-argv>   amend a build line (the build-
+                                      node provision)
+    hwutcov probe <executable>        can it REGISTER coverage? refuse
+                                      by name before the run spends
+    hwutcov run <argv>                wrap where the road wraps
+    hwutcov report <work-dir>         the named second call
+    hwutcov harvest <work-dir>        artifact -> record
+    hwutcov merge <record>...         where the measures admit it
+
+-- so the orchestration's build and run nodes consume the component
+without importing it, and records remain the only interchange.
+

+corrections, named-point measures, and readers for verilator .dat,
+ghdl psl.json, simplecov resultset and ucis xml all shipped in

+       five copies of the tool/format table withdrawn in favour of
+       one generated one (D-13).
+    2. THE PROVISION CHAIN -- the run side of the reader role. Today
+       'wrap' is the IDENTITY in nine of eleven readers and
+       'report_argv' is None in nine: the component READS eleven
+       formats and can ARRANGE two. For the other nine the readers
+       say in PROSE what the build line must carry -- gcov's
+       '--coverage', verilator's '--coverage', jacoco's '-javaagent:',
+       ghdl's '-fpsl', luacov's 'require' -- and a forgotten flag is
+       discovered at HARVEST, as an honest ABSENT, after the run has
+       already been spent. So:
+           instrument(build_argv, config)  the build node asks what
+                                           the build line must carry
+           probe(executable, config)       can this executable REGISTER
+                                           coverage? ('.gcno' present,
+                                           '__gcov_' symbols, coverage
+                                           points in a verilated model)
+                                           -- refuse BY NAME before the
+                                           run spends anything
+       plus 'report_argv' on the 'verilator_coverage' alias naming
+       'verilator_coverage --write-info' where a 'coverage.dat' stands
+       -- which is also the first alias that must OVERRIDE rather than
+       forward, since two tools sharing a format do not share a drive.
+    3. 'hwut.cov', the unifying EXECUTABLE. Its verbs and the reader
+       role's calls are ONE LIST, or one of them is lying:
+
+           elect       (registry)
+           instrument  instrument(build_argv, config)
+           probe       probe(executable, config)
+           run         wrap(argv, ...)
+           report      report_argv(...)
+           harvest     harvest(dir, root, config)
+           merge       (record.merge)
+           formats     the generated table (D-13)
+
+    4. deferred by doctrine: covergroup BINS (line-less by the UCIS
+       XSD itself), the long-tail readers, and every refusal stands
+       until a real artifact arrives.

+SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+==============================================================================
+RATIONALE -- coverage                                     (settled 2026-08-22)
+==============================================================================
+
+What is DECIDED and WHY. Open choices live in DISCUSSIONS.txt; the
+mechanics live in README.txt. An entry migrates here when it is settled,
+and its disc entry is deleted.
+
+
+D-1  COVERAGE IS A COMPONENT, NOT A SPREAD OF OPTIONS         (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   operations/DISCUSSIONS todo-22 places coverage as four small
+          additions: 'StoreConfig.record_coverage', an argv change in
+          the execute stage, a store sidecar, a rendering in the pack.
+          That is the shape 'record_timing' has -- and it fits timing,
+          because a delta is one float and no tool is involved.
+          Coverage involves a TOOL, and the tool is per LANGUAGE.
+DECISION  A peer component, 'coverage/', beside procsitter, compare and
+          hwut_pype. It owns three things and nothing else:
+              CONTRACT   CoverageConfig -- what is gathered
+              WRAPPING   the tool's own call form; THE one place a
+                         language's coverage tool is named
+              HARVEST    the tool's artifact -> the homogeneous record
+          Held VERBATIM in TestConfiguration (aggregation, not
+          restatement). The four seams above stay one line each.
+COST      One more component to carry: README, RATIONALE, DISCUSSIONS,
+          TEST/GOOD.
+GRAVEYARD Tool knowledge inside 'stage_execute.py': puts a tool
+          vocabulary ABOVE the TRANSLATION line (operations README 2.2),
+          which no component type may cross.
+
+
+D-2  THE COMPONENT CHOOSES THE TOOL; THE CONF NAMES IT        (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   'gcov', 'lcov' and 'gcovr' are one language and three output
+          shapes. Does a configuration entry name a tool, a reader, or
+          both?
+DECISION  'hwut.conf' carries a dict whose KEY is a GLOB over the
+          LANGUAGE parameter and whose VALUE is an ORDERED LIST OF
+          CANDIDATE TOOLS. The component takes the first candidate that
+          is actually available on this machine, and resolves tool ->
+          reader from its own registry. A configuration never names a
+          reader.
+
+              "python*"   : ["coverage", "slipcover", "trace"]
+              "c"         : ["gcov", "llvm-cov", "kcov"]
+              "verilog"   : ["verilator_coverage", "vcover", "urg"]
+              "pascal"    : []          <- an EMPTY list is an ANSWER
+
+          THE LANGUAGE IS THE KEY, not the interpreter: it is the one
+          thing all three source kinds have. An EXECUTABLE and a COMPILED
+          test have no interpreter to match on, and 'python3' vs 'pypy3'
+          is one language under two names.
+          WHERE THE LANGUAGE IS NOT STATED it is DERIVED from the source
+          file's extension. The derivation is stated, never silent: the
+          language that served appears in the record's header (D-7) and
+          in any refusal, so an author never wonders what was assumed.
+          A default dict ships with the component; 'hwut.conf' overrides
+          it, inherited global to specific by the existing rule.
+          The services gain '--global-conf [<file>]'. Given no file, the
+          search runs UPWARD: the nearest ENCLOSING 'hwut.conf' wins,
+          layered over whatever stands further out.
+          NO CANDIDATE AVAILABLE is a REFUSAL at the door, naming the
+          candidates it looked for -- never a silent skip (a skipped
+          measurement reads as an absent one, and absence and emptiness
+          do not collapse).
+          THE ORDER IS PART OF THE TABLE: the shipped list puts the tools
+          whose FORMAT this build reads in FRONT, because 'elect' takes
+          the first candidate the machine HAS. A candidate with no reader
+          is still worth listing -- it is how a machine refuses BY NAME.
+          AN EMPTY LIST IS AN ANSWER, not an omission: where nobody can
+          vouch for a tool (Pascal, Tcl), the language refuses by name.
+          Inventing a candidate would be worse -- a tool that is wrong
+          about what it measures reports a green nobody earned.
+COST      A new tool needs a registry entry, not merely a conf line.
+          Which candidate served is not knowable from the configuration
+          alone -- hence D-7.
+GRAVEYARD Conf entries naming tool AND reader: two truths, and the second
+          one is the component's own business.
+          Inferring a tool from the source kind: a default that fails
+          silently, in the green direction (operations README 2.6).
+          A single tool per language: a machine without it has no
+          coverage at all, where a second candidate would have served.
+          Keying on the INTERPRETER: two of the three source kinds have
+          none, and one language would answer to several spellings.
+
+
+D-3  THE GATHER SET IS TWO GLOB LISTS, FOR EFFICIENCY ONLY    (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   todo-22's open question: coverage of WHAT -- the test
+          application only, or the units it exercises?
+DECISION  'CoverageConfig' carries two glob lists: the sources SUBJECT to
+          coverage, and those that are NOT. They exist to keep the
+          GATHERING cheap and for nothing else. What is displayed,
+          recorded or further processed is a LATER STAGE'S filter.
+COST      Two filters in two places; each must say which it is.
+GRAVEYARD One filter serving both purposes: the gathering set and the
+          reporting set are different questions, and welding them makes
+          "why is this file missing from the report?" unanswerable.
+
+
+D-4  COVERAGE IS ITS OWN ANIMAL                               (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A coverage run is a test run -- but slower, fatter on disk, and
+          measuring something the ordinary run does not.
+DECISION  It is a DIFFERENT kind of run, and says so:
+            -- individual caps, or ALL of them, may be DISABLED for it.
+               Declared, never inferred.
+            -- a coverage run produces NO timing measures.
+               'record_coverage' and 'record_timing' are mutually
+               exclusive.
+            -- the raw, language-specific artifact lands in
+               'OUT/COVERAGE/'; the reader converts it from there.
+            -- source references are RELATIVE TO THE TEST DIRECTORY, so
+               a later stage can aggregate across directories.
+COST      Two run kinds to keep honest; a suite measuring coverage cannot
+          also be measuring cadence.
+GRAVEYARD Silently relaxing caps under 'record_coverage': a cap that
+          disappears without being said is the green-direction failure.
+          Absolute source paths: they freeze one machine into the record
+          and make aggregation impossible.
+
+
+D-5  THE HOMOGENEOUS RECORD: LCOV'S SKELETON, NOT ITS GRAIN   (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Every coverage format on the market records ONE LINE OF TEXT
+          PER SOURCE LINE ('DA:2100,1'). That is where LCOV, Cobertura
+          and coverage.py's JSON all become slow and fat, and it is the
+          disruption to avoid.
+DECISION  Take LCOV's SKELETON -- keyed by source file, merge is addition
+          -- and drop its granularity. Per source file, two sorted
+          INTERVAL lists:
+              EX   the ranges that could be hit
+              CV   the ranges that were
+          'uncovered = EX - CV'; percentage is derived. Neither stored.
+          The ranges are DELTA CODED: each is (start - previous_end,
+          length), so both numbers stay small.
+          HIT COUNTS are OPTIONAL and OFF by default; the header declares
+          whether they are recorded, so a reader never guesses.
+COST      A file whose coverage is genuinely scattered line-by-line
+          compresses less well than one with runs.
+MEASURED  (expected, to be confirmed -- DISCUSSIONS disc-1) a 5000-line
+          file collapses from 5000 records to a handful of ranges.
+GRAVEYARD Per-line records: the very cost this format exists to avoid.
+          Counts always on: they are what prevents the interval collapse,
+          and HWUT asks "did this test reach this code", not "how often".
+
+
+D-6  A CONVERTER MAKES THE STORAGE FORMAT PRIVATE             (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   LCOV is the lingua franca: 'genhtml', CI dashboards, codecov
+          and IDE gutters read it and will never learn ours.
+DECISION  'hwut.convert_to_lcov' -- a service that emits LCOV from the
+          homogeneous record. It is the reader registry run BACKWARDS:
+          readers map tool format -> ours, this maps ours -> LCOV.
+COST      One more service face.
+CONSEQUENCE, and the reason this is settled before the format is: with a
+          converter between the store and the outside world, the internal
+          format is PRIVATE and REVERSIBLE. Text first, measure, go
+          binary later -- and the service does not change. So the format
+          question need not be answered now, and answering it now would
+          be answering it without numbers.
+GRAVEYARD Exposing the internal record as the export format: it would
+          then be frozen by every consumer that ever read it.
+
+
+D-7  THE RECORD NAMES THE TOOL AND FORMAT THAT MADE IT         (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   With a CANDIDATE LIST (D-2), which tool served is decided at
+          RUN TIME, by what the machine happens to have. The
+          configuration cannot answer it, and the homogeneous record --
+          being homogeneous -- looks the same whichever tool produced it.
+          A later stage that must know is then guessing.
+DECISION  The record's HEADER carries the PROVENANCE: the LANGUAGE that
+          selected the candidates (derived or stated, D-2), the TOOL that
+          ran, and the FORMAT its artifact was in. Beside 'counts:
+          no|yes' and the format version, so one header answers
+          everything a reader needs before the first range.
+          SAME LAW AS THE BOOK ENTRY (operations README 6): a record is
+          HISTORY, and the configuration may have moved since. The book
+          records the canonicaliser and the compare setup for exactly
+          this reason; coverage records its tool for exactly this reason.
+COST      A record is no longer comparable byte-for-byte across machines
+          that resolved different candidates -- which is TRUE, and better
+          said than hidden.
+CONSEQUENCE An aggregate over records made by DIFFERENT tools is
+          admissible but no longer uniform, and the aggregator can now
+          SEE that. What it does about it -- merge, segregate, or refuse
+          -- is its own ruling, and it can only be taken because the
+          provenance is there.
+GRAVEYARD Provenance inferred from the configuration: with candidates it
+          is not derivable, and a derivation that is usually right is the
+          worst kind.
+          Provenance as a machine tag (host, version, path): the record
+          stays MACHINE-FREE (D-4). The tool's NAME is not a machine.
+
+
+D-8  WHO COVERED IT: A DIFFERENT FOLD, NOT A RICHER MERGE      (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   The aggregate must later answer WHICH RUN reached a line, so
+          that a change to code can conclude WHICH TESTS TO PERFORM.
+          'merge' cannot: a union of ranges is LOSSY BY CONSTRUCTION and
+          destroys who contributed which line. The obvious repair --
+          attribution inside the merged record -- forces every range to
+          split wherever authorship differs, which is the per-line grain
+          D-5 exists to avoid.
+DECISION  TWO QUESTIONS, TWO FOLDS, ONE SET OF RECORDS.
+              'record.merge'   what did the suite reach   (union)
+              'index.index_of' who reached this line      (segmentation)
+          The index cuts the line axis at every point where the SET OF
+          ORIGINS changes, and fuses segments carrying equal sets -- so a
+          file one run reaches whole costs ONE segment, not one entry per
+          line. A query is a bisect.
+          THE ATTRIBUTION WAS NEVER A FIELD TO ADD: it is the key the
+          record is already stored under, (test, choice). What was needed
+          is only that a record CARRY that key when it travels away from
+          the store -- so the header names 'test' and 'choice' beside the
+          provenance of D-7. 'choice' is '-' for the choice-less test, as
+          the runner's own DOWN grammar already spells it.
+CONSEQUENCE, and it is a RULE: THE PER-RUN RECORDS MUST BE KEPT. An
+          aggregate that replaces them answers the first question and
+          destroys the second, irreversibly.
+          The directory that disambiguates two 'core.py' is supplied by
+          the AGGREGATOR, not by the record (D-4) -- which makes disc-4's
+          recommendation load-bearing rather than tidy.
+COST      Storage is the sum of the runs, not the union of them.
+GRAVEYARD Per-range attribution inside the merged record: reinstates the
+          per-line grain by another road.
+          Deriving the run from the PATH a record was found at: the
+          fragility D-7 removed for the tool, reintroduced for the key.
+
+THE LIMIT, STATED ONCE AND REPEATED BY EVERY FACE OVER IT. The index
+          names what CERTAINLY executed a line. It never claims the rest
+          is unaffected: a test may depend on code it never executed -- a
+          branch that was deleted, a data file, a dynamic dispatch, a
+          configuration, an ABSENCE. Selecting only the named tests and
+          calling the suite green is a FALSE GREEN, the silent failure of
+          PHILOSOPHY section 7. A suggestion, never a clearance.
+
+
+D-9  A SEGMENT CARRIES A NUMBER: TEST IDS AND GROUP IDS        (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A segmentation carrying Origins carries the same test NAME
+          thousands of times, and a RENAME would have to rewrite every
+          record that ever mentioned it.
+DECISION  TWO INTERNINGS, in 'identity.py':
+              IdTable      Origin          <-> TEST ID
+              GroupTable   set of TEST IDs <-> GROUP ID
+          A segment carries ONE INTEGER -- its group. A query reads the
+          group, the GroupTable decodes it to ids, the IdTable decodes
+          those to runs: AT THE EDGE, for the few segments a query
+          touched, never for the whole fold.
+          GROUPS, not sets, because whole regions of a code base are
+          reached by exactly the same handful of tests: pay for the
+          DISTINCT set, not for every occurrence -- the same trick the
+          intervals are.
+          GROUP 0 IS THE EMPTY SET, allocated by construction. A stretch
+          nobody executed carries a group like any other, so no query
+          needs a special case for 'nobody'.
+
+          THE TWO LAWS OF A TEST ID
+          (1) AN ID IS NEVER REUSED. Allocation is monotone; a retired id
+              KEEPS ITS ENTRY so an old record still decodes, while the
+              forward lookup stops finding it. Reuse would make an old
+              record point silently at a DIFFERENT test -- a false
+              attribution, and one that reports nothing.
+          (2) A RENAME KEEPS THE ID. The name is an attribute of the
+              entry, never the identity. THIS IS THE WHOLE POINT: a
+              rename touches ONE table, and no record anywhere.
+
+          A rename onto a name a LIVE id already holds is REFUSED: two
+          live ids for one run makes 'which id is this test' unanswerable.
+COST      A second table to carry, and a second thing that can be lost.
+          A record without its id table is names without numbers -- which
+          is why the record itself still carries 'test' and 'choice'
+          (D-8): the tables ACCELERATE the index, they are not the only
+          copy of the truth.
+GRAVEYARD Names in every segment: a rename becomes a rewrite of history.
+          Reusing a retired id: the false attribution above.
+          Answering an unknown group with the empty set: it would read as
+          'nobody ran this' -- absence and emptiness, collapsed, in the
+          green direction.
+
+THE BOOKKEEPER. The table is THE BOOKKEEPER'S, eventually: it already
+          owns the naming of a test directory, and a RENAME SERVICE must
+          go through the same door or there are two truths about what a
+          test is called. 'identity.py' holds the MECHANISM and a
+          serialisation and deliberately reaches into no base. Which side
+          allocates, at what scope, and what a rename service owes, is
+          DISCUSSIONS disc-8 -- and settling it EDITS THE BOOKKEEPER, so
+          it waits for a quiet tree.
+
+
+D-10  A READER NAMES A SECOND CALL; IT NEVER MAKES ONE          (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Found while building the readers, and not foreseen: most
+          coverage tools do not leave a REPORT, they leave BINARY STATE.
+          coverage.py leaves a '.coverage' database; gcc leaves '.gcda'
+          counters. Turning either into something readable is itself a
+          PROCESS -- and every process HWUT runs goes through the
+          procsitter. A reader that spawned it would be a component
+          spawning subprocesses behind the execute stage's back.
+DECISION  The role grows a THIRD call, 'report_argv(config, work_dir)':
+          the reader NAMES the second supervised call, the execute stage
+          MAKES it, under the procsitter like every other process. None
+          says, honestly, that this tool needs no second call.
+
+              coverage    'coverage json'   -- a database to read
+              gcov        'gcov -b -p ...'  -- counters to annotate
+              lcov &c.    None              -- a tracefile is text
+
+          MADE LATE. gcov's call names the '.gcda' files the run just
+          wrote, which do not exist before it. 'report_argv' is called
+          after the application ended -- which is when the execute stage
+          would make it anyway -- and returns None where no '.gcda'
+          stands: that says 'the build was not instrumented' rather than
+          running gcov over nothing and reporting a failure with a
+          misleading name.
+COST      Three calls in the role rather than two, and one more thing
+          the execute stage does under 'record_coverage'.
+GRAVEYARD A reader that runs its own subprocess: unsupervised, uncapped,
+          unattributed -- the one thing the procsitter exists to
+          prevent (procsitter MANUAL, rule of thumb 1).
+          Harvesting the binary state directly by importing the tool's
+          library: it would make the component depend on every coverage
+          tool it supports, and 'gcov' has no library at all.
+
+ALSO SETTLED HERE, and small: '-p' is not decoration. Without it two
+          'core.c' in two directories both become 'core.c.gcov' and the
+          second silently REPLACES the first -- a whole file's coverage
+          lost, in the green direction.
+
+
+D-11  A MEASURE IS REGISTERED, NOT BUILT IN                     (2026-08-22)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Line coverage is one measurement among several. Branch,
+          condition and MC/DC each answer a DIFFERENT question about the
+          same source, and none of them is a flag on a line: they belong
+          to a DECISION POINT. todo-8 said 'a third interval list'; that
+          was wrong -- a decision is not a range, and 'a && b' is one
+          line with several of them.
+DECISION  'measure.py': a MEASURE owns a NAME, a record TAG, its own
+          encoding, and the answer to whether it can be merged. The
+          record dispatches on the tag and asks the measure; it knows
+          what none of them MEAN. Admitting a fourth is one 'register'
+          call and NO change to 'record.py'.
+
+              EX:3+3,1        line, executable      record.py's own
+              CV:3+3          line, covered         record.py's own
+              BR:2*1/2        branch                registered
+              MC:4*2/3,0*3/3  mc/dc                 registered
+
+          THE POINT SHAPE, shared by both built-ins: (line, covered,
+          total), delta coded on the line as the ranges are. A delta of
+          ZERO means ANOTHER DECISION ON THE SAME LINE -- which MC/DC
+          admits and branch does not, because branch data is reported per
+          line and MC/DC per decision.
+          A FILE WITH NO SUCH MEASUREMENT WRITES NO SUCH LINE, so a
+          record of line coverage alone is BYTE-IDENTICAL to what it was
+          before any measure existed. No GOOD moved.
+COST      Two registries in one component (readers, measures). They are
+          different things -- a reader knows a FORMAT, a measure knows a
+          QUESTION -- and one table for both would serve neither.
+
+WHY NEITHER CAN BE MERGED, and why that is refused rather than fudged. A
+          COUNT of arms taken does not carry WHICH arms. Run A takes arm
+          0, run B takes arm 1: together the decision is fully covered,
+          and no function of 1 and 1 yields 2.
+              max(1, 1) = 1   a LOWER BOUND reported as a measurement --
+                              a false RED, and a false GREEN the moment
+                              somebody 'fixes' it by summing
+          So a measure DECLARES 'mergeable', both declare False, and
+          'record.merge' refuses by name ('MeasureNotMergeable'). An
+          encoding carrying the SET of arms taken rather than their
+          number WOULD be mergeable and could declare so; that is the
+          shape to reach for if an aggregate over branch data is ever
+          wanted.
+
+MC/DC IS REGISTERED; NO READER PRODUCES IT YET, and that is stated rather
+          than hidden. GCC 14 gained '-fcondition-coverage' and 'gcov
+          --conditions'; the machine this was written on carries gcc 13,
+          so the artifact could not be SEEN. The ENCODING here is this
+          component's own and is tested; READING somebody else's is owed,
+          and must be written against a real artifact like every other
+          reader (DISCUSSIONS todo-8).
+
+GRAVEYARD A third interval list for branches: a decision is not a range,
+          and several sit on one line.
+          A flag on the line record: it would say 'this line has a
+          branch' and not how much of it was taken -- the whole
+          measurement, discarded.
+          Measures hard-coded in 'record.py': every new question would
+          then edit the format, and disc-9's HDL measures would edit it
+          five more times.
+
+WHAT THIS DELIBERATELY DOES NOT SOLVE. A measure with NO LINE cannot
+          live here at all: toggle coverage belongs to a SIGNAL, a
+          functional bin to a COVERGROUP, and this record is keyed by
+          file and line. disc-9 stands unchanged, and this registration
+          is no help with it -- pretending otherwise is how a design gets
+          reported '92% covered' while the coverage somebody came for is
+          discarded.
+
+
+D-12  A NAMED POINT MERGES WHERE A DIGEST CANNOT               (2026-08-24)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+SUPERSEDES IN PART D-11's closing paragraph ('a measure with NO LINE
+          cannot live here at all') and disc-9's 'NO LINE' column. Both
+          were sound on what they knew; the correction is EVIDENCE, not
+          argument, and the evidence is in WITNESS-hdl-artifacts.txt.
+PROBLEM   D-11 refused merge on 'branch' because (covered, total) does
+          not carry WHICH arms, and concluded that measures without a
+          line -- toggle, functional cover -- could not live in this
+          record. The artifacts say both halves were too broad. Every
+          point verilator emits carries a FILE and a LINE: toggle points
+          at the signal's DECLARATION line, branch ARMS as separate
+          named points, cover properties at their statement. GHDL's PSL
+          report names file, line and counts per directive. And every
+          one of them is NAMED -- 'verilator_coverage' merges its own
+          '.dat' files by addition, which is only possible because the
+          identity survives.
+DECISION  'NamedPointMeasure': a measure recorded per
+          (line, name, covered, total), the name carried in the record.
+          Because identity survives, two records UNION honestly, and the
+          measure declares 'mergeable = True' -- the first that does.
+          Two ride on it today, both from witnessed artifacts:
+
+              TG   toggle    a signal's bit, at its declaration line
+              CP   cover     a 'cover property' / PSL cover directive
+
+          UNMERGEABILITY WAS A PROPERTY OF THE DIGEST, NOT OF THE
+          MEASUREMENT. That is the whole of the correction, and it is
+          worth stating plainly because the original reasoning reads
+          like a statement about branch coverage and is in fact a
+          statement about the encoding chosen for it.
+COST      A third point shape in 'measure.py' beside 'PointMeasure', and
+          a record line that carries names -- so a named-point record is
+          wider than a digest one. Paid where the axis is asked for and
+          nowhere else: a file with no such measurement writes no such
+          line, exactly as before.
+GRAVEYARD Seating toggle points on a synthetic line: it would put a
+          measurement at a position no source holds, and every renderer
+          downstream would show it as a line fact.
+          Keeping the anonymous digest for toggle 'for consistency':
+          consistency with a shape that was already known to discard the
+          answer.
+
+WHAT REMAINS LINE-LESS REMAINS OUT, and the UCIS reader has now made the
+          gap STRUCTURAL rather than incidental. FSM states, assertion
+          bins and covergroup bins are line-less BY THE UCIS XSD ITSELF
+          -- not by the absence of an open-source emitter. disc-9's
+          option (b) stands, awaiting a real artifact like every reader
+          here. Its mandatory statement shrinks to 'FSM and covergroup
+          coverage are not measured here'.
+
+
+D-13  THE TOOL/FORMAT TABLES ARE GENERATED, NOT WRITTEN         (2026-08-24)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   One fact -- which tool speaks which format, and which of them
+          this build reads -- was written out at FIVE sites: the
+          'readers/__init__.py' docstring, the '[r]' markers in
+          'registry.py', README section 5, OVERVIEW's format table and
+          DISCUSSIONS todo-2. On the day this was written, THREE of the
+          five were already false: two said 'seven' where eleven stood,
+          and README named 'kcov' an alias of the tracefile after the
+          witness had moved it to cobertura AND the code had shipped the
+          move. The code was right at every point. Prose cannot be kept
+          true by discipline at five sites; it can only be kept true by
+          not being written five times.
+DECISION  The table has ONE author, and it is the registry. 'hwut.cov
+          formats' prints tool, format, language reach and whether this
+          build reads it, from 'registered_tuple()' and each reader's
+          own 'name' and 'source_format'. Its HWUT GOOD file IS the
+          table, so a reader admitted without its documentation updated
+          turns a test RED rather than leaving a document quietly wrong.
+          Every prose site carries a POINTER, never a copy.
+
+          THE DOCUMENTS KEEP WHAT THE REGISTRY CANNOT HOLD: todo-2's
+          ledger says what was built and WHEN and against WHICH witness;
+          OVERVIEW says which roads were walked and what each artifact
+          overturned. Those are history and do not rot. What rots is the
+          restatement of a table, and only that is withdrawn.
+COST      A prose reader must run a command -- or read a GOOD file -- to
+          see the table. The GOOD file is in the tree and is plain text,
+          so the cost is one path.
+          The corrections of 2026-08-24 are still made BY HAND here, one
+          pass, because 'hwut.cov' does not exist yet. That is accepted
+          rather than deferred: a document that states the disc-9
+          amendment while contradicting it three tables later fails its
+          own Defence Test.
+GRAVEYARD A tree-wide convention that the tables be updated together:
+          that convention was already in force and produced the three
+          falsehoods above.
+          Marking the tables stale and waiting for 'hwut.cov': it leaves
+          a repository asserting something untrue about kcov for the
+          length of two tasks.
+
+
+D-14  IDENTITY IS DIRECTORY-LOCAL; THE GATHER QUALIFIES            (2026-08-24)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+SUPERSEDES IN PART D-9's Origin shape, and SETTLES disc-8's second
+          fork (the scope of an id). disc-8's first fork -- who OWNS the
+          table -- stands open exactly as before.
+PROBLEM   Origin was '(directory, test, choice)', the directory relative
+          to wherever the aggregator stood. 'hwut.run' from the tree
+          root and 'hwut.cov' from a subdirectory would therefore
+          allocate DIFFERENT ids for the SAME run: an identity that
+          varies with where one stood when asking is not an identity.
+          Absolute paths are barred (D-4), environment variables are
+          barred by house doctrine, and disc-8's own repair --
+          partitioned id ranges per directory -- needs the very
+          coordination it was meant to avoid.
+DECISION  TWO KEYS, TWO LIFETIMES.
+
+              Origin    (test, choice)         PERSISTENT, per directory
+              Gathered  (found-dir, Origin)    EPHEMERAL, per gather
+
+          An Origin is unique inside one test directory by the
+          FILESYSTEM'S OWN GUARANTEE -- no allocation, no ranges, no
+          registry above the directories. It does not vary with the
+          invocation root, and a directory that MOVES touches no id:
+          the strongest form of the rename law, for free.
+          A gather across directories qualifies AT GATHER TIME: the
+          found-directory, relative to the gather root the caller
+          chose, beside the Origin. 'Gathered' lives exactly as long
+          as the aggregation; 'IdTable.format' REFUSES a table holding
+          one, because storing it would freeze one invocation's view
+          of the tree as if it were identity.
+          THE GATHER IS CANONICAL OR THE IDS ARE NOT REPRODUCIBLE:
+          records enter the fold sorted by found-directory then record
+          name, so two gathers over one tree allocate identically. The
+          walker sorts; 'index_of' trusts its caller.
+          THE SERIALISATION MOVES to '##VUT-TEST-IDS 2' with
+          'T:<id> <flag> <test>|<choice>'. Version 1's directory column
+          was a field whose only legal persisted value would have been
+          'empty' -- a spelling for a fact that cannot occur -- and no
+          table was ever persisted anywhere in the tree, so this was
+          the last cheap moment to cut it. The parser refuses version 1
+          BY NAME, saying what changed and what to do.
+COST      Three identity GOODs moved ('allocation', 'faults', 'tables')
+          -- an intended structural change, audited line by line: the
+          version bump, the two-part line, and the retired entry
+          decoding without a directory. 47 of 50 stood byte-exact,
+          because 'Gathered' spells 'directory:test--choice' precisely
+          as the old three-field Origin did.
+          'rename' loses its 'directory' arm: there is nothing of the
+          kind left to rename.
+GRAVEYARD Absolute directories: name a machine (D-4's whole point).
+          Directories relative to the invocation root: the defect
+          itself.
+          Partitioned id ranges per directory (disc-8's old (a)):
+          somebody must hand out the ranges, which is the external
+          coordination being removed.
+          A 'directory' field ruled always-None in persisted tables:
+          a vestigial column, and a parser accepting a field the law
+          forbids.
+
+
+D-15  THE REGISTER NUMBERS; THIS COMPONENT GROUPS               (2026-08-25)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+SUPERSEDES D-9's first interning and the whole of D-14's Origin, which
+          the orchestrator's D-7 replaced. D-14's DIR-LOCALITY and its
+          ephemeral gather qualification stand, and are the reason this
+          fits at all.
+PROBLEM   This component interned TWICE: a name became a test id, and a
+          set of test ids became a group. The first interning existed
+          because a segment carrying test NAMES would carry them
+          thousands of times. The register (orchestrator D-7) now
+          issues those numbers itself, at accept, per directory, and
+          keeps them through a rename. Interning them again here would
+          be a SECOND numbering of the same thing -- two id spaces, two
+          truths, and a decode that could disagree.
+DECISION  ONE INTERNING REMAINS: 'GroupTable', set of run keys -> group
+          id. 'IdTable', 'Origin', 'Entry' and 'parse_id_table' are
+          GONE from this component.
+          THE VALUE TYPE 'TestRunId' STANDS HERE, in the leaf, and the
+          register IMPORTS it: coverage imports nothing outward, and a
+          pair of integers has no business holding a file open. The
+          register owns allocation, the file and the names; this owns
+          the shape. Reversing that placement is two import lines.
+          'index_of' folds over whatever run keys it is GIVEN -- ids
+          for one directory, 'Gathered' for a gather -- and numbers no
+          test itself. 'affected' resolves names to ids through an
+          INJECTABLE seam ('resolve'), whose default numbers within one
+          gather, by the register's own rule and in its own shape, and
+          says at its definition which kind of number it is. A face
+          above hands in the real register and the NUMBERS change,
+          nothing else.
+          THE GROUP TABLE MOVES TO VERSION 2: a group holds RUN IDS,
+          spelled '47' / '47.66'. A GATHERED key offered for storage is
+          REFUSED by 'format' -- it belongs to one aggregation and
+          storing it would freeze that view as identity.
+COST      Three identity choices (allocation, rename, retire) LEFT this
+          component with the mechanism they tested; they stand in the
+          register's own test. Twelve GOODs moved, every movement an
+          id where a name stood -- audited, re-recorded.
+          A record still carries NAMES in its header; the resolve seam
+          is the bridge until the record format names run ids (todo-9).
+GRAVEYARD Coverage keeping its own IdTable and mapping register ids
+          onto it: two id spaces for one fact.
+          Coverage importing the register: the leaf would depend on
+          the orchestrator, and 'hwut.affected' would need a bookkeeper
+          to read a directory it does not administer.
+
+
+D-16  THE RUN SHAPE IS THE BOOKKEEPER'S                         (2026-08-25)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+CORRECTS D-15, which placed 'TestRunId' in this component.
+PROBLEM   D-15 put the shape of a test run here because coverage is a
+          leaf and imports nothing outward. That reasoning was about
+          LAYERING and said something false about MEANING: a test run
+          is not a coverage concept. The runner performs one, the base
+          records one, a report names one; coverage is one consumer
+          among several.
+DECISION  'TestRunId' and 'run_id_of_text' stand in the BOOKKEEPER,
+          which is a component of its own since bookkeeper B-1. This
+          component IMPORTS them, downward, like every other consumer.
+          WHAT REMAINS THIS COMPONENT'S: 'Gathered' -- how an
+          aggregator qualifies run ids across directories, at gather
+          time, never stored -- and the GROUP interning. Both are
+          questions only an aggregator asks.
+          'IdentityFault' is now a KIND of the bookkeeper's
+          'RunIdFault', so a caller catching the general one catches a
+          bad group too.
+COST      Two GOODs moved, both naming the refusing layer.
+GRAVEYARD The leaf-purity argument of D-15: it would have made every
+          future consumer of a run id import COVERAGE to name one.
+
+
+D-17  IDENTITY.PY DISSOLVED; IDS COUNT FROM 0 AND ARE ISSUED ONCE   (2026-08-25)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+CORRECTS  D-15 and D-16 in what they left here: 'the group interning'.
+PROBLEM   D-16 moved the run's shape to the bookkeeper because a run is
+          not a coverage concept. The same argument holds for a SET of
+          runs, and 'identity.py' -- a group table plus one value type
+          -- was the last file whose name promised an identity this
+          component does not own.
+          Separately, the register's id law changed (bookkeeper B-2):
+          issued once, from 0, never re-used. Every GOOD here that
+          spelled '1.1' spelled an id the register no longer issues
+          first.
+DECISION  'identity.py' is GONE. 'GroupTable' and its file format are
+          the bookkeeper's ('group_table.py', B-3), with 'GroupDb'
+          persisting per directory; 'Gathered' stands in 'index.py',
+          the one module that folds over it; 'IdentityFault' is the
+          bookkeeper's 'GroupFault'. 'index_of' takes the bookkeeper's
+          table, so a one-directory fold keeps its group ids across
+          builds and a gather makes an ephemeral one.
+          '_local_resolver' in 'affected.py' numbers from 0 in the
+          register's own rule, as before in the register's own shape.
+          The cross-directory group of groups a gather may need is
+          todo-10, ephemeral to hwut by ruling.
+COST      'test-identity.py' and four GOODs left; 'keys' joined
+          'test-index.py'. Twelve GOODs re-recorded for 0-based ids,
+          each movement audited to be an id and nothing else.
+GRAVEYARD Keeping 'identity.py' as a re-export of the bookkeeper's
+          names: a file that says 'coverage has an identity' and holds
+          none.
+
+
+D-18  A RECORD NAMES RUN IDS, AND NAMES A SET OF THEM          (2026-08-25)
+------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+COMPLETES D-8, which put the run in the header as (test, choice) NAMES
+          because ids could not be persisted then. Orchestrator todo-4
+          t-9.
+PROBLEM   Names in the header make every rename rewrite every record of
+          that test -- 'hwut.rename' would have to walk and edit records
+          it otherwise only moves. Ids could not be used while the
+          register re-issued them (a record naming run 47, kept across a
+          removal and a later accept, would attribute its lines to a
+          test that never ran them). Bookkeeper B-2 removed that: an id
+          is issued once.
+          Separately, 'merge' had to say WHOSE the aggregate was, and
+          did it by joining name strings -- 'test: a,b' / 'choice:
+          basic,deep' -- which spells a CROSS of names, not the pairs
+          that actually ran.
+DECISION  FORMAT VERSION 2. One header line replaces two:
+
+              ##run:      47.66      one run
+              ##run:      -          NO run: fresh from a reader
+              ##run:      0.0,0.1,3  a MERGED record: the set
+
+          'CoverageRecord.run' is a frozenset of 'TestRunId'; 'merge'
+          UNIONS it, so a merged record names every run that made it and
+          the cross disappears. The spelling is the group table's own
+          spelling for a set, so a merged record's 'run' line reads as a
+          group-table line does.
+          THE SET, NOT A GROUP ID: a group id would be one integer, but
+          a merged record could then not be read without the
+          directory's group table, and a record that TRAVELLED would be
+          mute. Bytes are paid only by merged records, which are
+          aggregates and few.
+          'seated(record, run)' is the ONE SEAM between a reader (which
+          knows the artifact) and the caller that knows the run.
+          Version 1 is refused by name.
+          THE RESOLVE SEAM IS GONE. 'record_iterable' no longer takes a
+          'resolve'; '_local_resolver' is deleted. A record carries its
+          ids, a gather qualifies them into 'Gathered', and only the
+          EDGE that prints an answer needs the register. A MERGED record
+          is yielded once per run it names; a record naming NO run is
+          skipped and said on stderr -- attributing it to a guess is
+          worse than losing it.
+COST      Version 1 records do not read; none exist outside GOODs.
+          Thirty-two GOODs re-recorded (readers, record, measure, index,
+          affected), every movement a header line.
+GRAVEYARD Keeping names beside the ids 'for readability': two truths,
+          and the rename problem back in full.
+          A group id in the header: a record that cannot be read alone.
+
