+"""SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PURPOSE: 'spawn' -- ONE SUPERVISED CALL, synchronously, in the shape
+         'subprocess.run' answers (E-28).
+
+Every test application and every pype runs under the procsitter; a
+test of the framework that runs a command of its own should get the
+same supervision, and above all the same ANSWER to a command that
+cannot be launched: a record that says so, not an exception out of the
+test. 'subprocess.run' raises 'PermissionError' for a she-bang whose
+interpreter lacks its execute bit and 'FileNotFoundError' for one that
+names nothing; here both are 'FAIL_LAUNCH', with 'returncode' None
+and the reason on 'stderr'.
+
+It lives beside the procsitter, not in the test-writing support: the
+support is SEALED (imports nothing of this tree), and a test that
+wants the supervisor asks the supervisor.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+"""
+class CSpawned:
+    """WHAT A SUPERVISED CALL ANSWERED, in the shape 'subprocess.run'
+    answers so that a test reads it the same way -- and one thing more:
+    a call that could not be LAUNCHED is an answer, not an exception.
+
+    'returncode'  the call's own exit code; None where the supervisor
+                  ended it or it never started
+    'stdout'      str
+    'stderr'      str; on a failed launch, the reason -- the command,
+                  and what the system said
+    'containment' the supervisor's word, 'E_Containment'
+    """
+    __slots__ = ("returncode", "stdout", "stderr", "containment")
+
+    def __init__(self, returncode, stdout, stderr, containment):
+        self.returncode  = returncode
+        self.stdout      = stdout
+        self.stderr      = stderr
+        self.containment = containment
+
+    def launched_f(self):
+        """RETURN: bool, True where the command started at all."""
+        from vut.engine.procsitter.procsitter import E_Containment
+        return self.containment is not E_Containment.FAIL_LAUNCH
+
+
+def spawn(argv, input=None, cwd=None, env=None, max_wall_clock_sec=60.0,
+          capture_output=True, text=True):
+    """
+    RETURN: CSpawned, the answer of running 'argv' UNDER THE PROCSITTER
+            -- the same supervision every test application and every
+            pype gets from the framework (E-27). A command that cannot
+            be launched -- not found, not executable, a she-bang that
+            names nothing runnable -- comes back with 'returncode' None
+            and the reason on 'stderr', never as a traceback out of the
+            test.
+
+    'input' is fed on stdin, closed after. 'capture_output' and 'text'
+    are accepted so that a 'subprocess.run' call site reads unchanged;
+    output is always captured, always text.
+    """
+    import asyncio, os
+    from vut.engine.procsitter.procsitter   import (Procsitter,
+                                                    ProcsitterConfig,
+                                                    E_Containment)
+    from vut.engine.procsitter.construction import Link
+
+    async def go():
+        out, err = [], []
+        async def take_out(data): out.append(data)
+        async def take_err(data): err.append(data)
+        source = Link()
+        if input is not None:
+            await source.feed(input.encode("utf-8") if isinstance(input, str)
+                              else input)
+        source.close()
+        config = ProcsitterConfig(max_wall_clock_sec=max_wall_clock_sec,
+                                  env=env)
+        record = await Procsitter(config, cwd or os.getcwd()).run(
+                     [str(a) for a in argv],
+                     stdout_handler=take_out, stderr_handler=take_err,
+                     stdin_reader=source.reader)
+        return record, b"".join(out), b"".join(err)
+
+    record, out, err = asyncio.run(go())
+    stdout = out.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+    stderr = err.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
+    if record.containment is E_Containment.FAIL_LAUNCH:
+        stderr = ("LAUNCH FAILED: %s -- not found, not executable, or a "
+                  "she-bang naming nothing runnable\n"
+                  % " ".join(str(a) for a in argv))
+    return CSpawned(record.exit_code, stdout, stderr, record.containment)
+

+"""SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+PURPOSE: THE RUN REPORT PROTOCOL -- what a producer of the run's event
+         stream and a consumer of it agree on.
+
+    vocabulary.py   the kinds of event, and the fields of each
+    receiver.py     the class a consumer derives from: the
+                    queue-draining loop and the wire validation
+    summary.py      'fold', the pure fold that answers what a run came
+                    to
+
+THE STREAM IS THE ONE CARRIER OF THE RUN'S TRUTH (O-4). Whoever wants
+the whole at the end folds it; whoever wants the events derives from
+the receiver. NEITHER IS THE ORCHESTRATOR'S PRIVATE BUSINESS -- both
+were written to be consumed from outside, and their own purposes say
+so: "any consumer may use it: our exit-status logic, a TUI, a customer
+application".
+
+WHY IT MOVED. Measured ('adm/import_graph.py --shared'), 'fold' is
+read by 'engine/display', 'services/run' and 'services/stability' --
+the lowest common ancestor of its readers is THE TREE ROOT. Held
+inside 'orchestrator/run', it made the one SIDEWAYS arrow in the whole
+tree: 'engine/display -> engine/orchestrator', a consumer reaching
+into a producer for the shape they share. A TUI, an HTML renderer or a
+customer's own consumer had to drag the orchestrator along to get
+three leaf modules.
+
+IT IMPORTS NOTHING OF THIS TREE, which is what makes it a protocol
+rather than a part of one party: every party sits above it, so no
+party can be made to wait on another. Declared 'SEALED' in
+'adm/LAYERING.txt', and the seal is checked.
+
+WHAT IS NOT HERE: the QUEUE, the scheduler, the dispatcher, the fold's
+callers. A protocol is the SHAPE two parties agree on; the transport
+and the machinery stay where they run.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+"""
+from .receiver   import CRunReportReceiver
+from .summary    import CRunSummary, fold
+from .vocabulary import KIND_DB
+
+__all__ = ["KIND_DB", "CRunReportReceiver", "CRunSummary", "fold"]

+"""SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+PURPOSE: THE RECEIVER -- the convenience class a consumer derives from
+         (O-5). It owns the queue-draining loop and the wire
+         validation; the user overrides the 'on_<kind>' methods he
+         cares about, with NAMED parameters, and the wire protocol
+         stays ours to change underneath.
+
+Every handler is a concrete NO-OP: a vocabulary that grows never
+breaks a standing receiver. Three catch-alls take '**fields':
+
+    on_any(kind, **fields)      every event, raw, before its handler
+    on_unknown(kind, **fields)  a kind the vocabulary does not carry
+    on_misfit(kind, **fields)   a KNOWN kind whose structure does not
+                                fit -- a required field missing or
+                                badly typed, or no dict at all
+
+A specific handler receives exactly the vocabulary's fields of its
+format -- required ones always, optional ones defaulting to 'None';
+fields a NEWER stream adds are dropped before the call, which is how
+named parameters survive growth.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+"""
+from .vocabulary import KIND_DB
+
+
+class CRunReportReceiver:
+    """Derive, override what you care about, hand 'receive' the
+    queue."""
+
+    async def receive(self, queue):
+        """
+        RETURN: None. Reads the queue to its closing 'None', validates
+                every event against the vocabulary, and dispatches:
+                'on_any' first, then the event's own handler --
+                'on_unknown' or 'on_misfit' where it has none or does
+                not fit.
+        """
+        while True:
+            item = await queue.get()
+            if item is None: return
+            self._dispatch(item)
+
+    def _dispatch(self, item):
+        """
+        RETURN: None. One event routed (see 'receive').
+        """
+        if not isinstance(item, dict) or "kind" not in item:
+            self.on_misfit("?", raw=item)
+            return
+        field_db = {name: value for name, value in item.items()
+                    if name not in ("kind", "format")}
+        kind = item["kind"]
+        self.on_any(kind, **field_db)
+
+        entry = KIND_DB.get(kind)
+        if entry is None:
+            self.on_unknown(kind, **field_db)
+            return
+        required_db, optional_db = entry
+        for name, field_type in required_db.items():
+            if name not in field_db \
+               or not isinstance(field_db[name], field_type):
+                self.on_misfit(kind, **field_db)
+                return
+        if "when" not in field_db:
+            self.on_misfit(kind, **field_db)
+            return
+
+        handler  = getattr(self, "on_%s" % kind.replace("-", "_"))
+        argument_db = {"when": field_db["when"]}
+        argument_db.update({name: field_db[name]
+                            for name in required_db})
+        argument_db.update({name: field_db.get(name)
+                            for name in optional_db})
+        handler(**argument_db)
+
+    # -- the catch-alls, '**fields' ------------------------------------
+    def on_any(self, kind, **fields):
+        """RETURN: None. Every event, raw, before its handler -- the
+        tap for logging or relaying."""
+
+    def on_unknown(self, kind, **fields):
+        """RETURN: None. A kind this vocabulary does not carry -- a
+        NEWER stream at an OLDER receiver."""
+
+    def on_misfit(self, kind, **fields):
+        """RETURN: None. A known kind whose structure does not fit the
+        vocabulary: a required field missing or badly typed, or no
+        dict at all (then 'kind' is '?' and 'raw' carries the item)."""
+
+    # -- one handler per kind, NAMED parameters, concrete no-ops -------
+    def on_tree_begun(self, when, directory_list):
+        """RETURN: None. The run begins; the test directories in walk
+        order."""
+
+    def on_dir_begun(self, when, directory, node_n):
+        """RETURN: None. One directory's run begins."""
+
+    def on_frame(self, when, directory, role, good):
+        """RETURN: None. 'on_entry' or 'on_exit' ran."""
+
+    def on_run_begun(self, when, directory, node, node_kind):
+        """RETURN: None. One node's work was dispatched."""
+
+    def on_run_ended(self, when, directory, node, node_kind, good,
+                     verdict, cause=None, report=None, detail=None):
+        """RETURN: None. One node's work ended; 'verdict' says WHY
+        coarsely, 'report' is the operation's own finer word where one
+        is known, 'detail' the report's numbers where it has them
+        (O-19), and 'cause' names the node whose breaking failed this
+        one, where one did."""
+
+    def on_fault(self, when, directory, text):
+        """RETURN: None. A fault of exploration or the walk."""
+
+    def on_report(self, when, directory, text):
+        """RETURN: None. A report of determination -- e.g. an empty
+        selection."""
+
+    def on_dir_done(self, when, directory, good, fail_db):
+        """RETURN: None. One directory's run ended."""
+
+    def on_tree_done(self, when, good, fail_n):
+        """RETURN: None. The run ended; 'None' follows on the
+        queue."""

+"""SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+PURPOSE: THE SUMMARY -- a pure fold over the report stream (O-4). The
+         stream is the ONE carrier of the run's truth; whoever wants
+         the whole at the end folds it, with this function or their
+         own.
+
+Any consumer may use it: our exit-status logic, a TUI, a customer
+application. It reads the vocabulary and nothing else; an unknown kind
+passes through untouched, as the format promises.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+"""
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
+class CRunSummary:
+    """What one run came to, folded from its stream.
+
+    'verdict_db' maps (directory, node) to the verdict word;
+    'cause_db' names, for the nodes that have one, the node whose
+    breaking failed them. 'good_f' and 'fail_n' are 'tree-done's own
+    word -- 'None' where the stream ended without one."""
+    directory_tuple: tuple = ()
+    verdict_db:      dict  = field(default_factory=dict)
+    cause_db:        dict  = field(default_factory=dict)
+    detail_db:       dict  = field(default_factory=dict)   # O-19
+    frame_db:        dict  = field(default_factory=dict)
+    fault_tuple:     tuple = ()
+    report_tuple:    tuple = ()
+    dir_good_db:     dict  = field(default_factory=dict)
+    good_f:          bool | None = None
+    fail_n:          int  | None = None
+
+    def failure_db(self):
+        """
+        RETURN: dict, (directory, node) -> verdict, every run whose
+                verdict is not 'ok'.
+        """
+        return {key: verdict for key, verdict in self.verdict_db.items()
+                if verdict != "ok"}
+
+
+def fold(event_iterable):
+    """
+    RETURN: CRunSummary, the given events folded in order. Events of
+            an unknown kind are ignored, and so is a known kind whose
+            required fields are missing -- the vocabulary's promise,
+            honoured at the consumer; anything that is not a dict ends
+            the fold ('None' does).
+    """
+    directory_list = []
+    verdict_db     = {}
+    cause_db       = {}
+    detail_db      = {}
+    frame_db       = {}
+    fault_list     = []
+    report_list    = []
+    dir_good_db    = {}
+    good_f         = None
+    fail_n         = None
+
+    def fits(*name_tuple):
+        """RETURN: bool, True where 'item' carries every named field
+        -- the promise extended: a malformed known kind is ignored
+        like an unknown one, never a crash at the consumer."""
+        return all(name in item for name in name_tuple)
+
+    for item in event_iterable:
+        if not isinstance(item, dict): break
+        kind = item.get("kind")
+        if   kind == "tree-begun":
+            if not fits("directory_list"): continue
+            directory_list = list(item["directory_list"])
+        elif kind == "run-ended":
+            if not fits("directory", "node", "verdict"): continue
+            key             = (item["directory"], item["node"])
+            verdict_db[key] = item["verdict"]
+            if "cause" in item: cause_db[key] = item["cause"]
+            if "detail" in item: detail_db[key] = item["detail"]
+        elif kind == "frame":
+            if not fits("directory", "role", "good"): continue
+            frame_db[(item["directory"], item["role"])] = item["good"]
+        elif kind == "fault":
+            if not fits("directory", "text"): continue
+            fault_list.append((item["directory"], item["text"]))
+        elif kind == "report":
+            if not fits("directory", "text"): continue
+            report_list.append((item["directory"], item["text"]))
+        elif kind == "dir-done":
+            if not fits("directory", "good"): continue
+            dir_good_db[item["directory"]] = item["good"]
+        elif kind == "tree-done":
+            if not fits("good", "fail_n"): continue
+            good_f = item["good"]
+            fail_n = item["fail_n"]
+
+    return CRunSummary(directory_tuple = tuple(directory_list),
+                       verdict_db      = verdict_db,
+                       cause_db        = cause_db,
+                       detail_db       = detail_db,
+                       frame_db        = frame_db,
+                       fault_tuple     = tuple(fault_list),
+                       report_tuple    = tuple(report_list),
+                       dir_good_db     = dir_good_db,
+                       good_f          = good_f,
+                       fail_n          = fail_n)
+
+
+async def drain(queue):
+    """
+    RETURN: CRunSummary, the queue read to its closing 'None' and
+            folded.
+    """
+    event_list = []
+    while True:
+        item = await queue.get()
+        event_list.append(item)
+        if item is None: break
+    return fold(event_list)

+"""SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+PURPOSE: THE EVENT VOCABULARY -- the shape of what the report queue
+         carries (O-2, O-3). One flat JSON-able dict per event; the
+         table below IS the format, and 'format_text()' prints it for
+         the outside world.
+
+THE STABILITY PROMISE: fields are only ever ADDED; a kind is never
+removed and its stated fields never change meaning. A consumer must
+ignore an unknown kind and unknown fields, and must treat an unknown
+'verdict' as not-ok. 'FORMAT' rises only where that promise cannot
+hold.
+
+Kinds are plain ASCII strings, at most 9 bytes, unique -- a consumer
+MAY zero-pad one into an integer and switch on it; the wire stays
+legible.
+______________________________________________________________________________
+"""
+
+FORMAT = 1
+
+#  Everything that leads to the executability of a test IS the test
+#  (O-3): 'run-ended' therefore names WHY in 'verdict', and 'cause'
+#  names the node whose breaking failed this one. The verdict words
+#  are OPEN under the add-only promise.
+VERDICT_TUPLE = ("ok", "test-failed", "build-failed", "launch-failed",
+                 "unsupported", "misdep")
+
+#  kind -> (required {field: type}, optional {field: type}).
+#  'when' is on EVERY event and stated once below the table.
+KIND_DB = {
+    "tree-begun": ({"directory_list": list}, {}),
+    "dir-begun":  ({"directory": str, "node_n": int}, {}),
+    "frame":      ({"directory": str, "role": str, "good": bool}, {}),
+    "run-begun":  ({"directory": str, "node": str,
+                    "node_kind": str}, {}),
+    "run-ended":  ({"directory": str, "node": str, "node_kind": str,
+                    "good": bool, "verdict": str}, {"cause": str,
+                                                    "report": str,
+                                                    "detail": str}),
+    "fault":      ({"directory": str, "text": str}, {}),
+    "report":     ({"directory": str, "text": str}, {}),
+    "dir-done":   ({"directory": str, "good": bool,
+                    "fail_db": dict}, {}),
+    "tree-done":  ({"good": bool, "fail_n": int}, {}),
+}
+
+_FIELD_TEXT_DB = {
+    "when":           "ISO-8601 UTC instant of the event",
+    "directory":      "the test directory, RELATIVE to the root, "
+                      "'/'-separated",
+    "directory_list": "every test directory of the tree, walk order",
+    "node_n":         "how many nodes the directory's plan holds",
+    "role":           "'on_entry' or 'on_exit'",
+    "good":           "true where the thing stood",
+    "node":           "the plan node's name, e.g. 'test-a.py one', "
+                      "'build[make test-a.py]'",
+    "node_kind":      "'TEST', 'BUILD' or 'SESSION'",
+    "verdict":        "WHY it ended so: " + ", ".join(VERDICT_TUPLE)
+                      + ", ... (open; unknown reads not-ok)",
+    "cause":          "the node whose breaking failed this one; "
+                      "absent else",
+    "detail":         "the report's numbers, where it has them: which "
+                      "cap, the cap, the peak (O-19); absent else",
+    "report":         "the operation's own word for WHY (open list, "
+                      "e.g. 'pype-failed', 'test-app-stalled'); "
+                      "absent where nothing finer than the verdict "
+                      "is known",
+    "text":           "one line, verbatim",
+    "fail_db":        "node name -> terminal state, the failures "
+                      "alone",
+    "fail_n":         "how many nodes failed, tree-wide",
+}
+
+
+def format_text():
+    """
+    RETURN: str, the format description -- the promise, then every
+            kind with its fields, required first, optional marked.
+    """
+    line_list = [
+        "REPORT STREAM, format %d" % FORMAT,
+        "",
+        "One JSON object per event. Every event carries 'format' "
+        "(int),",
+        "'kind' (str) and 'when' (%s)." % _FIELD_TEXT_DB["when"],
+        "After 'tree-done' one null closes the stream. A 'run-ended'",
+        "may arrive WITHOUT a 'run-begun': a node that never",
+        "dispatched -- [MISDEP], or failed by its supporter -- ends",
+        "without starting.",
+        "",
+        "THE PROMISE: fields are only ever added; a kind is never",
+        "removed. Ignore unknown kinds and fields; an unknown",
+        "'verdict' reads not-ok. Kinds are ASCII, <= 9 bytes, unique:",
+        "a consumer may zero-pad one into an integer.",
+        "",
+    ]
+    for kind in KIND_DB:
+        required_db, optional_db = KIND_DB[kind]
+        line_list.append(kind)
+        for name, field_type in required_db.items():
+            line_list.append("    %-16s %-6s %s"
+                             % (name, field_type.__name__,
+                                _FIELD_TEXT_DB[name]))
+        for name, field_type in optional_db.items():
+            line_list.append("    %-16s %-6s (optional) %s"
+                             % (name, field_type.__name__,
+                                _FIELD_TEXT_DB[name]))
+        line_list.append("")
+    return "\n".join(line_list).rstrip() + "\n"
+
+
+def event(kind, when, **field_db):
+    """
+    RETURN: dict, one event of the vocabulary: 'format', 'kind' and
+            'when' beside the given fields.
+
+    Raises AssertionError for a kind the table does not carry, a
+    required field missing or badly typed, or a field the kind does
+    not know -- the EMITTER is ours and a wrong event is a defect,
+    named here, not a riddle at a consumer.
+    """
+    assert kind in KIND_DB, "unknown event kind '%s'" % kind
+    required_db, optional_db = KIND_DB[kind]
+    for name, field_type in required_db.items():
+        assert name in field_db, \
+               "'%s' misses its field '%s'" % (kind, name)
+        assert isinstance(field_db[name], field_type), \
+               "'%s': field '%s' is %s, not %s" \
+               % (kind, name, type(field_db[name]).__name__,
+                  field_type.__name__)
+    for name in field_db:
+        assert name in required_db or name in optional_db, \
+               "'%s' does not know a field '%s'" % (kind, name)
+    return dict(format=FORMAT, kind=kind, when=when, **field_db)

+#  SPDX-License: MIT; Project VUT; (C) Frank-Rene Schaefer
+#  --------------------------------------------------------------------------
+#
+#  THE ROOT OF THIS TREE, and the boundary of the climb.
+#
+#  Every face ASCENDS from where it is called, collecting each
+#  'hwut.conf' it passes, until it reaches this file. What is collected
+#  is then applied OUTERMOST FIRST -- this file first of all -- so the
+#  innermost word wins and a test directory's own 'hwut.conf' has the
+#  last word before the source headers.
+#
+#  It plays TWO ROLES: it is the MOST DOMINANT configuration there is,
+#  and it STOPS the climb, so nothing above this project can reach into
+#  it. An empty block is a complete statement -- it says only 'the tree
+#  ends here', which is what this one says.
+#
+#  LOCAL KEYS ARE REFUSED HERE -- 'on_entry', 'on_exit', 'collision',
+#  'dependency' and the directory's own targets name local matters and
+#  belong in a test directory's own 'hwut.conf'.
+#
+#  'language-setup' STANDS HERE AND NOWHERE ELSE (exploration R-73): one
+#  block per language, holding everything HWUT does WITH that language.
+#  The block's NAME is the language; a source file's 'language' word
+#  selects it by that name, and the name is free -- 'dep4711_c' is a
+#  language. Where a header states no language, 'extensions' selects.
+#
+#      extensions       the file extensions that select this entry
+#      interpreter      the call for an interpreted test; the entry's
+#                       own name where unstated
+#      coverage         the candidate coverage tools, PREFERENCE ORDER;
+#                       the first one this machine has serves, and an
+#                       EMPTY LIST IS AN ANSWER: nobody vouches for a tool
+#      coverage_target  the coverage-capable build target of a compiled
+#                       test; '%' is the source file's stem (R-74)
+#
+#  THE ORDER OF A 'coverage' LIST IS PART OF THE TABLE: a tool whose
+#  format this build reads stands first, since election takes the first
+#  candidate the machine HAS. A candidate with no reader is still worth
+#  listing -- it is how a machine refuses BY NAME. 'hwut.cov formats'

+#  WHAT IS LEFT OUT IS LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE. No 'interpreter' where a
+#  language is compiled, or where no launcher takes a source file as
+#  its first argument. Every extension is owned by ONE entry: '.m' is
+#  objective-c's (a MATLAB or Octave file states 'language'), '.pl' is
+#  perl's (Prolog has '.pro'), '.sh' is bash's ('shell' names 'sh' and
+#  claims nothing). '.h' is not claimed: a header is not a test. A
+#  language's name is a bare word, shell-safe: 'csharp', 'fsharp',
+#  'vbdotnet'.
+#  --------------------------------------------------------------------------

+disc-10  THE WISH NAMES DIRECTORIES TOO                     ** SETTLED **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+RAISED (chat, 2026-08-29) out of the face inventory (disc-9), which
+found 'hwut.target' sharing NOTHING with any other face. The reason is
+not that target is peculiar. It is that THE WISH CANNOT SAY WHAT
+TARGET NEEDS.
+
+==============================================================================
+1.  THE GAP
+==============================================================================
+THE WISH SELECTS RUNS. A directory enters only as a FILTER on a run's
+path -- '--exclude-dir vendor', or a path-bearing glob
+'messaging/*/TEST/test-a.sh'. There is no way to say THESE
+DIRECTORIES.
+
+THE ASYMMETRY IS ALREADY VISIBLE AND ALREADY WRONG:
+
+    --exclude-dir <glob>    exists
+    --dir <glob>            does not
+
+A vocabulary that can SUBTRACT a thing and cannot NAME it is a
+vocabulary with a hole in it, and the hole was there before anybody
+wanted the feature.
+
+'hwut.target' EXPOSES IT because its subject genuinely IS directories.
+It iterates every directory whose 'hwut.conf' binds the named target
+and executes it there -- one directory implementing 'clean' as 'make
+clean', another as 'rm *.o *.so', and what unifies them is not the
+script but THE USER'S NOTION OF CLEANING. Target therefore parses its
+own arguments and shares no selection with anybody, which is exactly
+the shape a missing brick leaves behind.
+
+==============================================================================
+2.  THE TWO SETS, AND THE TRANSLATION BETWEEN THEM
+==============================================================================
+    A CHOSEN SET OF RUNS          what the wish selects today
+    A CHOSEN SET OF DIRECTORIES   what target needs, and what nothing
+                                  provides
+
+THESE ARE TWO VIEWS OF ONE SELECTION, not two selections, and the
+translation runs BOTH WAYS:
+
+    IN A RUN-RELATED MODE, a chosen directory means EVERY RUN IN IT --
+    or, where runs are also named, it RESTRICTS to those within it.
+        'hwut.run --dir "messaging/*"'          every run below there
+        'hwut.run --dir "messaging/*" --fail'   the failing ones there
+
+    IN A DIRECTORY-RELATED MODE, the directories ARE the subject and
+    the runs are not consulted at all.
+        'hwut.target clean --dir "messaging/*"' clean, in each
+
+    AND A RUN NAMES ITS DIRECTORY. A wish stating only runs still
+    answers the directory question: the directories are those the
+    selected runs stand in. So a directory-related face may take a
+    wish of any shape and get a sensible answer.
+
+THAT LAST RULE IS WHAT MAKES THIS ONE VOCABULARY rather than two. A
+face asks for the view it needs; the wish need not know which face
+asked.
+
+==============================================================================
+3.  WHAT IT COSTS -- ALMOST NOTHING, AND THAT IS THE ARGUMENT
+==============================================================================
+THE MATCHER ALREADY EXISTS. 'task_list_query._directory_hit_f' does
+precisely the matching '--dir' needs, and has since '--exclude-dir'
+was built: a glob carrying '/' is matched against the whole relative
+path, a BARE NAME against every path COMPONENT, so 'TEST' names
+'a/TEST' and 'a/b/TEST' alike.
+
+THE SELECTION ALREADY KEYS BY DIRECTORY. 'selection.of_tree' answers a
+'result_db' keyed by directory and a 'case_list' whose entries each
+carry theirs. The directory view is nearly there already.
+
+SO THE WORK IS: one field on 'Wish', one option at the door, one
+condition in the query, and one new door on the selection.
+
+==============================================================================
+4.  HOW IT HARMONISES WITH WHAT STANDS
+==============================================================================
+THE EMPTY-WISH LAW IS UNTOUCHED (E-20). A bare command line takes all
+available; an empty wishlist FILE is an empty wish, nothing to do.
+'--dir' is a statement like any other, so a wish carrying only '--dir'
+STATES SOMETHING and 'states_nothing_f' must say so.
+
+AN EXCLUSION STILL OUTRANKS EVERY INCLUDE. '--dir a --exclude-dir a/b'
+takes 'a' and not 'a/b'. The existing law needs no amendment; '--dir'
+joins the includes, which exclusions already outrank.
+
+THE UNION LAW OF '--label' IS THE MODEL. Several '--dir' globs are a
+UNION among themselves -- naming two directories asks for both -- and
+NARROW against the rest of the wish, exactly as '--label' does
+(disc-8). One rule, learnt once.
+
+THE SHORT FORM IS UNAFFECTED. Bare words are TARGETS (E-21), and a
+target names a file and optionally a choice. A directory is named by
+'--dir', never positionally: 'hwut.run messaging' must stay a target
+that matches nothing rather than silently becoming a directory.
+
+LITERAL TARGETS AND THE SILENCE (disc-8). A literal target overrides
+the standard label's silence; A '--dir' GLOB DOES NOT, because a glob
+over directories is a pattern and names a set nobody has seen yet.
+Same line, drawn the same way.
+
+THE WISHLIST FILE holds targets, one per line. IT DOES NOT GAIN
+DIRECTORIES: a wishlist is a list of RUNS, and a directory line would
+make a file that reads differently depending on which face read it.
+Where a person wants a directory in a list, they write the glob.
+
+==============================================================================
+5.  WHAT IT MIGHT FOLD IN
+==============================================================================
+'hwut.sanitize' also works PER DIRECTORY -- session wreckage, stale
+locks, 'OUT/'. RULED (chat, 2026-08-29): IT TAKES A WISH AND DOES NOT
+PARSE ITS OWN, and 'selection.directory_tuple' is the door it takes it
+through.
+
+NOT BUILT HERE, and for a plain reason: 'services/sanitize.py' does
+not stand in this tree. E-18 records its design; the face and its
+suite live elsewhere and must be migrated before the wish can reach
+them. THE RULING STANDS AND WAITS.
+
+WHAT IT WILL LOOK LIKE:
+
+    hwut.sanitize --session --dir "messaging/*"
+    hwut.sanitize --orphans --fail
+
+-- the second being the case that shows why a WISH rather than a
+directory option: 'the orphans of directories holding a failing run'
+is a sentence only the wish can say.
+
+AND A FIX SCRIPT (chat, 2026-08-29): 'hwut.sanitize --script' should
+write a script the person READS AND THEN RUNS, rather than acting
+itself. That is better than '--apply' for the reason E-18 already
+gives -- sanitize never guesses at blessed work -- because a script
+is REVIEWABLE BEFORE IT RUNS: every removal visible, lines deletable,
+the whole kept as a record of what was cleaned. '--apply' asks for
+trust; a script asks for a reading.
+
+    hwut.sanitize --session --dir "messaging/*" --script > clean.sh
+
+ALSO NOT BUILT, and for the same reason: the face is not in this
+tree.
+
+==============================================================================
+RULED, AND BUILT (2026-08-29)
+==============================================================================
+ a  RULED: IT RESTRICTS. Where a wish names both runs and
+    directories -- 'hwut.run --glob "test-a.sh" --dir "messaging/*"'
+    -- is the answer 'test-a.sh anywhere, PLUS everything under
+    messaging', or 'test-a.sh, but only under messaging'?
+    '--label' narrows against the rest of the wish and is a union
+    only among its own labels; '--dir' reads the same way, and 'the
+    failing ones under messaging' is the sentence people want. A
+    person wanting the union writes two commands, or a wishlist.
+
+ b  RULED: UNCHANGED. What does a directory-related face do with a
+    directory that binds nothing?
+    'hwut.target clean --dir "messaging/*"' where a matched directory
+    binds no 'clean'. Today target reports 'no directory binds any
+    target' only when NONE does.
+    A directory that does not bind the target is not an error, and
+    'hwut.target' already says so.
+
+WHAT WAS BUILT
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+    Wish.dir_tuple                  the field
+    '--dir <glob>', '--dir=<glob>'  the door, in the ONE wish parser
+    query._outside_dir_f            the narrowing, using the matcher
+                                    '--exclude-dir' already had
+    selection.directory_tuple       THE OTHER VIEW: the directories a
+                                    wish names, however it names them
+    hwut.target --dir               the first directory-related face
+                                    to read the wish's own word
+
+AND ONE LAW HAD TO BE STATED RATHER THAN CHANGED. 'hwut.target' passes
+EVERYTHING AFTER THE TARGET NAME to each directory's script,
+argv-style and untouched -- so '--dir' names directories where it
+stands FIRST, and is a word for the script where it stands second.
+That was this face's oldest law; '--dir' does not get to break it, and
+the help now says so where a person will read it.
+______________________________________________________________________________

+disc-2  THE TARGET SERVICE 'hwut.target'                          ** OPEN **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+RULED (chat, 2026-08-24):
+
+ 1  'hwut.conf' binds USER-DEFINED TARGETS in a SEPARATE dictionary --
+    a 'target { }' scope of the directory's own keys:
+
+        hwut {
+            target {
+                clean = "./clean.sh"
+            }
+        }
+
+    'on_entry'/'on_exit' are STANDARD targets with fixed semantics and
+    their own top-level keys; the separate dictionary exists so the
+    open-ended namespace can never collide with them. The validator
+    refuses standard names inside 'target { }' by name.
+
+ 2  THE FACE:  hwut.target <option-list> <target> <passed-through>
+    Everything before the target name is the service's vocabulary;
+    everything after it goes to each directory's script, argv-style,
+    untouched. One target per invocation.
+
+ 3  TWO PHASES. Phase one explores EVERY directory below the root and
+    settles the plan; phase two executes. A failure in phase one costs
+    ZERO executions -- nothing has run when exploration refuses.
+
+ 4  ABSENCE IS A FAILURE BY DEFAULT: a walked test directory that does
+    not bind the target fails the run in phase one. Softening options:
+        -i, --ignore-absence     skip directories lacking the target
+        --default <script-name>  run that script where the target is
+                                 absent
+
+OPEN (each a fork, one at a time, before any build):
+
+ a  Inheritance: is 'target { }' LOCAL like the frames (R-69), or may
+    a parent bind 'clean' for a subtree? Locality is the standing law;
+    inheritance is genuinely useful for 'clean'; this is the hardest
+    fork of the cluster.
+ b  Walk membership: is a directory with a 'hwut.conf' carrying only
+    'target { }' and no test applications walked at all? Today the
+    explorer would not call it a test directory.
+ c  Machinery: through CDirectoryWork/strategy/budget/lock (a target
+    run then never collides with a test run on the same directory), or
+    deliberately simpler because it is not a test run?
+ d  Exit law and output shape: OK / FAULT on any script failure; wire
+    events like a run, or a flatter report?
+ e  Script working directory, environment, and what a script's exit
+    code means per directory.

+disc-3  '--confs [file-name]+' -- THE SETUP FROM FILES              ** OPEN **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+RULED (chat, 2026-08-26, with E-9): the command-line faces gain a way
+to take the compare SETUP from configuration files --
+
+    --confs [file-name]+
+
+-- so that a richer setup (constraints, region parameters, marker
+changes) is reachable without a test run around it. The flag lands in
+'_core.py' with the other shared setup flags, so 'hwut.compare' and
+'hwut.merge' gain it together ('homogeneous by design', _core.py).
+Later files override earlier ones; the explicit flags ('--numeric',
+'--pattern', '--nothing') override every file.
+
+This closes the capability that 'tool/hwut_compare.py' carried as
+'--config cfg.py' and took to its grave (E-9).
+
+OPEN (the fork, one at a time, before any build):
+
+ a  THE FILE'S LANGUAGE. Candidates:
+      1  the 'hwut.conf' specification language, restricted to the
+         compare scope -- ONE language in the whole tool, read by the
+         one reader exploration already owns;  <- recommended
+      2  a bespoke key=value form -- a second language, a second
+         reader, a second place to be wrong.
+    The retired tool's form -- an exec'd Python file -- is not a
+    candidate.
+
+ b  Whether a bare test directory ('hwut.conf' present, no --confs
+    given) is read implicitly, or only what the flag names is ever
+    read. Refuse-rather-than-guess says: only what is named.

+disc-4  'hwut.play' -- RUN ONE TEST, SHOW THE READING            ** SETTLED **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+RULED (chat, 2026-08-26), the four forks RULED AND BUILT
+(2026-08-28). A new face, named 'hwut.play' --
+
+    hwut.play TEST-APP [CHOICE]
+
+-- explores the directory, resolves the test's OWN compare
+configuration, performs the optional build, runs the choice, and
+displays the READING of the produced output under that configuration:
+the stream fed against itself, marks by tolerance kind, exactly the
+face 'hwut.compare FILE' shows -- but under the test's setup, not the
+command line's.
+
+PLAY JUDGES NOTHING AND RECORDS NOTHING; it renders. 'hwut.run' is the
+face that judges and records; the README holds the distinction in one
+line. This is the closing of the seam '_core.py' names: "a service run
+inside a test run receives that Configuration object directly" -- play
+is the command line's way to stand inside.
+
+Per the naming law: 'services/play.py', launcher 'bin/hwut.play',
+suite 'TEST/test-play.*'.
+
+RULED, and built:
+
+ a  CHOICE ABSENT -- REFUSED where the application offers SEVERAL, the
+    choices listed by name; PLAYED UNASKED where it offers exactly
+    one; and a choiceless application plays its one run.
+    Refuse-rather-than-guess, and here the guess would be expensive:
+    playing 'the first' RUNS THE AUTHOR'S PROGRAM under a choice
+    nobody asked for, and renders an answer to a question nobody put.
+    (Note for the builder: a choiceless application keys its single
+    entry 'None' -- exploration's law, absence is None, never an empty
+    stand-in -- and 'None' is not a name a person may type, so it is
+    not among the choices offered back.)
+
+ b  WHICH STREAM -- THREE VIEWS, each a named region:
+
+        (default)  THE SUBJECT: what is going to enter the
+                   comparator, under the READING.
+        --raw      what came out of the APPLICATION, before any pype.
+                   Shown plainly: compare never reads this text, so
+                   marking it would state a thing that is not so.
+        --pyped    what the PYPE made of it. Where none stands, the
+                   view says so rather than printing the stream twice.
+
+    THE DEFAULT IS THE SUBJECT because that is the stream the question
+    is about. An author asking 'how does the framework read my output'
+    is asking about what the framework reads, which for any test with
+    a pype is NOT what the application printed.
+
+    THE REGION BANNER IS ONE SHAPE, '===== <name> =====', padded to
+    one width: a reader must never have to work out which picture
+    they are looking at.
+
+    THE PYPE VIEW EARNS ITS KEEP: a pype is part of the test
+    application, an artifact that may contain errors, and therefore
+    part of the ORACLE (display/DISCUSSIONS/todo-2). An author
+    debugging one needs to see what it did to the stream.
+
+    STDERR is shown only on '--stderr', and shown MARKED. E-5 says
+    stderr is never subject to testing, and it stands: play does not
+    test it. But SEEING IS NOT JUDGING, and a face whose whole purpose
+    is to show an author what their program produced may show what
+    their program produced. The mark is what keeps the two apart.
+
+ c  THE FAILING BUILD -- the report is named, every missing target is
+    named, the build tool's OWN STREAMS are shown, and play STOPS with
+    FAULT. It does not go on to run a subject that was never built.
+    In a run a failed build is a failing TEST (the differentiator);
+    here there is no verdict to reach, so it is simply the reason
+    there is nothing to play.
+
+ d  THE DIRECTORY MUTEX -- TAKEN, for the duration of build and
+    execution. Play records nothing, but it RUNS something, and what
+    it runs may write: a concurrent run meeting half-written artifacts
+    would be the same fault arriving by another door. The lock is
+    released before the rendering, which touches nothing.
+
+PLAY IS WIRING, NOT MACHINERY -- ruled, and it is the reason the
+face can be trusted. It owns no ceremony of its own:
+
+    the wish + CTestTaskListQuery   which run is meant -- so the 1.0
+                                    short form and globbing come free,
+                                    and a choice that does not stand
+                                    is refused in the words the whole
+                                    framework uses
+    provision_of(...)               SUBJECT PROVISION: build, launch,
+                                    contain, collect, CANONICALISE --
+                                    the very provision a run consumes
+    compare's reading               INTERPRETATION: the lexical
+                                    analysis, marks by tolerance kind
+    TuiDisplay                      DISPLAY
+
+WHAT PLAY SHOWS IS WHAT A RUN COMPARES, BY CONSTRUCTION rather than
+by re-implementation -- which is the only way the answer can be
+trusted to be the framework's answer and not this face's.
+
+    THE FIRST BUILD GOT THIS WRONG, and instructively: it reached
+    past 'provision_of' for 'StageExecute' alone, and so displayed
+    the RAW stream. For any test with a pype -- every
+    nondeterministic test there is -- that is the wrong stream in the
+    one place it matters, and nothing in the picture said so.
+
+BUILT: 'services/play.py', 'bin/hwut.play',
+'services/TEST/test-play.sh' -- seven choices, recorded.
+
+WHAT THE SUITE SHOWS, and why the face exists: two applications with
+identical output and different declared tolerance, side by side --
+
+    setup | numeric=+/-0.01 | ...     1  1 | value {3.14159} done
+    setup | numeric=exact   | ...     1  1 | value 3.14159 done
+
+-- the same bytes, read two ways, because the READING IS THE TEST'S,
+not the command line's.
+
+AND THE 'reading' CHOICE PROVES PLAY RECORDS NOTHING: it lists the
+directory afterwards, and the directory holds exactly what it held
+before -- no session directory, no result database, no book.

+disc-5  'hwut.wishlist' -- THE LIST, PRINTED AND SPENT       ** OPEN **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+RULED (chat, 2026-08-26): a face that PRINTS what a wish selects, and a
+'--wishlist' option that READS such a file back --
+
+    hwut.wishlist [<wish>]        prints, one per line:
+
+        ./<path>/test-app [choice]
+
+    hwut.run --wishlist FILE      spends it
+
+THE ROUND TRIP CLOSES: the printed form and the accepted form are the
+same form, so an author asks once, prunes and comments the file, and
+maintains it as text. 'hwut.run --wishlist messaging.txt' then names a
+suite by intent rather than by pattern.
+
+RULED with it:
+
+  - './' in a wishlist line is '$(dirname <the wishlist file>)'. A list
+    is relative to ITSELF, so it travels with the directory it
+    describes.
+  - GLOBBING IS ALLOWED throughout a line, path member included.
+  - Lines starting with '#' are comments; blank lines are ignored.
+  - '--wishlist' belongs in 'plan/wish.py', not in one face: every
+    face that takes a wish gains it at once, one parser, one place to
+    be wrong. (The same homogeneity that put '--confs' in '_core.py',
+    disc-3.)
+
+OPEN -- ONE RULING, AND IT BLOCKS THE CONSUMING HALF:
+
+    Does 'CTestTaskListQuery' LEARN ITS DIRECTORY (relative to the run
+    root), so that a glob may carry a path member?          <- needed
+
+    Today it cannot. The query is built per directory and matches
+    'case.source_file' against the glob; a 'CTestCase' carries
+    'source_file', 'choice', 'parameters', 'origin', 'position' -- no
+    path. So a path-qualified target has nothing to match against.
+
+    RECOMMENDED: yes. It is the smallest change that lets ONE matching
+    law serve both '--glob' and '--wishlist', and the path member is
+    what makes a cross-directory list worth maintaining. '--glob' then
+    gains paths too, which is a plain gain.
+
+    COST: the query's constructor changes, and every construction site
+    with it (the dispatcher, the explorer, the faces that build one).
+
+NOT AFFECTED: 'collision' and 'dependency' keep the bare R-34 target
+and keep REFUSING a path. They are different animals -- dependencies
+are RESOLVED within a directory, and collisions only prevent parallel
+running of sensitive neighbours. Neither has any use for a path, and
+admitting one would invite a cross-directory dependency, which the
+plan does not mean. THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE and belongs in the
+exploration RATIONALE beside R-34 when this is built:
+
+    a path is legal where a target SELECTS ACROSS A TREE,
+    illegal where a target NAMES A NEIGHBOUR.
+
+THE PRINTING HALF needs none of this and could stand alone; delivering
+it without the consuming half would be half a round trip, which is why
+it waits.

+disc-6  hwut 2.0 OVER THE WHOLE TREE: THE ROOT CAUSES     ** OPEN **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+MEASURED (2026-08-27): 'hwut.run' called IN each of the 25 TEST
+directories. No crash, no hang, no unretrieved task anywhere. ~600
+cases; 581 failures, and they are THREE CAUSES, not 581.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+r-1   567 x 'GOOD missing'  -- THE SUBJECT SUFFIX               ** OPEN **
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+The tree holds     GOOD/test-group_table.py--groups.txt
+The framework asks GOOD/test-group_table.py--groups.stdout
+
+HALF OF THE 1.0 NAMING IS IN PLACE and half is not. The KEY is the
+source file WHOLE ('key_name', E-14's ruling: 'test-x.lua' and
+'test-x.py' must not share a record). The SUFFIX is still the
+SUBJECT's -- '.stdout', '.stderr' -- where 1.0 names one file, '.txt'.
+
+That single suffix is the whole of r-1. It was left deliberately: the
+1.0 GOODs are the ones that RUN today, and renaming them would break
+the framework the code base is actually tested with. E-14 holds the
+open question -- the framework learns '.txt', or the files are moved
+to '.out'/'.err' when 2.0 is functional. RULED: not now.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+r-2   8 x  -- 'hwut-info.dat' IS NOT READ                     ** CLOSED **
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+    7  test-test_id_db.py [every choice]  'killed by the supervisor'
+    1  benchmark-hwut_hocon.py            3 faults, read as a header
+
+'engine/bookkeeper/TEST/hwut-info.dat' says
+
+    python *.py
+    --not config.py
+
+and that is CORRECT AND SUFFICIENT for hwut 1.0: the file needs no
+she-bang, because the directory states its interpreter. VUT 2.0 does
+not read that file, so it launches the application BY ITS OWN NAME,
+finds no she-bang, and reports a containment that never happened.
+
+'test_writing_support/python/TEST/hwut-info.dat' likewise says
+'--not benchmark*.py'; unread, the benchmark's SAMPLE HOCON is taken
+for a header and faults three times.
+
+THIS IS THE RENOVATOR GAP (todo-1), and it now accounts for more of
+the residue than everything except the suffix. A tree that states its
+own interpreter perfectly, to a framework that cannot hear it.
+
+CLOSED (2026-08-30, R-73): the root cause was NO DERIVATION in the
+exploration, not the unread file. 'language-setup' in 'hwut-root.conf'
+now binds '.py' to python and names the interpreter, so the seven
+choices run as 1.0 ran them, she-bang or none. What 'hwut-info.dat'
+still says that the framework does not hear is the '--not' line; that
+becomes 'ignore' in the directory's 'hwut.conf', and renovate (todo-1)
+translates it. The benchmark is that case.
+

+                                  stderr_tail_cap
+    2  test-csp_backtracking_mrv.py  soduko, massive-pipe

+disc-7  CADENCE NEEDS A THEORY, OR IT IS A WITCH HUNT     ** OPEN **
+______________________________________________________________________________
+
+OBSERVED (2026-08-27): 'hwut.stability --repeat=5' over 64 keys.
+
+    TALLY: 1 unstable, 14 warned, 49 steady
+
+The ONE was real: 'test-stability.sh verbose' flipped ok / test-failed
+/ ok / ok / ok, and was rightly stained.
+
+THE FOURTEEN WERE ALL THE SAME SENTENCE. Every one of them --
+'test-accept.sh', 'test-remove.sh', 'test-report.sh',
+'test-wishlist.sh' -- is a suite that SPAWNS PROCESSES. What the
+warning told the reader is 'this test runs subprocesses', fourteen
+times, in the vocabulary of instability.
+
+A WARNING THAT FIRES ON A PROPERTY OF THE TEST RATHER THAN ON ITS
+INSTABILITY IS NOT EVIDENCE. It is a hunt: a reader who acts on it
+changes tests that were never broken, and a reader who learns to
+ignore it stops reading the one line that mattered.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+WHAT IS WRONG WITH 'rt = stddev(delta) / average(delta)'
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+The measure is not wrong; it is UNCALIBRATED and MEASURES THE WRONG
+CLOCK. Four faults, each independently sufficient.
+
+f-1  IT IS WALL CLOCK.  'operations/run/core.py' marks with
+     'time.monotonic()'. A line that WAITS ON A SUBPROCESS is timing
+     the operating system's scheduler, not the test. Under load it
+     varies hugely and honestly. THE TEST DID NOTHING DIFFERENT.
+
+f-2  THERE IS NO NULL MODEL.  No one has measured what 'rt' looks
+     like for a KNOWN-STEADY line on THIS machine under THIS load. A
+     threshold without that is a number somebody liked. 'Unsteady'
+     means 'more variable than steady', and nothing in the run says
+     what steady is.
+
+f-3  THE SAMPLE IS FAR TOO SMALL.  At n = 5 the standard error of a
+     standard-deviation estimate is roughly 35% of the value. An 'rt'
+     computed from five repeats cannot separate a doubled variance
+     from noise. Any threshold at that n has a false-positive rate
+     nobody has computed -- and fourteen of sixty-four is 22%, which
+     is about what one would expect from thresholding noise.
+
+f-4  THE LOAD IS COMMON AND UNSUBTRACTED.  The repeats of ALL keys run
+     under the same machine at the same time. A slow repeat is slow
+     for EVERYONE. That common factor inflates every key's 'rt'
+     together, and is exactly the part that is not the test's.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+RULED (chat, 2026-08-27): OFF BY DEFAULT; THE CAUTIOUS TESTER ASKS
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+TIMING IS A MESS AND WILL STAY ONE, and the framework cannot measure
+its way out. It sets '--jobs', which is ITS OWN parallelism -- NOT the
+machine's load. A hundred niced processes and ten busy ones are not
+comparable, and nothing the framework records tells them apart. A
+'processes now / processes then' ratio multiplies a number we know by
+a number we do not.
+
+SO: STABILITY DOES NOT CHECK TIMING UNLESS ASKED.
+
+    default        the VERDICT detectors only. Two runs of one test
+                   that disagree on a verdict disagree, full stop --
+                   no statistics between the reading and the report.
+    '--cadence'    the timing findings, for a tester who knows the
+                   machine, chose the moment, and knows what the
+                   number is worth. THEY are the calibration; the
+                   framework has none.
+
+CADENCE IS NEVER A SHOW STOPPER: it does not stain, and it does not
+move the exit status, asked for or not.
+
+SHOULD IT BE ASKED FOR, it speaks only of the GROSS: a deviation above
+5 SECONDS -- far past any resolution question -- AND some 50x the
+usual delta for that line. Not 2x, not 5x. Nothing clearing both bars
+is noise, and nothing below them can be told from noise by any means
+the framework has.
+
+FOUND WHILE BUILDING IT: 'THE USUAL DELTA' MUST BE THE MEDIAN, NOT
+THE AVERAGE. 'spread / average' CANNOT EXCEED THE REPEAT COUNT -- one
+slow run among four is at most 4x, whatever its size, because the
+outlier drags up the very average it is measured against. A 50x bar
+against the average is therefore unreachable below fifty repeats, and
+would have been silent for ever. Against the MEDIAN the same outlier
+scores thousands, and one slow repeat does not move it -- which is
+exactly what 'usually' means.
+
+The same arithmetic says what shape the rule describes: a line that is
+USUALLY instant and ONCE was not. An ALTERNATING slowness puts half
+the samples either side of the median and collapses the factor to 2x
+-- correctly, because a line that is slow half the time is not an
+outlier, it is a bimodal test.
+
+WHAT REMAINS OPEN is whether the option is worth its code. Nobody has
+measured whether a cadence finding predicts a later verdict flip. Off
+by default, it can at least do no harm while that stays unknown.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+THE THEORY IT WOULD NEED
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+WHAT CADENCE IS FOR, stated first, because the measure follows from
+it: a line whose duration varies across repeats MAY be a race, a
+timeout-dependent path, or contention -- a thing that will LATER
+become a verdict flip. Cadence is a LEADING INDICATOR of instability,
+never instability itself. That is why it warns and does not stain,
+and that part of the design is right.
+
+A leading indicator earns its place only if a reading of 'unsteady'
+raises the probability of a future flip. Nothing has ever measured
+that. THE FIRST WORK IS NOT A THRESHOLD, IT IS THAT MEASUREMENT: keep
+cadence findings and verdict flips over many runs and ask whether the
+first predicts the second. If it does not, the detector should go, and
+the honest answer to this discussion may be its removal.
+
+Should it survive, three corrections, in order of how much they buy:
+
+t-1  MEASURE CPU, NOT WALL CLOCK.  A line that waits on a subprocess
+     costs no CPU; a line that spins, races or retries does. procsitter
+     already reports CPU time. This alone would silence most of the
+     fourteen for a reason, not by tuning.
+
+     COST: the timing sidecar records a second number, and 'D-x' would
+     have to say which one a cadence reads. Wall clock stays -- it is
+     what a person feels -- but it is REPORTED, not JUDGED.
+
+t-2  SUBTRACT THE COMMON MODE.  Per repeat, form a load proxy from all
+     keys that ran in it; a key is unsteady only where its variation
+     exceeds what the common factor explains. The framework already
+     has the data: it runs every key over the same repeats. This is
+     ordinary common-mode rejection and it is the difference between
+     'the machine was busy' and 'this test is unsteady'.
+
+t-3  CALIBRATE, AND SAY THE SAMPLE SIZE.  Run a known-steady control
+     line in the same repeats; the threshold is a multiple of the
+     control's own 'rt', not a constant. And refuse the finding below
+     a repeat count at which it can mean anything -- if that count is
+     20, then '--repeat=5' should say 'too few repeats to judge
+     cadence' and judge only the verdicts. ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE, NAMED.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+THE STEPS, SHOULD IT SURVIVE
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+RECOMMENDED, as the smallest honest step: the cadence finding is not
+printed by default. '--cadence' asks for it, and the help says what it
+is -- a leading indicator, uncalibrated. The verdict detectors
+(VERDICT, BYTES, LENGTH) keep the terminal, and they are the ones that
+have a theory: two runs of one test that disagree on a VERDICT
+disagree, full stop, with no statistics in between.
+
+This costs one flag and removes fourteen sentences that mean nothing,
+without deleting work that may yet be made sound.
+
+OPEN: whether to correct it (t-1..t-3) or to withdraw it pending the
+predictive measurement. The measurement is the honest first move and
+nobody has made it.
+______________________________________________________________________________
