+==============================================================================
+services -- RATIONALE
+==============================================================================
+
+Settled decisions, read-only. Append-only; no entry is removed once
+written.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-1  THE EXIT STATUS LAW
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Five faces, five sets of magic integers, no shared source of
+          truth. A caller comparing '$?' against a literal had no
+          guarantee two faces agreed on what '1' meant.
+
+DECISION  One 'IntEnum', 'E_ExitCode', in '_exit.py'; every face
+          imports and returns its members:
+
+              OK      = 0   nothing refused, nothing failed
+              FAULT   = 1   a fault or failure; still printed what stands
+              REFUSED = 2   the command line cannot be READ
+              EMPTY   = 3   reads, asks for NOTHING
+              SIGPIPE = 141 reader hung up; face went quiet
+
+          'IntEnum': 'sys.exit()' takes a member unchanged, so a
+          standing suite's 'status == 2' check keeps holding without
+          change while the faces migrate.
+
+          For the three faces (compare, merge, report) that can be run
+          by path ('python3 .../report.py') in addition to '-m', the
+          'from ._exit import E_ExitCode' line is placed AFTER the
+          '_config' adoption guard so the relative import resolves in
+          both invocation modes.
+
+COST      Every face needed surgical edits; GOODs that print status
+          numbers changed for plan (E-2 below) and for the new run face.
+
+GRAVEYARD Bare integer returns -- every 'return 0/1/2' replaced.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-2  PLAN EMPTY-SELECTION EXIT STATUS RETROACTIVE CHANGE
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   'hwut.plan' with a wish that selects nothing previously
+          returned 0 -- indistinguishable from a plan that found tests.
+          An empty selection is a design signal, not a success.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.plan' with an empty plan now returns 3 (EMPTY), not 0.
+          The HELP text's status blurb extended with the EMPTY line.
+          The wish GOOD ('test-plan.py--wish') re-blessed: one line
+          changed from '[status 0]' to '[status 3]'. Named separately
+          here so the delivery header can state it explicitly.
+
+COST      Callers that checked 'hwut.plan ... && ...' for an empty
+          plan must adjust; the new status is more informative.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-3  FOLD HARDENING (FORCED FIX, NOT A DESIGN CHOICE)
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   'orchestrator/run/summary.py' fold() crashed with KeyError
+          when a KNOWN kind's required field was absent -- the
+          vocabulary's stability promise requires that a malformed
+          known kind be IGNORED, not crashed on, exactly as an unknown
+          kind is.
+
+DECISION  fold() now guards every branch with a 'fits(*fields)' check;
+          a known kind missing a required field is silently skipped.
+          The docstring updated to state the extended promise. The four
+          receiver GOODs are byte-exact unchanged -- fold() only changed
+          its error behaviour, not its happy path.
+
+COST      Marginally more code in fold(). The fix was forced by the
+          'test-plain.py unknown' choice, which crafted a 'run-ended'
+          lacking 'verdict' -- a legitimate test of the stability
+          promise at the consumer.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-4  ACCEPTANCE, AND WHAT IT REFUSES
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   'Store.accept()' existed -- "the only way a nominal comes to
+          exist" -- but nothing called it: no face promoted a
+          candidate, so the first pole could only be placed by hand.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.accept'. The table:
+
+              candidate  nominal  --force   accept
+              ---------  -------  -------   ------------------------
+                 yes       no        -      BLESS, the first pole
+                 yes       yes       no     MERGE REQUIRED: named,
+                                            nothing written, FAULT
+                 yes       yes      yes     BLESS, overwriting
+
+          '--yes' and '--force' are SEPARATE flags: '--yes' asserts
+          'I have already looked'; '--force' asserts 'overwrite the
+          thing I judge against' -- the one operation here that
+          destroys evidence, never implied by the other.
+
+          SELECTION IS THE WISH, once: the positional short form
+          ('hwut.accept "test-*.py" one two') is SUGAR that desugars
+          into '--glob' targets; 'task_list_query' does the selecting
+          for both spellings. Keys follow RECORDING: the stem
+          ('operations/session.py', configuration.stem), per subject
+          -- a choice can be part-blessed.
+
+          The interactive question shows the CANDIDATE -- the
+          canonicalised record, which is what the framework compares;
+          '.raw' is named, not printed. Anything but 'y' leaves the
+          pole alone.
+
+COST      Unattended '--yes --force' in a script can rewrite every
+          pole of a directory; the two-flag split is the guard, and
+          the words are deliberate.
+
+GRAVEYARD One combined '--force' meaning both -- rejected; unattended
+          first-blessing would silently acquire pole-clobbering.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-5  STDERR IS NEVER SUBJECT TO TESTING
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A run records a stderr candidate; accept blessed it; the
+          verdict stayed 'unexpected-stderr' -- the NOTE governs, not
+          the file, so accept could produce a nominal that provably
+          does nothing. Worse: a stream that both carries diagnostics
+          and is held to a blessed text can do neither job.
+
+DECISION  stderr is for ERROR REPORTING; that is its whole job. Never
+          a nominal, never compared, never pype-d. Where error
+          reporting is itself under test, the application FLUSHES IT
+          TO A FILE and names that file in 'output' (exploration/
+          DISCUSSIONS/todo-1). 'E_StderrNote.NOMINAL' is retired;
+          its code removal is its own step (a blessed suite iterates
+          it).
+
+          Accept's one stderr decision is the NOTE, and only where it
+          SPOKE:
+
+              silent            FORBIDDEN, silently, the default
+              spoke, no flag    REFUSED by name, both remedies stated
+              spoke, --stderr-tol[erated]
+                                the note IGNORED is written; it
+                                GOVERNS -- the re-run is green
+
+          THERE IS NO DEFAULT where stderr speaks: a default leaves
+          the user clueless in front of output that deviates.
+
+COST      One more flag, and a refusal where HWUT 1.0 users may have
+          expected a question. The refusal names both ways out.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-6  ACCEPT REFUSES THE STREAM THAT NEVER COMPLETED
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A candidate can sit in the store without its closing token:
+          a run cut short, an abort, a crash mid-write, or an
+          application that does not speak R-70. Promotion would bless
+          an INCOMPLETE stream as the pole every later run is judged
+          against.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.accept' refuses to operate where a selected stdout
+          candidate's last line is not '<hwut-end>'. Atomic, before
+          any pole is touched; every offending key named. NO FLAG
+          bypasses it: '--force' overrides a standing pole, never
+          stream integrity. Consistent by construction with the abort
+          ruling (the aborting entity provides FAIL; content
+          irrelevant) and with R-70 (the token is the stream's own
+          testimony of completeness). File subjects are exempt: their
+          completeness is the READING POINT (after the token), not a
+          token of their own.
+
+COST      Every fixture and every hand-run application must speak the
+          law -- print the token as its last line -- including the
+          suites' own bash fixtures, which were corrected rather than
+          exempted: a fixture that does not speak the law is a
+          fixture that lies.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-7  hwut.target -- USER-DEFINED DIRECTORY TARGETS
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A test tree accumulates directory chores -- clean, regenerate,
+          repack -- that belong to the directories and not to any test.
+          Without a home they end up as ad-hoc scripts run by hand, or
+          worse, as pseudo-tests that pollute the suite.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.conf' binds user-defined targets in a SEPARATE
+          dictionary -- a 'target { }' scope of the directory's own
+          keys:
+
+              hwut {
+                  target {
+                      clean = "./clean.sh"
+                  }
+              }
+
+          'on_entry'/'on_exit' are standard targets with fixed
+          semantics and their own top-level keys; the separate
+          dictionary exists so the open-ended namespace can never
+          collide with them. The validator refuses standard names
+          inside 'target { }' by name. The scope is LOCAL, never
+          inherited (R-69's locality law); a parent cannot bind a
+          target for a subtree.
+
+          A directory binding any target is WALKED, test applications
+          or none: definition is membership.
+
+          THE FACE:  hwut.target <option-list> <target> <passed-through>
+          Everything before the target name is the service's
+          vocabulary; everything after it goes to each directory's
+          script, argv-style, untouched. One target per invocation.
+
+              -i, --ignore     skip a directory failing a runnability
+                               reason (any of the three below)
+              --default <s>    run script <s> where the target is
+                               absent
+              -q, --quiet      no per-directory output recording
+              +x               set a+x where the executable bit is
+                               missing; never done without it
+
+          TWO PHASES. Phase one explores every directory below the
+          root and settles the plan; a refusal costs ZERO executions.
+          Per walked directory, three reasons decide, in order:
+
+              1  file present
+              2  file executable
+              3  shebang's interpreter executable (where one decides)
+
+          A failed reason refuses the COMPLETE target execution,
+          except under '-i'. The reason-2 refusal hints at '+x'.
+
+          TARGETS ARE NOT TESTS. Exit codes are informational:
+          reported per directory, never deciding. 'hwut.target'
+          succeeds iff phase one accepted and every planned script
+          was found and executed -- however it exited. Outputs and
+          exit codes are recorded into a per-directory report; '-q'
+          disables the recording.
+
+          A script's cwd is the walked directory; the environment is
+          inherited unchanged -- no injected variables, the operating
+          system provides what a script needs. The passed-through
+          arguments are the one channel the service adds.
+
+          THE DIRECTORY MUTEX IS LAW: the service takes DirectoryLock
+          per directory -- a target run never collides with a test
+          run, or another target run, on the same directory.
+
+          'target { }' stands in the configuration vocabulary; its
+          entry in the rendered SPECIFICATION.txt lands with the
+          configuration tree (R-72, exploration todo-9).
+
+COST      One more service face and one more 'hwut.conf' key. A
+          directory carrying only 'target { }' is now walked, which
+          widens the explorer's membership law.
+
+GRAVEYARD Inheritance of 'target { }' for a subtree -- rejected;
+          locality is the standing law, and a parent binding 'clean'
+          silently for children hides who runs what where.
+          Exit code deciding OK/FAULT -- rejected; targets are not
+          tests, and a non-zero 'clean' may be that script's normal
+          voice.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-8  THE LAUNCHER ROOF 'bin/'
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Two launchers existed, each beside its component
+          ('engine/hwut_pype/hwut.pype', 'engine/compare/tool/
+          hwut.compare'); the nine faces had none and answered only
+          as 'python3 -m vut.services.<name>'. Test scripts already
+          she-banged '#! /usr/bin/env hwut.pype' and relied on a PATH
+          nothing in the tree provides.
+
+DECISION  ONE ROOF: 'vut/bin/' holds every launcher of the tool, and
+          only launchers -- two-line shell shims that resolve their
+          own location ('readlink -f') and exec the face or the
+          module file. The faces stay in 'services/', unmoved; the
+          naming law gains one clause: a face's launcher is
+          'bin/hwut.<name>'. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      One more top-level directory; a shim per face to keep in
+          step with the naming law; PYTHONPATH is set by the shim,
+          which shadows an already-exported one only by prepending.
+
+GRAVEYARD A single 'hwut' dispatcher with subcommands -- rejected by
+          ruling: one door hiding many faces.
+          The modules AS the launchers ('bin/hwut.show' the Python
+          file itself) -- rejected: a dot in a file name makes it
+          unimportable, and every face's suite drives 'main(argv,
+          write)' by import; the form would break all nine suites.
+          Launchers beside their components -- rejected by ruling:
+          one roof, 'hwut.pype' included.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-9  hwut_compare.py RETIRED -- THE READING VIEW SUPERSEDES
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Two efforts displayed the tolerance lexing, and one name
+          covered both: 'engine/compare/tool/hwut_compare.py' (a
+          preview that rebuilt a PatternFinder by hand, exec'd a
+          '--config' Python file, forced numeric tolerance to 0.1 so
+          colour had something to show, and classified regions
+          against its own hardcoded set) and 'hwut.compare FILE'
+          (the face's reading view: the stream fed against itself
+          through the real 'reading/', marks by tolerance kind,
+          region handlers from the real registry).
+
+DECISION  The tool is RETIRED; the face keeps the name. The readings
+          a user sees are the readings the framework judges by --
+          one lexer, one registry, one door. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      The '--config <file>' path to a richer setup is gone until
+          the face gains a configuration-file argument
+          (DISCUSSIONS/disc-3); until then the command line reaches
+          only '--numeric', '--pattern', '--nothing'. The tool's
+          suite and four GOOD files go with it;
+          'tool/migrate_region_syntax.py' stands alone and untested,
+          as it already was.
+
+GRAVEYARD Renaming the tool to 'hwut.lex' or 'hwut.preview' --
+          rejected: nothing left to rename.
+          Keeping the tool for its '--config' -- rejected: 'exec' of
+          a Python file is not a configuration door, and the tool's
+          defaults were admittedly not the framework's.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-10  '--timing' RAISES THE STORE; 'hwut.stability' READS IT
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   The cadence apparatus was complete and dead. 'StoreConfig.
+          record_timing', 'Store.write_timing', 'Store.timing',
+          'keep_timing' and stage_execute's per-line delta all stood
+          and were unit-tested, while 'test_configuration_of' built
+          no StoreConfig at all -- so 'configuration.store' was None
+          for every test of every tree run, 'keep_timing' False, and
+          no '.times' sidecar was ever written. A question about
+          several runs ('does this suite pass RELIABLY') had no data
+          and no face.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.run --timing' raises a StoreConfig in the ADAPTER,
+          where a test's configuration is built and where the store's
+          word belongs. It is the only thing that raises one: until
+          something asks for more than the candidate there is nothing
+          for a StoreConfig to say. Refused beside '--coverage' --
+          ONE MEASUREMENT AT A TIME (coverage D-3): a coverage run's
+          times are the instrumentation's and a cadence read from
+          them would be a lie.
+
+          'run.main' gains an 'event_sink': the report stream is the
+          run's truth (O-4) and whoever wants the whole folds it.
+          THAT is the seam a face above a face folds at.
+
+          'hwut.stability' runs the wish N times ('--repeat', 3) and
+          reports FOUR findings: VERDICT differs (the fault, and the
+          only one that moves the exit status); BYTES differ though
+          the verdict held (the tolerance absorbed it -- one
+          tightening from flaky); LENGTH differs (unalignable, so not
+          timed); CADENCE unsteady, 'stddev/average' PER LINE ACROSS
+          THE REPEATS. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      A knob on 'hwut.run' and a seam in its 'main'. A stability
+          run is N runs: it costs what it measures. The repeats share
+          one store, so only the LAST candidate survives them -- the
+          face reads each snapshot before the next repeat overwrites
+          it.
+
+GRAVEYARD 'rt' across the LINES OF ONE RUN -- rejected: that measures
+          the shape of the test, not its stability. A test that
+          builds and then prints has a huge spread across its own
+          lines, every time, on every machine, and would be reported
+          forever. Across repeats, a legitimately slow step is slow
+          in all of them and scores zero.
+          A private keyword on 'run.main' instead of '--timing' --
+          rejected: the README names two uses of the measurement and
+          both are the analyst's, so the knob earns a door.
+          'record_timing' stated in 'hwut.conf' -- rejected: it makes
+          the test author responsible for what the analyst wants at
+          the moment of asking.
+          Warnings moving the exit status -- rejected by ruling:
+          tolerance is there for a reason.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-11  THE STAIN: INSTABILITY IS FALSE TESTIMONY, NOT A FAILURE
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A test that comes out 'ok' in one repeat and not in another
+          has not made a weak claim. It has made a claim it has no
+          right to make, ABOUT THE RELIABILITY OF THE UNIT BENEATH IT.
+          Reporting it as a failure understates the offence: a failure
+          is information, a switching verdict is noise wearing the
+          clothes of information. Nothing recorded it, so a suite
+          could switch for years and every run would look like a
+          fresh, honest verdict.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.stability' writes a STAIN into the book at
+          'choices/<key>/stain' -- 'repeat_n', 'when', and the
+          verdicts that convicted it. It stands beside 'stderr', the
+          other per-choice standing decision, and is written by the
+          face that takes it.
+
+          A STAINED CHOICE IS NOT RUN. The dispatcher reads the stain
+          before the ceremony and returns the verdict False with the
+          report 'unstable': there is nothing to learn from asking a
+          liar again. The choice fails, ITS DIRECTORY FAILS, and the
+          run fails -- what the run then says about the component
+          under test is that the component cannot be relied upon to
+          have been tested.
+
+          'E_TestRunResult.UNSTABLE' stands FIRST in the precedence
+          table: a stain outranks anything a run could have found,
+          because there was no run. Its phrase is 'UNSTABLE -- not
+          run'.
+
+          'hwut.accept' refuses a stained choice, by name, with the
+          way out. Acceptance declares the POLE of the good cluster;
+          a test that will not hold still has no cluster, and
+          blessing one of its runs would write the false testimony
+          into the nominal itself.
+
+          THE ONLY TWO WAYS OUT: 'hwut.stability' repeating AT LEAST
+          as often as the conviction and finding every verdict alike;
+          or 'hwut.remove' / 'hwut.remove-choice', which forgets the
+          book entry and the stain with it -- the urgent path, which
+          says 'this test has no history' (true) and never 'this test
+          is fine' (unsayable here). (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      'run.main' gains 'despite_stain_f' -- THE PROVER'S SEAM: the
+          face that disqualified a choice must be able to run it, or
+          a stain could never be answered. No command line reaches it.
+          A new failure token costs a phrase and a rank, both of which
+          the operations hygiene suite demanded before it would pass.
+
+GRAVEYARD Running a stained test and reporting UNSTABLE afterwards --
+          rejected by ruling: it spends the machine on testimony
+          already known worthless, and a green run beneath the stain
+          would tempt the reader.
+          Fewer repeats than convicted clearing the stain -- rejected:
+          a proof that repeats less often has not answered the charge.
+          'hwut.accept' clearing a stain -- rejected: acceptance is
+          the act the stain exists to forbid.
+          Time clearing a stain -- rejected: nothing about waiting
+          makes a witness truthful.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-12  REMOVAL FORGETS WHAT THE FRAMEWORK RECORDED, AND NOTHING ELSE
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   'hwut.remove' was owed (orchestrator todo-2) and became
+          urgent with E-11: the stain's escape hatch pointed at a door
+          that did not exist. And a test whose subject genuinely
+          changed has no nominal worth keeping -- an old pole is not
+          the centre of a new cluster, it is a fact about a program
+          that no longer exists.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.remove <test>' and 'hwut.remove-choice <test> <choice>'
+          forget, IN THIS ORDER, each step announced: the NOMINALS,
+          the CANDIDATES and every sidecar beside them (freshness,
+          raw, cadence, coverage), the BOOK ENTRY (the stderr note and
+          the stain with it), and the REGISTER ID -- retired, never
+          reissued, so no later test inherits an old test's coverage
+          history.
+
+          NEVER TOUCHED: the test application, its 'hwut.conf', and
+          'OUT/'. Removal forgets what the FRAMEWORK recorded; the
+          author's own files are the author's.
+
+          IT ASKS FIRST, showing the whole list, unless '--yes'. A
+          nominal is a blessed artefact and its loss is a real loss.
+
+          A TEST THE BOOK NEVER KNEW is not an error: there was
+          nothing to forget. Refusing would make removal depend on the
+          very history it exists to discard. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      Two faces over one module; the choice form differs in what a
+          word means and in nothing else. The paths are shown relative
+          to the test directory -- 'GOOD/x.stdout' and
+          '.hwut-store/x.stdout' are different files and a basename
+          alone would print them alike.
+
+GRAVEYARD Removing the test application too -- rejected: the framework
+          records; the author writes.
+          Removing without asking -- rejected: an unrecoverable act
+          with no confirmation is a trap, and '--yes' serves the
+          script that has already decided.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-13  A WISHLIST IS A FILE OF TARGETS, AND THE ROUND TRIP CLOSES
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A suite worth quick-checking -- 'the messaging tests' -- is
+          a thing a person MEANS, not a thing a glob expresses. It is
+          maintained by adding and removing entries and by writing
+          down why one was dropped. A command line holds none of that:
+          it cannot be commented, cannot be reviewed, cannot be
+          committed beside the tree it describes.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.wishlist [<wish>]' PRINTS what a wish selects, one
+          line per case, in walk order:
+
+              ./<path>/<test-app> [<choice>]
+
+          '--wishlist <file>' READS that form back: '#' comments and
+          blank lines dropped, the lines joining the '--glob' targets
+          and OR'ed with them. It lives in 'plan/wish.py', so every
+          face that takes a wish gains it at once -- one parser, one
+          place to be wrong (the homogeneity of disc-3).
+
+          THE ROUND TRIP CLOSES: what is printed is what is read, so
+          an author asks once, prunes, comments, and keeps the file.
+
+          THE LEADING './' IS THE LIST'S OWN GROUND -- resolved
+          ABSOLUTELY against the directory of the wishlist FILE, not
+          against the reader's cwd and not against the run's root. A
+          list beside the subtree it describes therefore travels with
+          it and reads the same from anywhere.
+
+          THE GLOB'S FILE MEMBER MAY CARRY A PATH, relative to the
+          run's root, with globbing throughout. 'CTestTaskListQuery'
+          learns its 'directory' (relative) and the 'root' (absolute)
+          to answer one. A path-bearing glob against a query that
+          knows neither matches NOTHING -- refused by silence rather
+          than answered by ignoring the path, which would select the
+          right file in the wrong place. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      The query's constructor gained two parameters and every
+          construction site with it ('plan/tree.py', 'services/plan.py',
+          'services/accept.py'). A single-directory face passes '.'
+          and its own absolute path: one directory is its own root.
+
+GRAVEYARD A second matcher for wishlist lines alone -- rejected: two
+          matchers, and a question about what a wishlist line means
+          when pasted after '--glob'.
+          './' resolved against the RUN'S ROOT -- rejected: the list
+          would then only work from one place, which is the opposite
+          of travelling.
+          A path admitted to 'collision' and 'dependency' -- rejected:
+          those are different animals. Dependencies are RESOLVED
+          within a directory and collisions only prevent PARALLEL
+          RUNNING of sensitive neighbours; neither has use for a path,
+          and admitting one would invite a cross-directory dependency,
+          which the plan does not mean.
+
+              a path is legal where a target SELECTS ACROSS A TREE,
+              illegal where a target NAMES A NEIGHBOUR.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-14  'hwut.tell' TELLS ABOUT ONE TEST; 'hwut.report' REPORTS ON A RUN
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   One word, two subjects. 'hwut.report' packed ONE TEST whole
+          -- metadata, source, GOOD, OUT, cadence -- for another pair
+          of eyes, human or model. But 'a report' in a testing tool is
+          also what CI reads: JUnit XML, TAP, the traditional HWUT
+          page. That is a WHOLE RUN, folded from the stream or queried
+          out of the result databases, and it is a different face
+          entirely. Left as one word, '--format' would have had to
+          mean two things.
+
+DECISION  THE PACKER IS RENAMED 'hwut.tell'. It tells you about one
+          test: 'hwut.tell TEST-APP [CHOICE]'. Nothing else about it
+          changes.
+
+          'hwut.report' is FREED for the reporting face -- queries
+          over the result databases, rendered by '--format':
+
+              traditional   the HWUT page: per-directory blocks with
+                            dot leaders, the summary with its
+                            prefix-elided directory column
+              junit         the XML every CI ingests
+              tap           still widely read
+              json          for whoever builds their own
+
+          THE WIDTH IS THE TERMINAL'S, never a constant: the
+          traditional page fills what it is given, as 'display/
+          console' already decides once for the run's own rendering.
+
+          '[OK]' and '[FAIL]' are RIGHT-ALIGNED to one column, so the
+          dot leader is two shorter for a failure and the verdicts
+          stand in a line. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      A rename of a face, its launcher, its suite and five GOOD
+          files. 'hwut.report' now names something that does not exist
+          yet -- a debt stated, not a promise kept.
+
+GRAVEYARD '--format' on 'hwut.run' -- rejected: the run RENDERS LIVE
+          and its stream is its truth; a report is asked for AFTER,
+          and may be asked of a run that happened yesterday, which
+          only the databases remember.
+          '--format' on the packer -- rejected: it packs one test and
+          a CI format wants the run.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-15  THE EXCLUSIONS, AND 'hwut' AS THE DEFAULT FACE
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A wish could only ADD. 'everything except the vendored tree'
+          and 'everything except the slow choice' had to be written as
+          an enumeration of what remains, which goes stale the moment
+          a test is added.
+
+DECISION  '--exclude <target>' takes the same form as '--glob', path
+          member and all. '--exclude-dir <glob>' names a DIRECTORY AND
+          EVERY DIRECTORY BELOW IT: a glob carrying '/' matches the
+          path or an ancestor of it, a BARE NAME matches any path
+          COMPONENT, so '--exclude-dir OUT' drops 'a/OUT/TEST' and
+          'a/OUT/b/TEST' alike.
+
+          AN EXCLUSION OUTRANKS EVERY INCLUDE. Asked first, answered
+          first: a case an exclusion names is not wanted, whatever
+          selected it -- a wishlist line, a glob, or the bare wish.
+
+          'bin/hwut' IS 'hwut.run'. A bare 'hwut' states no wish, a
+          wish that states nothing wants everything, so 'hwut' runs
+          the whole tree below the current directory. (Ruled
+          2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      Two more keywords in the one wish parser, and the query
+          answers a directory question it did not before.
+
+GRAVEYARD Negated globs ('--glob !x') -- rejected: one keyword doing
+          two jobs, and a shell that eats the '!'.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-16  'hwut.rename' FOLLOWS THE NAME; NO RECORD CONTENT IS TOUCHED
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   Renaming a test threw its history away: the nominals stood
+          under the old key and the next run reported a missing GOOD.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.rename <old> <new>' and 'hwut.rename-choice <test>
+          <old> <new>' MOVE the artefacts and re-key the book: not one
+          byte inside a nominal, a candidate, a cadence or a coverage
+          record changes. A VUT-COVERAGE record refers to its RUN ID,
+          and THE REGISTER KEEPS THAT ID across a rename -- which is
+          what the register is for.
+
+          A RENAME IS NOT A FRESH START. The book entry moves with
+          everything in it: the recorded runs, the stderr note, and
+          ANY STAIN. A test that switched results does not launder
+          itself by being called something else.
+
+          THE SOURCE FILE IS NOT MOVED. Renaming the author's own file
+          is the author's act ('git mv'); this face FOLLOWS it.
+
+          A COLLISION IS REFUSED BEFORE ANYTHING MOVES: half a rename
+          onto a live name is worse than none. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      Two faces over one module, as with removal.
+
+GRAVEYARD Moving the source file too -- rejected: the framework
+          records; the author writes.
+          A rename that drops the stain -- rejected: that is
+          laundering, and 'hwut.remove' is the honest verb for it.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-17  'hwut.report' -- FOUR FORMATS, AND THE STAIN IN EACH
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   'hwut.run' renders LIVE, for the person watching. CI reads
+          machine formats, and a human reading a finished run wants
+          the HWUT page. Neither is a live rendering, and both may be
+          asked of a run that happened yesterday.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.report [<wish>] [--format=<name>]' READS THE BOOKS.
+          It explores the tree for its SHAPE and asks each directory's
+          'result_db.json' for the VERDICT, so a report may be taken
+          long after the run. A case the books never saw is 'never
+          run' -- a finding, not a fault, and never a stand-in for a
+          failure.
+
+          FOUR FORMATS: 'traditional' (the default), 'junit', 'tap',
+          'json'.
+
+          THE WIDTH IS THE TERMINAL'S: '--width', else COLUMNS, else
+          the terminal's own, else 80, and never below 40. Nothing
+          assumes a constant.
+
+          '[OK]' AND '[FAIL]' ARE RIGHT-ALIGNED TO ONE COLUMN, so the
+          dot leader runs two shorter for a failure and the verdicts
+          stand in a line. The summary's directory column is
+          PREFIX-ELIDED against the line above, the shared leading
+          path replaced by dots of its own length, the sharing ending
+          at a separator. THE FAILURES ARE LISTED ONCE MORE at the
+          end, after the summary.
+
+          THE STAIN IS A FAILURE IN EVERY FORMAT. JUnit knows failure,
+          error and skipped; a stained choice is none of them -- it
+          was not run, and it did not fail. 'skipped' is the closest
+          and is a lie of exactly the kind E-11 forbids, so a stain is
+          emitted as a FAILURE whose message names it: CI goes red,
+          which is true, and the message says why. (Ruled 2026-08-26.)
+
+COST      A face that both explores and reads books; the shape is the
+          tree's and the verdict is the book's, and neither alone
+          would do.
+
+GRAVEYARD '--format' on 'hwut.run' -- rejected with E-14: the run's
+          stream is a live thing and a report is asked for after.
+          A stain as JUnit 'skipped' -- rejected: it would tell CI the
+          run was fine.
+          Failures shown only in place -- rejected by ruling: a list
+          at the end is what a reader scrolls to.
+
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+E-18  'hwut.sanitize' -- REPORTS BY DEFAULT; NEVER GUESSES AT BLESSED WORK
+----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+PROBLEM   A tree accumulates: sessions that did not finish, locks whose
+          holder is gone, 'OUT/' from last week, records naming cases
+          nobody offers. Nothing found any of it, and nothing could
+          call the project's own 'clean'.
+
+DECISION  'hwut.sanitize [<wish>] [--apply] [--target <name>]...'.
+          IT REPORTS AND DOES NOT ACT; '--apply' is the whole
+          difference, because the answers here are IRREVERSIBLE.
+
+          FIVE ASPECTS, none stated meaning all -- EXCEPT the targets,
+          which are never implied: running somebody's script is an act
+          nobody asked for.
+
+            --session  wreckage; nothing reads it between runs
+            --lock     a lock WHOSE HOLDER IS GONE. A LIVE LOCK IS
+                       NEVER TOUCHED, not even under '--apply'. The
+                       liveness is asked through the mutex's OWN
+                       predicate, so this face and the runner cannot
+                       disagree about who is alive.
+
+                       AND A CLAIM THAT CANNOT NAME ITS CLAIMANT IS
+                       GONE (ruled 2026-08-27): a record with no start
+                       time, one of the wrong shape, or none at all
+                       cannot be compared against any process -- so
+                       honoured, NO FUTURE RUN AND NO CLEANING COULD
+                       EVER BREAK IT, and the directory is blocked for
+                       ever. An unreadable claim and an absent one are
+                       the same claim, and the code already answered
+                       the absent one that way.
+            --out      the application's scratch
+            --orphans  records naming a case nobody offers
+            --target   the PROJECT'S OWN verb, in every directory that
+                       binds it (E-7). A target NO DIRECTORY BINDS is
+                       REFUSED BY NAME: a misspelt 'clen' that quietly
+                       does nothing is worse than one that stops.
+
+          THE ORPHAN GUARD, which is the ruling that matters: A RECORD
+          IS NEVER AN ORPHAN WHERE EXPLORATION CANNOT SEE THE
+          APPLICATION AND THE FILE STILL STANDS. It is UNREACHABLE --
+          the mending is in the configuration, not in the blessed
+          work.
+
+          MEASURED ON THIS TREE, and this is why the guard exists:
+          without it '--apply' would have deleted NINE blessed
+          nominals -- 'regression-1.py', 'regression-2.py',
+          'regression-3.py', 'verify_signature.sh' -- applications
+          hwut 1.0 runs and VUT 2.0 cannot yet see because their
+          'hwut-info.dat' is unread (disc-6, r-2).
+
+          THE GUARD IS NARROW. Where exploration DOES offer the
+          application and has no such CHOICE, the record is a reliable
+          orphan: the configuration was read, understood, and does not
+          name it.
+
+          AND ORPHANS ARE NOT JUDGED AT ALL where exploration raised a
+          fault, or where the wish hides cases -- a tree that cannot be
+          read cannot say what it offers, and hidden cases would look
+          orphaned. (Ruled 2026-08-27.)
+
+COST      One face that must know every kind of record the framework
+          writes; a record name it cannot parse is passed over, which
+          is the safe way to be wrong.
+
+GRAVEYARD ACTING BY DEFAULT -- rejected: a GOOD file deleted by a tool
+          that guessed is gone.
+          THE FRAMEWORK CLEANING A PROJECT'S OWN LEAVINGS -- rejected:
+          it does not know what they are; the project says so through
+          a target.
+          A 'test-' PREFIX as the gate for 'is this a record' --
+          rejected: this tree holds 'regression-1.py' and
+          'verify_signature.sh', and the gate would pass over their
+          records in silence. The gate is a SOURCE EXTENSION in the
+          test part.
+
+E-19  LABELS -- SETS OF RUNS IN ONE FILE; THE NAMING LAW'S DOTTED CLAUSE
+
+PROBLEM   Suites hold tests about the SUITE ('meta' -- every GOOD ends
+          in the terminal) that have no business in the run a person
+          makes after changing the product; and authors need durable,
+          nameable SETS of runs ('concern', 'slow') that a wish can
+          ask for. Where does membership live, and through which
+          faces?
+
+DECISION  ONE FILE, 'hwut-root.labels', beside 'hwut-root.conf' at
+          the boundary the configuration climb ends at: literal
+          targets only, sorted, elided, rewritten whole; absent means
+          no label exists, which is not an error. FIVE FACES,
+          'hwut.labels.create/add/remove/list/query' -- the naming
+          law gains its dotted clause: a dotted launcher name is a
+          package. '--label <expr>' joins THE WISH, one parser for
+          every face; the GRAMMAR ('AND', 'OR', 'NOT', 'all'; ',' is
+          'OR') lives with the engine ('plan/label.py') because the
+          selection evaluates it; the file's reader and writer are
+          the faces' own ('services/lib/labels/_file.py'). ABSENT A LABEL
+          QUESTION, the standard label 'meta' is SILENT -- and the
+          silence is THE WISH'S, not one face's, or 'hwut.wishlist'
+          and 'hwut.run --wishlist' would select different sets and
+          the disc-5 round trip would not close. A face the label
+          view does not reach REFUSES '--label' rather than guessing.
+          'create' refuses a label that stands; 'add' refuses one
+          that does not: A TYPO MUST NOT SILENTLY MAKE OR GROW THE
+          WRONG SET. All three writers refuse a wish that states
+          nothing: enrolling or stripping EVERYTHING must be asked
+          for in words ('--label all', '--label <label>'). A glob
+          that met only silenced runs draws a WARNING naming it: the
+          silence must speak where it swallows an explicit match.
+          The whole design: services/DISCUSSIONS/disc-8-labels.txt.
+
+COST      Every selection that would honour labels must be HANDED the
+          view -- construction sites change one by one (the label
+          faces first; 'run', 'plan' and the rest follow). The file
+          is rewritten whole, so a hand comment does not survive a
+          write.
+
+GRAVEYARD SELF-LABELLING IN THE TEST HEADER -- rejected: no set from
+          a query, no labelling of tests one does not own, no single
+          file saying what sets exist.
+          GLOBS STORED IN THE FILE -- rejected: the file would hold
+          two truths, the pattern and the snapshot the next write
+          turns it into.
+          'hwut.labels-add' AND 'hwut.labels add' -- rejected: five
+          hyphen-launchers collide with '-' <=> '_'; a face with a
+          verb is a shape no face has.
+          '--group' -- rejected: the file is 'hwut-root.labels';
+          two words for one thing is what terminological invariance
+          forbids.
+
+E-20  THE LABELS GO LIVE -- THE VIEW IN EVERY WISH; NAMES FOLLOWED
+
+PROBLEM   E-19 delivered the file and its faces, but '--label'
+          reached no selecting face and the standard label silenced
+          nothing: a parsed option that does not act is a lie waiting
+          to be believed. And a rename or removal that the labels
+          file does not follow loses a member SILENTLY -- unlabelled
+          looks exactly like never labelled.
+
+DECISION  'view_at(directory)' ('services/lib/labels/__init__.py') is THE
+          ONE DOOR a face obtains the view through; 'hwut.plan',
+          'hwut.wishlist', 'hwut.report' and 'hwut.accept' build it
+          at their doors, and 'hwut.run' threads it through
+          'orchestrator' -> 'orchestrate' -> 'determine_tree', which
+          also serves 'hwut.cov' and 'hwut.stability' riding
+          'run.main'. 'RootConfMissing' is the face's REFUSED,
+          'LabelFileError' its FAULT, and it does not run. THE LAWS
+          OF EMPTINESS STAND: an empty command line takes all
+          available; an empty wishlist FILE is an empty wish, nothing
+          to do; and a view assigning the standard label nowhere
+          imposes NOTHING -- the selection walks the very path, byte
+          for byte, it walked before labels existed
+          ('CLabelView.silences_f' guards the fast path).
+          'services/_follow.py' is THE ONE PLACE a changed or
+          forgotten name reaches the boundary records, called LAST by
+          'hwut.rename', 'hwut.rename-choice', 'hwut.remove' and
+          'hwut.remove-choice': a crash above leaves an entry loud
+          and findable (E-18), never one silently pointing at
+          nothing; a stale-entry collision is a FAULT, not a merge.
+          'hwut.show' answers section 6: an '==[ LABELS ]' section,
+          the silent entries marked -- because the failure mode of
+          every label mechanism is a test that silently does not run.
+
+COST      Every future face that selects through a wish must hand the
+          view down or its '--label' refuses -- deliberate: refused,
+          never silently ignored. 'hwut.accept' under a bare wish no
+          longer touches what the standard label silences; blessing a
+          silenced GOOD asks for '--label' in words.
+
+GRAVEYARD THE ENGINE READING 'hwut-root.labels' ITSELF -- rejected:
+          data flows into the engine, the engine imports nothing
+          back; one reader, owned by the faces.
+          LIFTING THE SILENCE BY EXPLICIT TARGET -- still open
+          (disc-8, fork b); the warning speaks meanwhile.
+
+E-21  THE SHORT FORM OF HWUT 1.0; AN EXPLICIT TARGET OVERRIDES
+
+PROBLEM   Two things HWUT 1.0 had and 2.0 had lost or never gained.
+          FIRST, 'hwut test-app choice' -- the shortest thing a
+          person types all day -- lived in 'hwut.accept' alone, and
+          every other face refused a bare word by name. SECOND, a
+          face could NAME a run and then decline to act on it: the
+          standard label's silence hid what 'hwut.accept
+          test-meta.sh' explicitly asked for, which is the silent
+          failure labels exist to prevent, arriving from the other
+          side.
+
+DECISION  THE SHORT FORM MOVES TO THE WISH ('desugar_positional',
+          'with_targets' in 'plan/wish.py'): the first word names
+          files, every further word a choice, globbing in both, and
+          it is SUGAR FOR '--glob' -- one selection language, so the
+          short form can never mean what the long form cannot say.
+          'hwut.run', 'hwut.plan', 'hwut.wishlist', 'hwut.report' and
+          'hwut.accept' take it; 'hwut.stability' and 'hwut.cov'
+          inherit it by forwarding their words to 'hwut.run'. A face
+          whose bare words already mean something else --
+          'hwut.rename', 'hwut.labels.create', 'hwut.show' -- does
+          not call it: the sugar is a thing a face ASKS FOR, never a
+          thing 'parse_wish' does behind its back.
+          AN EXPLICIT LITERAL TARGET OVERRIDES THE SILENCE
+          ('literal_target_f'): the silence is what a wish carries
+          when it asks nothing, and a named run is not nothing. A
+          GLOB DOES NOT -- the same line 'hwut-root.labels' draws by
+          holding literal targets only -- and where a glob's every
+          match is silenced it draws a WARNING naming the remedy, in
+          EVERY face ('swallowed_warning_tuple', accumulated over the
+          whole walk through 'CTestTaskListQuery.glob_reach' and
+          carried on 'CTreePlan.warning_tuple'). No face is special,
+          'hwut.accept' least of all: were it to read targets
+          differently, one wishlist file would select two sets and
+          the disc-5 round trip would break.
+
+COST      A bare word is no longer refused, so a mistyped word is a
+          target that selects nothing rather than a refusal by name.
+          An unknown OPTION is still refused, which is where typos
+          mostly land. The warning makes the quiet case speak.
+
+GRAVEYARD '--force-also-meta' -- rejected: '--label meta', '--label
+          all' and a literal target already say it.
+          ANY STATED TARGET OVERRIDING, globs included -- rejected:
+          '--glob "*"' would then run what a bare wish does not.
+          THE SUGAR INSIDE 'parse_wish' -- rejected: it would swallow
+          the words of every face that has its own.
+
+
+E-22  'hwut.play' -- THE COMMAND LINE'S WAY TO STAND INSIDE A TEST
+
+PROBLEM   'hwut.compare FILE' shows how compare READS a stream, but
+          under the command line's setup. An author asking 'why did
+          the framework not see these two numbers as equal' needs the
+          reading under THE TEST'S OWN setup -- and had no way to ask
+          that did not also produce a verdict and a record.
+
+DECISION  A face, 'hwut.play <test-app> [<choice>]', BUILT AS WIRING
+          over bricks that already exist and owning no ceremony of
+          its own: the wish and 'CTestTaskListQuery' say which run is
+          meant; 'provision_of' builds, launches, contains, collects
+          and CANONICALISES -- the very provision a run consumes;
+          compare's reading interprets; 'TuiDisplay' displays. What
+          play shows is what a run compares BY CONSTRUCTION.
+          THREE VIEWS, each a named region '===== <name> =====': the
+          SUBJECT by default (what enters the comparator, under the
+          reading), '--raw' what the application produced, '--pyped'
+          what the pype made of it.
+          PLAY JUDGES NOTHING AND RECORDS NOTHING; IT RENDERS.
+          No nominal is read, no Bookkeeper is made, no result is
+          written, nothing is stored. 'hwut.run' judges and records,
+          and the distinction is the whole point: ASKING MUST NOT
+          BECOME A RESULT.
+          This closes the seam '_core.py' names -- a service run
+          inside a test run receives that Configuration object
+          directly; play is the command line's way to stand inside.
+          The four forks of disc-4 are ruled there: refuse rather
+          than guess a choice; stderr shown only when asked and
+          always marked untested (E-5); a failed build named and
+          stopped upon; the directory mutex held while the author's
+          program runs.
+
+COST      Play runs the author's program, so it holds the directory
+          and cannot be used while a run holds it. The stream is not
+          kept: what a run would store, play shows and forgets.
+
+VERIFIED  Six choices recorded. The 'reading' choice lists the
+          directory afterwards and finds it unchanged, which is the
+          claim 'records nothing' made testable.
+
+GRAVEYARD PLAYING 'THE FIRST' CHOICE where several stand and none is
+          named -- rejected: it runs the author's program under a
+          choice nobody asked for.
+          A '--record' FLAG -- rejected: a face that may record is a
+          face whose output an author must think twice about. That
+          face exists, and is called 'hwut.run'.
+
+E-23  A PACK STATES ITS PLACE, AND TELLS BOTH READINGS
+
+PROBLEM   'hwut.tell' answered one field, 'hint:', for five different
+          situations -- two of them comparisons, three of them the
+          ABSENCE of one. A test that had never run and a test that
+          had failed read alike at a glance, and the pack said
+          nothing about WHERE the test stood. A pack is handed to a
+          bug hunter as a formal input, and it was not one.
+
+DECISION  THE HEAD NAMES THE PLACE AND BOTH READINGS:
+
+              directory:     services/TEST
+              test:          test-app.sh
+              choice:        one
+              verdict:       OUT differs from GOOD: stdout
+              status report: run and accepted -- both records stand
+
+          'verdict' is what a COMPARISON found, or that none could be
+          made. 'status report' is what the RECORDS say -- which
+          streams stand. TWO QUESTIONS, TWO FIELDS: one field
+          answering both is how a test that never ran comes to be
+          read as a test that failed. A MISSING PROVISION IS A
+          RESULT, stated as one -- the same law that makes a broken
+          specification a failing test rather than a fault beside the
+          directory.
+          THE DIRECTORY IS RELATIVE TO 'hwut-root.conf', the one
+          ground every reader of a pack shares; a directory in no
+          tree says so. Never an absolute path: a pack is
+          MACHINE-FREE, and stays comparable, storable and pasteable.
+
+COST      The head grew from three lines to six, and anything parsing
+          'hint:' by name must read two fields instead.
+
+VERIFIED  All four states exercised; the suite's GOODs re-recorded.
+
+DEFECT FOUND, and it was older than this change: the verdict paired
+          whichever 'out' key came first with whichever 'good' key
+          came first -- 'out stderr' against 'good stdout' -- and so
+          called two byte-identical streams different. A COMPARISON
+          IS BETWEEN ONE SUBJECT AND ITS OWN NOMINAL; the subjects
+          are paired by name now, and both fields say which subject
+          they speak of.
+
+GRAVEYARD KEEPING ONE 'hint:' FIELD -- rejected: the word 'hint'
+          understates a result, and one field carrying five
+          situations is how the pack misled its reader.
+
+E-24  OPENING THE LABELS IS ONE BRICK -- 'labels/_editing.py'
+
+PROBLEM   'create', 'add' and 'remove' had the IDENTICAL nine lines
+          apiece -- climb to the boundary or REFUSE, read the file or
+          FAULT, build the view, select what the wish states -- and
+          each wrote the file at the end. THREE VERBS ON ONE ENTRY SET
+          IS ONE ACTION, and it was written three times.
+
+          The face inventory (disc-9) found it by comparing WHAT EACH
+          FACE DOES rather than what it is called: the three rows were
+          identical.
+
+DECISION  'opened', 'stands_f', 'selected', 'written'. The brick
+          climbs, reads, views, selects and writes; the face keeps
+          what is ITS OWN -- which of the three verbs, and what to say
+          about the label standing or not.
+
+          EACH DOOR ANSWERS 'None' OR 'False' WHERE IT ALREADY SPOKE,
+          and carries the status on 'COpenLabels.status'. THE FACE
+          STILL OWNS ITS EXIT: what a face answers is part of its
+          contract with a script (E-1), and no shared module may
+          decide it. The brick says what went wrong and hands the code
+          back.
+
+COST      A face reading the entry set now says 'open_labels.entry_db'
+          rather than a local name. The indirection is real and small.
+
+VERIFIED  17 label choices unmoved, 352 declared choices unmoved. Six
+          imports fell out: the three faces no longer know what a
+          'SelectionError' or a missing boundary is -- the brick does.

+E-25  THE BOUNDARY FACE WRITES THE LANGUAGE TABLE               (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   Exploration R-73 and coverage D-26 moved every per-language
+          default out of the code. Something has to put it in front
+          of the author.
+DECISION  '_boundary.placed' writes 'hwut-root.conf' WITH the full
+          'language-setup' block: every language the coverage registry
+          vouched for, its candidate tools in preference order; its
+          'extensions', every one owned by a single entry ('.m' is
+          objective-c's, '.pl' perl's; MATLAB and Prolog files say so
+          in their header or use '.pro'); its 'interpreter' wherever a

+          ...); and 'coverage_target = "%.cov.exe"' for the gcc family,
+          whose instrumented build is one more target of the author's
+          own build rules. The text is the one template in
+          '_boundary.py'; a face that prints it prints exactly what it
+          would write. A language's NAME IS A BARE, SHELL-SAFE WORD:
+          'csharp', 'fsharp', 'vbdotnet' -- it travels on a command
+          line ('--language=csharp') and in a HOCON key unquoted.
+COST      A new root conf is ~200 lines instead of two. The two-line
+          form is still valid HOCON and still a boundary. A launcher
+          named here that is not installed refuses by name when a test
+          of that language runs; nothing is guessed.

+E-27  THE PROCSITTER NAMES WHAT A CALL MADE AND LEFT            (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   '/tmp' filled with 'vut_ids_*', 'vut_mutex_*' and their kin:
+          33 tests make scratch through 'tempfile', several never
+          remove it, several remove it only on the happy path, and a
+          killed choice removes nothing. Nobody could say which call
+          left what.
+DECISION  Two things, ruled together (chat, 2026-08-30).
+          THE PROCSITTER SUPERVISES THE CALL FOR CREATED FILES: a
+          before-and-after listing over the work dir and the call's
+          scratch ground, reported as 'ProcsitterResult.created_tuple'
+          -- what stands at exit and did not before. The work dir's
+          own 'TMP/' is the framework's and is never listed. It is an
+          OBSERVATION, not a cap: the procsitter deletes nothing.
+          EVERY CALL GETS A SCRATCH GROUND OF ITS OWN,
+          'TEST/TMP/scratch/<file>[--<choice>]', exported to it as
+          TMPDIR, so that what 'tempfile' leaves is attributable to
+          one call and lands where 'hwut.sanitize --transient' clears
+          it. The machine's '/tmp' sees nothing of a test.
+          The observation rides with the other telemetry into the
+          record; where it lands for good is pass D's (todo-2), and
+          'hwut.sanitize' reading it is later.
+COST      One listing before the spawn and one after, over the test
+          directory -- the walk the disk watchdog already makes on
+          every poll. A test that wants the machine's '/tmp' must ask
+          for it by name.
+GRAVEYARD A watch (inotify) in place of the listing: not portable, and
+          the interesting set -- what was LEFT -- is exactly what a
+          listing at exit sees.
+

+E-28  THE PYPE CALL IS OPERATIONS', AND EVERY CALL IS SUPERVISED    (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   A stated 'pype = "./tidy.pype"' was exec'd as stated, so the
+          script's she-bang line and execute bit decided whether a
+          test's stream could be canonicalised -- a bundle extracted
+          without its chmod script turned every pype-d test red with
+          'Permission denied'. And the language suite ran its own
+          launches through 'subprocess.run', which answers a missing
+          execute bit with a traceback out of the test.
+DECISION  Inside the framework THE CALL IS FORMED IN ONE PLACE,
+          'operations.run.stage_canonicalise.pype_call': a first word
+          ending in '.pype' runs as '[python, hwut_pype.py, <script>,
+          ...]' -- the interpreter, this Python -- whatever the file's
+          she-bang or mode. Any other first word is the author's own
+          command and runs as stated. Under the procsitter, as before.
+          A TEST THAT RUNS A COMMAND OF ITS OWN asks the supervisor
+          too: 'engine/procsitter/spawn.py' gives 'spawn(argv, ...)'
+          in 'subprocess.run''s shape, and a command that cannot be
+          launched comes back as 'FAIL_LAUNCH' with the reason on
+          'stderr', never as an exception. It stands beside the
+          procsitter, since the test-writing support is SEALED.
+COST      The she-bang of a '.pype' still matters to a SHELL -- a
+          person typing './tidy.pype' or a test through 'spawn' -- and
+          that is where it belongs. 'bin/hwut.pype' is that person's
+          door, and the extraction's chmod script is not optional.
+

+E-29  THE SHAPE OF A DIFFERENCE, AND WHO IS NOT TOLD BY IT     (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   'differs from GOOD' sends every reader to the same place. A
+          GOOD blessed under a framework that SWALLOWED output is
+          missing lines it should always have carried, and the reader
+          who must re-record it reads it the same way as one hunting a
+          regression.
+DECISION  A difference wears one of three SHAPES, and the shape is the
+          word:
+              GREW      every recorded line stands, in order; lines
+                        stand between or around them
+                        -> 'extra lines; GOOD intact'
+              SHRANK    every line that stands was recorded, in order;
+                        lines the GOOD holds are gone
+                        -> 'lines missing; rest intact'
+              DIVERGED  neither: a recorded line changed or moved
+                        -> 'differs from GOOD'
+          ALL THREE ARE [FAIL]. The badge does not move, and the shape
+          is the explanation beside it.
+          THE SHAPE SAYS WHERE TO LOOK, NEVER WHO IS WRONG. A stale
+          GOOD grows; so does A FILTER THAT STOPPED FILTERING -- and
+          that second one is the defect a golden master exists to
+          catch. They wear the same shape. Reading 'GREW' as 'safe to
+          bless' would bless noise into the oracle, which is the one
+          unrecoverable act in this tree.
+          'adm/good_audit.py' reads a whole tree's shapes at once from
+          what a run already left, in these same words. It stays in
+          'adm/' and is NOT an aspect of 'hwut.sanitize': sanitize's
+          subject is rubbish and its findings are decidable from the
+          tree alone, while a shape is evidence about the oracle; and
+          an aspect of sanitize would give '--apply' the meaning
+          'overwrite the nominals'. 'hwut.accept' is the one door a
+          nominal changes through.
+COST      One extra read of both texts per failing subject.
+GRAVEYARD 'STALE' as a verdict name -- rejected on the author's
+          objection: it names a culprit the test cannot identify.
+          A '--stale-goods' aspect of 'hwut.sanitize' -- see above.
+
+E-30  THE REPEAT MARK STANDS UNDER WHAT IT REPEATS            (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+DECISION  Where an application repeats, its ':' stands in the
+          APPLICATION'S COLUMN, under the first letter of the name --
+          ':/ :' and not ':/:'. A mark that says 'the same as above'
+          belongs above what it repeats.
+
+
+E-31  THE SHAPE IS THE REPORT'S TO SAY, NOT THE RUN'S          (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   E-29 took the shape AT THE COMPARE SITE, on fresh readers.
+          That contradicts the compare's own law: 'is_equivalent'
+          aborts as soon as 'False' can be stated and CONSUMES NO
+          FURTHER INPUT, so the caller may terminate the producer.
+          At verdict time neither text has been read whole -- and
+          GREW and SHRANK are claims ABOUT THE WHOLE TEXT. Re-reading
+          both entire, at that moment, pays exactly the cost early
+          abort exists to avoid, and on a stream cut short at the
+          abort it would classify a fiction.
+DECISION  THE RUN SAYS 'differs from GOOD', AND NO MORE. The shape is
+          taken by 'hwut.report' ('services/report.py.difference_shape'),
+          afterwards, from the stored candidate and the nominal --
+          whole files, no producer to starve, no economy to keep. It
+          is asked only of a difference the run already found, of
+          'stdout', and it DECLINES -- leaving the run's own word --
+          where a file is missing or cannot be read.
+          'adm/good_audit.py' is the tree-wide reading of the same
+          question and stands unchanged.
+COST      A shape needs a stored candidate; a report of a run whose
+          'TMP/' was cleared says 'differs from GOOD', which is true
+          and all that is left to say.
+OPEN      WAS THE CANDIDATE THE WHOLE OUTPUT? A comparison that
+          aborted early may have left a PREFIX, and a prefix read as
+          'shrank' would be the false claim this entry removes. The
+          note -- ran to the end / aborted at the first difference --
+          is machine-local, per (test, choice, operation), and
+          regenerable: the local observation database's shape exactly
+          (bookkeeper todo-2, pass D). BUILT THERE, NOT BEFORE: a
+          field added to the base now is one pass B must strip. Until
+          it stands, 'difference_shape' is honest about what it reads
+          and nothing warns that the candidate might be a prefix.
+
+
+E-32  ONE USAGE LINE PER FACE, GENERATED                        (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   'hwut.report --help' printed its usage TWICE and the two
+          disagreed: a hand-written block inside the module docstring,
+          which named neither the target globs, and the generated
+          'USAGE' appended at the end, which did. 'hwut.sanitize' and
+          'hwut.wishlist' carried the same pair. A usage line written
+          by hand drifts from the tokens the face actually reads --
+          which is the defect 'usage_line' exists to prevent.
+DECISION  THE DOCSTRING STATES NO USAGE. One 'USAGE = usage_line(...)'
+          per face, built from the token tuples, appended to 'HELP'.
+          And every prefix reads 'usage: hwut.<face>': five faces said
+          only 'hwut.<face>', so their line was the one line in the
+          help that did not say what it was.
+COST      Six GOODs re-recorded.
+OPEN      'hwut.accept', 'hwut.run' and 'hwut.plan' hold a hand-written
+          'HELP' string and do NOT append their 'USAGE' -- it is
+          printed only on a refusal. Their help therefore ends without
+          a usage line while the others end with one. One shape or the
+          other; not decided here.

+E-33  THE FLOW SAYS ONLY WHAT CHANGED                          (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   Two columns of the flow repeated things the reader already
+          knew. A run that never leaves ONE directory printed that
+          directory's nickname on the first line and ':/' -- 'the same
+          as above' -- on every line after, about a thing that was
+          never in question. And a block of twenty runs beginning at
+          once printed 'START' twenty times, the word carrying no more
+          information the nineteenth time than the fill dots do.
+DECISION  ONE DIRECTORY, NO DIRECTORY COLUMN. Where 'tree-begun' names
+          a single directory the column is not drawn at all; what
+          repeats is the application alone, and its ':' stands under
+          its name (E-30). The 'DIR' line still names the directory:
+          which place this is remains worth saying once.
+          A BADGE THAT REPEATS BECOMES AN ARROW. The first of a run of
+          'START's says 'START'; those under it say '---->', as wide
+          as a badge so no column moves. Only the flow badges elide --
+          'DIR', 'TREE' and 'FRAME' announce something and are never a
+          run.
+COST      Thirteen GOODs re-recorded, all of them the columns
+          themselves.
+

+E-36  THE CRITERION IS TIME AND PLACE, NOT REPRODUCIBILITY   (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   E-20 asked "can a run make it again, identically?" and then
+          kept 'verdict' and 'report', which a run makes again every
+          time. The criterion did not decide its own leading case, and
+          a rule that needs an exception on its first application is
+          the wrong rule.
+DECISION  THE QUESTION IS WHETHER A THING DEPENDS ON WHEN AND WHERE.
+
+          THE BOOK HOLDS WHAT THE SOFTWARE IS. A verdict and a report
+          are a statement about the software and the test applications
+          AS THEY WERE CONFIGURED at the time of the test, and about
+          nothing else. They must not depend on history, on the host,
+          on the weather in Los Angeles, or on what the Chancellor had
+          for breakfast. That is what makes them worth keeping: THEY
+          TELL A READER WHETHER THE SOFTWARE IS RELIABLE WITHOUT
+          RUNNING IT AGAIN.
+
+          THE LOCAL DATABASE HOLDS WHAT THIS MACHINE SAW. Execution
+          time, memory, pids, disk, the host, the instant: queryable,
+          and queryable with the understanding that they are LOCAL TO
+          THE TIME AND PLACE the test was executed. The same test on
+          another machine answers differently, and that is the correct
+          answer (E-22).
+
+          Where a thing is place-dependent it goes local, whether or
+          not a run reproduces it; where it is a claim about the
+          software it stays in the book, whether or not a run
+          reproduces it. 'verdict' and 'report' stay by the second
+          clause -- and now they stay BY THE RULE, not despite it.
+
+          TWO CONSEQUENCES, ruled with it (chat, 2026-08-30):
+
+          THE BOOK WRITES THE CAPS THAT HELD, by the name an author
+          states them under, through the adapter's '_CAPS_FIELD_DB' --
+          the one list of that vocabulary. The framework's defaults
+          ride with the stated ones, because THE DEFAULT IS WHAT HELD
+          and a reader asking what this test was configured to do must
+          be told it. Writing the procsitter's dataclass whole had put
+          'scratch_dir' and 'env' into every oracle: the EXECUTOR'S
+          fields, place-dependent, and growing whenever the procsitter
+          grows.
+
+          'first_accept' BECOMES 'last_accept'. The book dates the
+          nominal NOW STANDING -- a fact about the oracle in front of
+          the reader -- and a re-accept moves it. Every earlier
+          acceptance is HISTORY, and history is the configuration
+          management system's: git holds each one dated, attributed
+          and undoable, and a second, poorer copy in the book is a
+          copy that can disagree.
+COST      A book written before this entry carries 'first_accept'; it
+          is not read, and the next acceptance writes 'last_accept'
+          beside it.
+GRAVEYARD "Machine-authored is transient": bins 'GOOD/test_ids.dat'
+          wrong (B-2 -- ids are issued once and a re-run issues
+          different ones), which is why E-20 reached for
+          reproducibility in the first place. Time-and-place bins it
+          right: an id is a decision about a file, not an observation
+          of a machine.
+
+
+E-37  A COMPONENT MAY HAVE ONE DOOR                            (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   'engine/compare' is the largest component of the tree and the
+          one whose insides move most -- regions, solvers, edit
+          operations, readers. The rest of the tree reached it at four
+          different depths, one of them ('region/registry') for a
+          single exception class. Nothing said where the component
+          ended, so nothing could tell a rearrangement from a breach.
+DECISION  'engine/compare/api.py' is the ONE DOOR, and holds five
+          names: 'Configuration', 'is_equivalent', 'associate',
+          'RegionSyntaxError', 'feeder_ui'. Nothing of its own -- a
+          door with logic in it becomes a component, and then there
+          are two compares. 'RegionSyntaxError' moved to
+          'compare/contract/enums.py' on the way: a class the CALLER
+          CATCHES crosses the wall, and what crosses is vocabulary.
+          THE RULE IS EXECUTABLE. 'adm/LAYERING.txt' gains a third
+          line shape beside '->' and 'SEALED':
+              DOOR <module>   nothing outside the component may import
+                              anything beneath it but this
+          judged at MODULE depth like a seal, and the component's own
+          modules are unaffected -- a door is for callers, and a part
+          is not a caller. A seal says NOTHING LEAVES; a door says
+          NOTHING ENTERS BUT HERE.
+          THIS IS A TEMPLATE. Any component whose surface is small and
+          whose insides move may take a door the same way; the check
+          reads as many as are declared. Three followed at once
+          (E-38).
+COST      Seven modules touched, no behaviour change. The door was
+          proved by breaking it: one import restored to its old
+          spelling, and the check named the module, the target and the
+          door.
+FOUND ON THE WAY, and fixed: 'bookkeeper -> orchestrator', an
+          inversion E-36 had just introduced -- the book read the caps
+          vocabulary from the adapter, which stands above it. The
+          vocabulary now stands at 'bookkeeper/configuration.CAPS_FIELD_DB',
+          below both its readers. The layering check found it, which is
+          the argument for the whole mechanism in one line.
+
+
+E-38  FOUR DOORS, AND THE CONFIGURATION LAW                    (2026-08-30)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   'operations' and 'orchestrator' depend on the same
+          components, which reads like a case for ONE SHARED API.
+          Measured, it is not: of nineteen names crossing, six overlap
+          -- the procsitter's five and 'compare.Configuration'.
+          Operations RUNS things ('pack_record', 'harvest',
+          'is_equivalent'); orchestrator ARRANGES them ('Bookkeeper',
+          'elect', 'ObservationDb', 'event'). A common api would be
+          the UNION of two vocabularies, and each caller would see nine
+          names it must not use: a bag, not a door.
+DECISION  DOORS ON WHAT THEY BOTH CALL, not a door between them. Three
+          more, by E-37's rule: 'engine/procsitter/api' (sealed AND
+          doored -- nothing leaves, nothing enters but here),
+          'engine/coverage/api', 'engine/bookkeeper/api'. With
+          'compare', four.
+
+          A CONFIGURATION CONFIGURES A COMPONENT, SO IT STANDS ON THE
+          COMPONENT'S DOOR. There is no question about it: the type a
+          caller must build in order to call at all is the first thing
+          the door owes them. 'ProcsitterConfig', 'CoverageConfig',
+          'StoreConfig', 'NamingConfig', 'CAPS_FIELD_DB' and
+          'compare.Configuration' each stand on the door of the
+          component they configure, and each door's docstring names it
+          first.
+
+          SUBSTITUTE AT THE DOOR, stated in every door's docstring: a
+          re-export binds its names ONCE, at import, so 'api.X' and
+          'module.X' are two names for one object and rebinding one
+          does not touch the other. A test replacing a class must
+          replace it at the door, because the door is what the product
+          reads; patching behind it leaves the door holding the
+          original, the substitution appears to succeed, and the code
+          under test runs against the old class. Found by
+          'test-bookkeeper.py setup_delta', which invents a future
+          'compare.Configuration' and had been patching the module the
+          door imports from.
+COST      71 files rewritten, mechanically, no behaviour change. The
+          bookkeeper's door carries 25 names -- the widest of the four,
+          because the component owns TWO databases; if that is too
+          wide, the answer is to split the component, and the door now
+          makes the width visible.
+
+
+E-39  A RECORDING OLDER THAN ITS TEST IS NOT EVIDENCE          (2026-08-31)
+______________________________________________________________________________
+PROBLEM   An author edits a test, runs it BY HAND to look at the
+          output, and accepts. 'hwut.accept' reads the STORE, not the
+          terminal, and the store still holds what the PREVIOUS text
+          printed. Every refusal it can make -- the token (R-70),
+          stderr, the standing pole -- is then a verdict on the wrong
+          evidence, and the most confusing kind: right about what it
+          read, wrong about what is there. The observed case: a test
+          gained its '<hwut-end>' and accept went on reporting the
+          token missing, from a recording made before the edit.
+DECISION  THE UPDATE CHECK STANDS BEFORE EVERY OTHER CHECK. Where a
+          candidate's mtime is older than the test file that produced
+          it, acceptance REFUSES, names the test, and says to re-run.
+          Nothing is read from that candidate first: a check that
+          reads stale evidence in order to complain about it has
+          already misled.
+          THE LAW IS THE BOOK'S ('Bookkeeper.outdated_f'), beside
+          'candidate_path' -- the component that knows where a
+          recording lives is the one that can say whether it is out of
+          date. Compare B-5.
+          MTIME, NOT CONTENT: a test whose text changed and whose
+          output did not must still be re-run, because the store's
+          business is what THIS text produced and only running it can
+          say.
+          ONE FILE, NOT A CLOSURE: the application's own mtime, not
+          what it reads -- its configuration, its pype script, the
+          library under test. A check that tried to be complete would
+          be a build system; being NEARLY complete is worse than being
+          plainly one file, because a reader would trust it.
+NOT DONE  ACCEPT DOES NOT RE-RUN, it refuses and says to. Running the
+          selected cases means driving the orchestrator, and
+          'services -> services' is not a permitted edge
+          ('adm/LAYERING.txt'): accept cannot call 'run'. Duplicating
+          run's drive loop inside accept would be one law in two
+          places. The way in is to move 'drive these cases' down into
+          'engine' as a brick both faces stand on -- a fork, not a
+          detail, and not closed here. Nor is the BUILD half done: a
+          test that must be built before it runs is the same question
+          one step earlier.
+COST      One method on the Bookkeeper, one check in 'accept.main'
+          before 'stderr_decision', one paragraph in the README.
+          SUPERSEDED the same day by 'engine/operations/DISCUSSIONS/
+          disc-2-subject-provision.txt': the update check is part of
+          ONE subject-provision procedure in 'operations', not a
+          check this face performs on its own. The check in
+          'accept.main' stands only until provision carries it.
+          DONE 2026-08-31, later the same day: the check now lives in
+          'engine/operations/subject_provision.py: decide()', steps
+          (0)/(A)/(B) explicit, and this face calls it with
+          'production=False'. 'accept.main' carries no check of its own.
